note: AI-written plain-language summaries (Claude) for roll calls whose official source has none. Each was written from the official page in basisUrl and is shown labeled as AI-generated. Applied only when the bill title matches.

az:HB 2010.title: digital goods; seller's requirements; enforcement
az:HB 2010.summary: Requires digital goods sellers advertising "buy" or "purchase" to disclose it is a license with restrictions and revocation terms; if access is later permanently lost, requires a prorated refund of 20 percent per year for up to five years on goods costing $20 or more.

az:HB 2013.title: exceptional events; air quality; wildfires
az:HB 2013.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to submit an exceptional event demonstration to the U.S. EPA when a wildfire over 25,000 acres on federally managed land affects Arizona through smoke or land damage.

az:HB 2015.title: budget procedures; late filing penalty
az:HB 2015.summary: Sets penalties for organizations that fail to submit accurate financial statements to the Department of Administration for federal single audits, capped each fiscal year at $8 million or 1 percent of their General Fund appropriation, whichever is less.

az:HB 2028.title: DWR; application; administrative completeness
az:HB 2028.summary: Allows a court to order an indigent defendant experiencing homelessness to perform community restitution instead of paying the $20 assessment deposited in the Judicial Collection Enhancement Fund.

az:HB 2047.title: writ of restitution; criminal trespass
az:HB 2047.summary: Makes it first-degree rather than third-degree criminal trespass for a person served with a writ of restitution after an eviction to remain in or return to the property.

az:HB 2086.title: vaccination mandates; masks; prohibition
az:HB 2086.summary: Extends the ban on government mask requirements beyond government premises to all residents, and the ban on government vaccine requirements from COVID-19 to any disease or virus, overriding other vaccination laws; removes exemptions for health care districts and institutions.

az:HB 2105.title: agricultural property; inspections; notice
az:HB 2105.summary: Requires the Department of Revenue, for property inspections, and county assessors, for agricultural property, to give owners advance notice of the inspection date and a copy of the report; bars consecutive-year on-site assessor inspections of agricultural property unless listed changes occur.

az:HB 2113.title: public service corporation; rates; intervenor
az:HB 2113.summary: Requires the Residential Utility Consumer Office director to intervene in a utility rate case when the proposed increase to residential customers is 100 percent or more.

az:HB 2114.title: motorcycle registration requirements; safety fund
az:HB 2114.summary: Requires at least one registered owner to hold a motorcycle license to renew a motorcycle registration, with a 30-day temporary registration for those enrolled in an approved training program; trusts need a licensed trustee; business-owned motorcycles are exempt.

az:HB 2118.title: mobile food vendors; licensure
az:HB 2118.summary: Bars cities and towns from requiring mobile food vendors to obtain a local regulatory permit or license, and removes the allowance for local licenses requiring background checks or identification.

az:HB 2133.title: sexual material; consent; synthetic depiction
az:HB 2133.summary: Exempts clearly manipulated parody, comedy, artistic or critical works from the offense of disclosing nude or sexual images; requires commercial websites publishing sexual material to have uploaders verify depicted people's consent and adult age; violators face $10,000 per day.

az:HB 2134.title: critical infrastructure; foreign adversaries; prohibition
az:HB 2134.summary: Bars use of software and communications equipment from Chinese companies in Arizona critical infrastructure, overrides contracts allowing foreign access or control, and sets certification, reporting and publication requirements.

az:HB 2140.title: bullion depository; state monies; treasurer
az:HB 2140.summary: Allows the State Treasurer to invest up to 10 percent of state trust and treasury monies in physical gold or silver bullion held in a U.S. commercial depository meeting security, insurance and audit standards.

az:HB 2170.title: state contracts; foreign adversary; prohibition
az:HB 2170.summary: Bars companies domiciled in China and controlled by its government, military or ruling party from state contracts for electronic or information technology, requires bidders to certify they are not domiciled in China, and sets a $100,000 civil penalty for false certification.

az:HB 2174.title: insurance; modeling organizations; predictive models
az:HB 2174.summary: Renames advisory organizations as model and data organizations, applies the same rules to them, and removes the insurance director's authority to examine them.

az:HB 2244.title: evictions; satisfaction of judgments
az:HB 2244.summary: Sets that if a landlord does not respond within 15 days to a tenant's motion to compel satisfaction of an eviction judgment, the filing fee is waived, no hearing is held, and the judgment is deemed satisfied on proof of payment.

az:HB 2249.title: parents' bill of rights; remedies
az:HB 2249.summary: Bars school districts and employees from facilitating a minor's social transitioning, such as using a different name or pronouns, without both parents' written consent; adds parental access to the full educational record; sets minimum liability of $500,000 per instance for governmental entities, $20,000 for officials.

az:HB 2257.title: HOV lane; blood transport vehicles
az:HB 2257.summary: Changes the split of watercraft registration fees to 55 percent (was 65) for the Watercraft Licensing Fund, and sets fixed county percentages for the Law Enforcement and Boating Safety Fund in place of a Game and Fish Commission formula.

az:HB 2279.title: commercial river outfitters; limited liability
az:HB 2279.summary: Gives commercial river outfitters in Grand Canyon National Park immunity from claims arising out of a river trip's inherent risks, and from ordinary negligence claims waived in a liability release; does not cover gross negligence or willful acts.

az:HB 2305.title: private towing carriers; regulation; rates
az:HB 2305.summary: Makes private-property towing rates a statewide concern not open to further local regulation; cities, towns and counties without rates on January 1, 2026 default to the Department of Public Safety tow agreement rate, and existing local rates must be updated by July 1, 2027.

az:HB 2311.title: artificial intelligence service; disclosures; requirements
az:HB 2311.summary: Requires operators of conversational AI services to disclose users are interacting with AI, limits sexual and self-harm content, sets rules for minor account holders and age-verification data; the attorney general can seek $1,000 per violation, up to $500,000 per operator, from September 30, 2027.

az:HB 2321.title: DCS; credit freeze; consumer reporting
az:HB 2321.summary: Requires the Department of Child Safety to place a security freeze on a dependent child's credit record within 30 days of placement, keep it until age 16 when the child may keep or remove it, and notify parents or guardians.

az:HB 2379.title: school district governing boards; training
az:HB 2379.summary: Requires each school district governing board member to complete school finance training within 45 days after their term begins, and sets requirements for the training program.

az:HB 2380.title: school districts; board meetings; expenditures
az:HB 2380.summary: Requires school district boards to hold meetings at a public facility in the district and give public access to meeting materials and recordings, lets members pull items from consent agendas, and sets rules for approving out-of-state travel.

az:HB 2397.title: homeowners' associations; property covenants; disclosures
az:HB 2397.summary: Changes resale disclosure rules for condominiums and planned communities: associations must give buyers added documents, including recent board meeting minutes, a financial statement and insurance information, may deliver them electronically, and must update the report on an owner's request.

az:HB 2406.title: department of veterans' services; study
az:HB 2406.summary: Makes images, recordings and 911 calls involving deceased minors and child abuse victims confidential except to parents, investigators, courts and others listed; sets a $100,000 civil penalty per violation for profiting from death scene images and a class 1 misdemeanor for knowing unauthorized release.

az:HB 2408.title: nursing board; regulatory actions; expungement
az:HB 2408.summary: Changes Arizona Board of Nursing complaint handling: complainants generally must identify themselves, complaints are prioritized by patient harm, nurses get notice and file access, the board has 180 days to act, and the board may expunge some discipline once.

az:HB 2482.title: building renewal grants; procurement practices
az:HB 2482.summary: Caps individual job orders at $1 million for non-emergency construction projects funded by Building Renewal Grant monies, and requires the School Facilities Division to verify that projects are not split to avoid the cap.

az:HB 2502.title: ASRS; retirement; elected officials
az:HB 2502.summary: Lets an elected official who has reached normal retirement date retire from the state retirement system without resigning from office, and requires the employer to pay the alternate contribution rate.

az:HB 2592.title: artificial intelligence; state agencies; rules
az:HB 2592.summary: Requires state budget units to identify uses of artificial intelligence that reduce administrative burdens, eliminate regulations that unnecessarily restrict AI innovation and streamline AI procurement, and requires the Department of Administration to report annually by December 1.

az:HB 2611.title: group homes; safety; training; rights
az:HB 2611.summary: Adds foster children's rights to join enrichment activities and be free of bullying or discrimination, and bars retaliation for reporting violations; for group foster homes, requires drug-test reporting, removal of employees after positive results, and rules on background checks, training, security and unannounced inspections.

az:HB 2661.title: parents' rights; guardianship; notice; attestation
az:HB 2661.summary: Adds to the rights of parents or guardians under a Department of Child Safety abuse or neglect investigation the right to be told they may delegate temporary guardianship of the child.

az:HB 2662.title: parenting time; expert testimony; qualifications
az:HB 2662.summary: Allows a court in a parenting-time case involving alleged domestic violence or abuse to hear expert testimony only from witnesses with clinical experience working with victims, and limits the psychological methods experts may use to empirically established ones.

az:HB 2729.title: nursing board; continuation
az:HB 2729.summary: Continues the Arizona State Board of Nursing, the Board of Occupational Therapy Examiners, the Regulatory Board of Physician Assistants and the Department of Economic Security until July 1, 2030, and the Board of Pharmacy until July 1, 2032.

az:HB 2745.title: legislative subpoena; perjury; refusal; contempt
az:HB 2745.summary: Lets the Senate President, Speaker or a committee chairperson issue an order holding a witness in contempt for ignoring a legislative subpoena, after notice and an opportunity for a hearing, and allows a county sheriff to arrest the witness.

az:HB 2755.title: state land use; highest; best
az:HB 2755.summary: Lets holders of underperforming commercial state land leases, or leases expired under a year, apply to buy the land; requires the commissioner to appraise and sell it at public auction within 18 months of the application, and give lessees ample notice before ending such leases.

az:HB 2762.title: food products; labeling; cultivated cells
az:HB 2762.summary: Requires labels reading cell-cultivated or cell-cultured on food products derived from cultivated cells, placed by the manufacturer, packager or retailer.

az:HB 2763.title: shooting range; closure; conditions
az:HB 2763.summary: Adds a condition to closing a shooting range: the Legislature must adopt a joint resolution approving the Game and Fish Commission's closure.

az:HB 2771.title: community supervision; rehabilitation; costs
az:HB 2771.summary: Lets the Department of Corrections require, as a condition of community supervision, that a prisoner pay reasonable costs of participating in a rehabilitation program.

az:HB 2782.title: corporation commission; utilities; amortization; tariffs
az:HB 2782.summary: Requires the Corporation Commission and utilities to make disclosures when a regulatory asset is included in rate base or reflected in rates based on a test year or historical balance.

az:HB 2800.title: ignition interlock devices; violation; classification
az:HB 2800.summary: Raises from a class 1 misdemeanor to a class 6 felony the penalty for knowingly lending a vehicle without an ignition interlock device to a DUI-restricted driver who then causes a collision with serious injury or death.

az:HB 2830.title: fetal and prenatal development; instruction
az:HB 2830.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt age-appropriate science standards that include instruction on fetal and prenatal human development.

az:HB 2874.title: campaign committees; termination statements; contributions
az:HB 2874.summary: Changes how late-filing penalties are assessed for campaign committees that file termination statements, letting treasurers certify the committee received no contributions. Applies retroactive to July 6, 2016, as an emergency measure.

az:HB 2941.title: motorcycles; reckless driving
az:HB 2941.summary: Classifies riding a motorcycle between lanes of traffic, or passing in the same lane, as reckless driving, a class 2 misdemeanor, except where authorized.

az:HB 2950.title: tourism improvement areas; municipalities; counties
az:HB 2950.summary: Allows cities and counties to create tourism improvement areas funded by assessments on lodging businesses, managed by a destination marketing organization, and sets procedures for formation petitions, hearings, assessments and dissolution.

az:HB 2957.title: driver license; enhanced; mobile; prohibition
az:HB 2957.summary: Bars the state, cities, towns and counties from requiring digital or mobile driver licenses and requires physical licenses to be accepted; requires the transportation department to keep issuing non-REAL ID licenses, with limits on retaining documents and sharing data.

az:HB 2970.title: fraudulent schemes; artifices; jurisdiction
az:HB 2970.summary: Provides that in fraudulent scheme prosecutions the state need not prove all unlawful acts happened in Arizona or one jurisdiction, and that this is no defense.

az:HB 2995.title: domestic relations; domestic violence
az:HB 2995.summary: Extends the domestic violence presumption to parenting time as well as legal decision-making, requires written court findings, revises rebuttal factors, requires clear and convincing evidence to overcome it for decision-making or unsupervised time, and defines coercive control.

az:HB 4010.title: genetic counselors; board; licensure
az:HB 4010.summary: Creates the Board of Genetic Counselors to license and regulate genetic counselors, and requires practitioners to be licensed in Arizona on completion of Board rulemaking and no later than October 1, 2026.

az:HB 4018.title: technical correction; public records
az:HB 4018.summary: Lets a county sheriff use volunteer posse and reserve organizations and gives the sheriff exclusive authority to regulate their organization and equipment under written policy.

az:HB 4043.title: training; AEDs; CPR; school personnel
az:HB 4043.summary: Requires each school district and charter school campus to have, from August 1, 2027, at least one employee trained in CPR and first aid, and in AED use if the campus has one.

az:HB 4049.title: attorney general; legal counsel; exemption
az:HB 4049.summary: Lets the Department of Child Safety employ its own legal counsel, and requires the Attorney General to represent the state's interest, not the department, in child-welfare cases alleging department misconduct.

az:HB 4056.title: technical correction; double punishment
az:HB 4056.summary: Bars charging a legislator any fee for a public records request made in an official capacity, and requires the records be provided in any format the legislator requests.

az:HB 4117.title: disturbing religious services; worship
az:HB 4117.summary: Makes it a class 1 misdemeanor to intentionally block entry to a place of worship or cause a protracted disruption of a religious service; a class 6 felony for repeat offenses, force or threats, or group blocking of entry. Peaceful protest is exempt.

az:SB 1011.title: medical examiners; sudden infant death
az:SB 1011.summary: Requires medical examiners or forensic pathologists, in sudden and unexplained infant deaths, to review the infant's immunization history and any countermeasures given in the 90 days before death, and report the death to a national case registry.

az:SB 1012.title: concealed weapons; notice; repeal
az:SB 1012.summary: Lets permit holders who do not drink carry concealed handguns in restaurants with only a restaurant liquor license; allows license suspension over concealed handguns only for gross negligence; limits licensee liability for handgun-caused harm unless a court or jury finds specified conduct.

az:SB 1013.title: public employees; merit; hiring practices
az:SB 1013.summary: Bars the state and political subdivisions from adopting hiring policies based on anything other than merit, or from manipulating employee composition by race, ethnicity, sex or national origin; allows lawsuits with attorney fees; keeps veterans' preference.

az:SB 1015.title: gender transition procedures; provider liability
az:SB 1015.summary: Makes health professionals who provide gender transition procedures to minors strictly liable for related injury and detransition costs within 25 years, and allows injured persons to sue for damages, including punitive damages, and attorney fees.

az:SB 1018.title: foreign law; sharia law; prohibition
az:SB 1018.summary: Adds Sharia law, and foreign, religious or cultural customs or practices that allow or excuse listed conduct such as honor killings or forced marriage, to the definition of foreign law in Arizona's limit on applying foreign law in courts.

az:SB 1040.title: voter registration rolls; internet access
az:SB 1040.summary: Requires county recorders to give the public free, read-only, downloadable internet access to voter registration rolls; extends the political-and-election use limit to the rolls; removes the fee schedule and the existing limits on posting voter data online and on access to certain personal details.

az:SB 1057.title: watermark; paper ballots
az:SB 1057.summary: Repeals and re-enacts the existing ballot-paper section without changing its text: vendors must hold ISO 27001, 17025 or 9001:2015 certification, and ballots must use at least three listed anti-fraud features such as watermarked paper, holographic foil or security inks.

az:SB 1060.title: voter registration; temporary absence
az:SB 1060.summary: Repeals the provisions letting a U.S. citizen who has never lived in the U.S., and whose U.S.-citizen parent is registered to vote in Arizona, register and vote by federal write-in early ballot, and removes the matching residence rule.

az:SB 1061.title: fentanyl; sale amount; nine grams
az:SB 1061.summary: Lowers from 200 grams to 9 grams the amount of fentanyl in a sale to another person that triggers specified criminal sentencing ranges.

az:SB 1068.title: disruption; educational institution; concealed weapon
az:SB 1068.summary: Bars the governing board of any university, college or community college from enforcing a policy that prohibits concealed weapon permit holders from possessing a concealed weapon, or prohibits the lawful transport or storage of a firearm.

az:SB 1069.title: prohibited weapons; muffling device; repeal
az:SB 1069.summary: Removes devices designed to muffle the sound of a firearm (silencers) from the state's definition of prohibited weapons.

az:SB 1075.title: foreign entities; land; legislative approval
az:SB 1075.summary: Bars sale, lease or sublease of Arizona land to a foreign entity hostile to the United States without Foreign Entity Review Commission approval, requires grantee identification be filed with the Department of Real Estate, and allows the Attorney General to seek civil penalties.

az:SB 1095.title: gender transition; minors; prohibitions
az:SB 1095.summary: Extends Arizona's ban on gender reassignment surgery for minors to all gender transition procedures, including puberty blockers and cross-sex hormones, and to other health professionals; also bars referrals for them; effective April 1, 2027.

az:SB 1113.title: service of process; evaluation agencies
az:SB 1113.summary: Lets a court authorize employees of a licensed screening or evaluation agency to serve evaluation or treatment petition documents on a patient already admitted to the facility; the agency may be reimbursed for this only under a county contract.

az:SB 1121.title: radiation protection systems; medical procedures
az:SB 1121.summary: Bars hospitals from requiring health professionals to wear lead aprons during cardiac catheterization procedures using real-time x-ray when the room has a radiation protection system.

az:SB 1124.title: health boards; evaluations; notice
az:SB 1124.summary: Requires health profession regulatory boards to vote on, and give the professional at least 14 days' notice with a summary of the complaint before, ordering a psychological or psychiatric evaluation. The professional may submit a written response and testify.

az:SB 1127.title: duty to report; abuse; neglect
az:SB 1127.summary: Requires mandatory reporters with direct knowledge of child abuse or neglect to report to the Department of Child Safety rather than delegate, except in health care institutions; bars school resource and safety officers from supervising law enforcement investigations of school employee conduct involving minors.

az:SB 1136.title: workers' compensation; death benefits; remarriage
az:SB 1136.summary: Lets the surviving spouse of a first responder keep receiving workers' compensation death benefits for life, including spouses who lost benefits through remarriage on or after January 1, 2000, going forward only.

az:SB 1160.title: drones; entertainment districts; prohibition
az:SB 1160.summary: Makes it a class 1 misdemeanor to intentionally operate a civil drone within 5,280 feet of, or 5,280 feet above, a ticketed entertainment event, with exceptions such as written consent, venue and utility employees, and owners over their own property.

az:SB 1164.title: ALTCS; providers; change of ownership
az:SB 1164.summary: Sets change-of-ownership procedures so licensed skilled nursing and assisted living facilities can keep processing claims for services to Arizona Long-Term Care System members.

az:SB 1167.title: cities; towns; counties; posting; website
az:SB 1167.summary: Lets cities, towns and counties meet legal notice advertising requirements by posting on their own website and the website of a qualified newspaper.

az:SB 1174.title: DCS; intake hotline; case history
az:SB 1174.summary: Requires, from January 1, 2027, the Department of Child Safety intake hotline to produce one report covering the full hotline and investigation history of a child and the child's siblings.

az:SB 1180.title: DOR; income tax forms; conformity
az:SB 1180.summary: Extends the deadline for penalty-free amended returns after federal tax nonconformity to the extended due date of the second following year, sets publication dates for supplemental forms, and has the Department of Revenue assume conformity when preparing forms.

az:SB 1189.title: campaign spending; personal security
az:SB 1189.summary: Lets a candidate committee spend campaign money on the personal security of the candidate and family members.

az:SB 1198.title: Arizona beef council; continuation
az:SB 1198.summary: Continues the Arizona Beef Council and the State Veterinary Medical Examining Board until July 1, 2034.

az:SB 1206.title: storm related insurance claims
az:SB 1206.summary: Bars adjusters from working on repairs for claims they adjust and from soliciting clients during an active loss event or emergency response; bars contractors from soliciting then, or paying or promising to pay a policyholder's deductible on catastrophic storm claims.

az:SB 1210.title: private postsecondary education; nondomiciled institutions
az:SB 1210.summary: Creates a separate registration process for private postsecondary schools based outside Arizona, setting the information they must submit to the state board.

az:SB 1212.title: health insurance; reimbursement rates; vaccines
az:SB 1212.summary: Bars health insurers, beginning January 1, 2027, from paying a health professional a different reimbursement rate because a covered patient refuses one or more vaccines.

az:SB 1215.title: firefighters; occupational disease; cancers
az:SB 1215.summary: Clarifies, retroactive to July 1, 2021, which conditions are presumed work-related for workers' compensation coverage of peace officers, firefighters and fire investigators.

az:SB 1221.title: tax laws; interpretation; application; hearing
az:SB 1221.summary: Requires the Department of Revenue to notify the Legislature before adopting a tax-law interpretation that adversely affects taxpayers, and to testify if the Legislature holds a hearing.

az:SB 1233.title: administrative deficiencies; cure period
az:SB 1233.summary: Bars the Department of Health Services, AHCCCS and Department of Economic Security from disciplining or taking enforcement action against a licensed or contracted facility with only administrative deficiencies unless the facility first gets 72 hours to cure them.

az:SB 1242.title: mental health; hearings; audiovisual technology
az:SB 1242.summary: Changes procedures for court-ordered mental health evaluation and treatment, including virtual hearings and testimony, and sets care-coordination requirements between treatment agencies and secure behavioral health residential facilities.

az:SB 1253.title: safe haven providers; hospital deliveries
az:SB 1253.summary: Lets a parent or agent surrender a newborn at the hospital of birth without first being discharged and later returning to complete the surrender.

az:SB 1259.title: campaigns; protected residential addresses
az:SB 1259.summary: Lets a person whose residential address is protected by a court-sealed voter record give an alternate mailing address and attest they reside in the district they propose to represent, on committee organization statements and annual public officer financial disclosures.

az:SB 1274.title: special plate; police foundation
az:SB 1274.summary: Creates a timeshare salesperson license, effective July 1, 2027, and sets licensure requirements and qualifications.

az:SB 1280.title: public monies; Mexican wolf; prohibition
az:SB 1280.summary: Bars the Game and Fish Commission from transporting Mexican gray wolf puppies into Arizona or using public money or resources to do so.

az:SB 1281.title: federal government; land acquisition; consent
az:SB 1281.summary: Requires escrow agents to notify the Senate president and House speaker when private land goes into escrow for sale to the federal government, and extends the State Land Department's catalog and boundary review from national monuments to other listed federal designations.

az:SB 1286.title: veterinarian visits; electronic means; prescriptions
az:SB 1286.summary: Extends from 14 to 30 days the period a veterinarian may prescribe and renew non-antimicrobial, non-flea-and-tick drugs after an electronic examination; allows one electronic antimicrobial prescription of up to 14 days, and flea and tick prescriptions of up to three months.

az:SB 1315.title: public schools; interoperable communications; requirements
az:SB 1315.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools that receive state or local law enforcement money for interoperable communications to maintain capabilities to alert and talk with law enforcement in school emergencies and file annual affidavits; agencies with available money must offer it.

az:SB 1318.title: mammography results; notice; repeal
az:SB 1318.summary: Repeals the requirement that health care facilities give patients identified as having heterogeneously dense or extremely dense breasts a specified notice.

az:SB 1327.title: ABOR; foreign countries; restrictions; penalties
az:SB 1327.summary: Requires the Board of Regents to have each public university adopt a research security policy to guard research against foreign influence, and sets required policy elements and reporting to the Board.

az:SB 1332.title: light rail expansion; participation; prohibition
az:SB 1332.summary: Requires the Auditor General, with an independent transportation research entity, to review light rail expansion in Maricopa County by December 31, 2027, comparing it with other transit options, and report to the governor and legislative leaders; the act is repealed after June 30, 2028.

az:SB 1335.title: water banking; annual report; posting
az:SB 1335.summary: Lets a holder of groundwater savings credits keep irrigating the land under its former irrigation grandfathered right for up to two years after the credits are issued, under a temporary permit from the Department of Water Resources.

az:SB 1336.title: state land department; continuation; oversight
az:SB 1336.summary: Continues the State Land Department until July 1, 2030, creates a joint legislative ad hoc committee on state land oversight, changes mineral exploration permit rules, and lets the land commissioner renew some production leases without public auction.

az:SB 1338.title: state; local public benefits; eligibility
az:SB 1338.summary: Removes the exclusion for state public retirement system benefits from the definition of state or local public benefit, and lists persons who are ineligible to receive any state or local public benefit.

az:SB 1345.title: health facilities; anonymous complaints; prohibition
az:SB 1345.summary: Requires the Department of Health Services to approve or deny initial health care institution license applications within 90 days and submit third-party accreditation survey results for certification within 30 days; lets its Director set initial licensing inspection fees by rule.

az:SB 1366.title: commercial buildings; telecommunications services
az:SB 1366.summary: Creates the Public Property Towing and Impound Practices Study Committee.

az:SB 1399.title: prepaid capitated contractors; cost reports
az:SB 1399.summary: Requires the state Medicaid agency (AHCCCS) to report to the Legislature and Governor each December 1 the share of money its prepaid managed-care contractors spend on provider payments and on categories of administrative costs.

az:SB 1422.title: credit enhancement eligibility board; continuation
az:SB 1422.summary: Continues the Credit Enhancement Eligibility Board, which oversees the program guaranteeing financing for achievement district public schools, for 10 years, until July 1, 2036.

az:SB 1429.title: board of directors; commerce authority.
az:SB 1429.summary: Applies a strict compliance standard of review to city, town and county initiatives and referenda, and adds requirements for petition circulators.

az:SB 1445.title: water quality; testing; on-site
az:SB 1445.summary: Lets cities and towns of 1,000 to 9,999 people test bacteriological samples on-site, and bars the Department of Environmental Quality from requiring more than 1,000 gallons of storage at community water systems with 25 or fewer connections in counties of 400,000 or fewer.

az:SB 1452.title: cargo theft task force
az:SB 1452.summary: Directs the Attorney General to create a Cargo Theft Task Force, subject to legislative appropriation, to investigate cargo theft and related offenses, with set membership and annual reporting.

az:SB 1456.title: ADOT; primitive roads; designation
az:SB 1456.summary: Exempts employers and associations with at least 500 employees or members from the bond that authorized third-party driver license providers must post.

az:SB 1457.title: air mobility fund; border security
az:SB 1457.summary: Allows the advanced air mobility fund to be used to buy advanced air mobility vehicles for border security, giving priority to counties along the international border.

az:SB 1475.title: interscholastic activities; criminal offenses; ineligibility
az:SB 1475.summary: Requires school district boards to bar students from school-sponsored interscholastic activities if convicted of, or admitting to, listed offenses such as aggravated assault, sex offenses, stalking and domestic violence, and to require students to certify whether they committed one.

az:SB 1476.title: child neglect; prenatal substance exposure
az:SB 1476.summary: Makes it a class 6 felony for a person with custody to neglect a child through conduct that harms the child, when it involves a newborn's prenatal drug exposure or fetal alcohol findings; a mother who completed treatment during pregnancy has an affirmative defense.

az:SB 1477.title: assisted living facilities; referral agents
az:SB 1477.summary: Requires assisted living referral agencies to document that referral agents are not on the adult protective services registry, or use an accredited provider for criminal history checks, and to carry $1 million per occurrence and $3 million aggregate general and professional liability insurance.

az:SB 1494.title: technical correction; open pit mining
az:SB 1494.summary: Bars health care providers, institutions and drug manufacturers from paying enrollees' health insurance premiums unless federal law allows, bars clinicians from advising patients to switch plans unless licensed insurance producers, and sets civil penalties of at least $1,000 per violation.

az:SB 1497.title: classical learning; tests; examinations
az:SB 1497.summary: Requires school districts with a self-insurance program and at least 300 employees to obtain coverage quotes at least once every four years.

az:SB 1520.title: agencies; immigration; data sharing
az:SB 1520.summary: Requires this state and its agencies to share any data the federal government requests about unauthorized immigrants or visa overstayers; the requirement is repealed after December 31, 2028.

az:SB 1549.title: ultralight vehicles; definition
az:SB 1549.summary: Adds ultralight vehicles, meaning single-occupant aircraft without airworthiness certificates under set weight and fuel limits, to the definition of advanced air mobility.

az:SB 1560.title: cap; water supply development fund
az:SB 1560.summary: Raises the cap on a single loan from the Water Supply Development Revolving Fund from $3 million to $20 million.

az:SB 1563.title: barbering and cosmetology board; continuation
az:SB 1563.summary: Continues the Board of Barbering and Cosmetology until July 1, 2034 and lowers the maximum fees for many licenses and renewals.

az:SB 1572.title: public schools; civics instruction requirement
az:SB 1572.summary: Requires each public school to observe Celebrate Freedom Week, with instruction on the Declaration of Independence and Constitution in social studies courses and a student recitation of a Declaration passage in grades 3-12. Sets exemptions and State Board of Education duties.

az:SB 1573.title: judicial determinations; religious sectarian laws
az:SB 1573.summary: Bars courts, including federal courts sitting in diversity, from relying on religious sectarian law as controlling or persuasive authority. Exempts law based on Anglo-American legal tradition and recognition of a traditional marriage between a man and a woman.

az:SB 1620.title: Arizona space commission; board; membership
az:SB 1620.summary: Requires municipalities to set a reimbursement process for telecommunications utility facility relocation costs and to give the utility public notice of voter-approved bond projects at least 30 days before requesting relocation.

az:SB 1624.title: photo radar enforcement; civil penalty
az:SB 1624.summary: Caps the penalty for photo-enforcement traffic violations at $75 with exceptions, sends $15 to the Peace Officer Training Equipment Fund, and bars using such violations to set insurance or affect driving privileges.

az:SB 1627.title: schools; prohibition; unmanned aircraft
az:SB 1627.summary: Makes it a class 3 misdemeanor for a hobby or recreational drone operator to photograph or loiter 200 feet or less above posted, non-residential K-12 school property after being told to leave; people with legal authority over the property or the owner's consent are exempt.

az:SB 1630.title: home; community-based services; mental illness
az:SB 1630.summary: Creates a three-year pilot, pending federal approval, for enhanced residential treatment services for adults with serious mental illness, run by AHCCCS with enrollment capped at 60 members unless data supports raising it; also adds licensing for enhanced residential treatment facilities.

az:SB 1669.title: sexual offenses; victim; evidence
az:SB 1669.summary: Replaces "trauma" with "physical injury" in the exception allowing evidence of a sexual offense victim's specific sexual activity that shows the source of semen, pregnancy, disease or injury.

az:SB 1671.title: gaming; racing; boxing; conflict-of-interest continuation
az:SB 1671.summary: Continues the racing and boxing commissions and the Department of Gaming until July 1, 2032, requires conflict-of-interest disclosure forms from their directors and employees, and adds complaint tracking and an annual complaint report for the gaming department.

az:SB 1711.title: age-appropriate resources; inappropriate contact; schools
az:SB 1711.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to compile recommended resources for age-appropriate education on recognizing and preventing inappropriate contact, and requires public schools to make them available to students and parents.

az:SB 1713.title: AHCCCS; procurement; contracting
az:SB 1713.summary: Lets pharmacists, under a Board of Pharmacy protocol, order CLIA-waived tests and start treatment for flu, strep throat and COVID-19 (minors need parental consent; no opioids), and start HIV prevention medications.

az:SB 1723.title: domestic violence; release conditions
az:SB 1723.summary: Requires judges to impose electronic monitoring, where available, and a no-contact order on people released after a domestic violence charge causing physical harm; bars unsupervised parenting time on a finding of significant domestic violence; lets courts require order-of-protection defendants to give identifying information.

az:SB 1741.title: public schools; released time courses
az:SB 1741.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to let students attend released time courses of religious instruction during the school day, with parental consent and academic credit, and lets adversely affected persons sue for violations.

az:SB 1808.title: homeowners' associations; allied countries' flags
az:SB 1808.summary: Adds a flag from a nation allied with the United States as a major non-NATO ally and established on May 14, 1948 to the flags that condominium and planned community associations may not prohibit owners from displaying.

az:SB 1814.title: substance use disorder treatment; committee
az:SB 1814.summary: Creates the Substance Use Disorder Treatment Standards and Oversight Study Committee to review treatment programs, access gaps, standards and funding needs, and sets its membership and reporting duties.

ca:AB 1537.title: Peace officers: secondary employment.
ca:AB 1537.summary: Bars certain peace officers from secondary employment involving immigration enforcement, makes violations grounds for decertification, and requires officers to report related job offers to their agency, which must keep records.

ca:AB 1645.title: Corrections: Humanizing and Uniting Generations Safely Act of 2026.
ca:AB 1645.summary: Enacts the Humanizing and Uniting Generations Safely Act: prison visiting regulations must consider the importance of physical contact, and the department may not unreasonably restrict nonsexual contact or discipline for physical contact without first giving a warning.

ca:AB 1679.title: Local pop-up small business program.
ca:AB 1679.summary: Requires cities and counties to allow temporary pop-up small businesses to operate up to 120 days in eligible commercial spaces without full permanent-occupancy compliance, while meeting temporary health and safety standards.

ca:AB 1776.title: Cartwright Act: violations.
ca:AB 1776.summary: Prohibits monopolizing or monopsonizing any part of trade or commerce, requires plaintiffs to prove substantial market power, exempts small businesses, and limits enforcement actions to the Attorney General or district attorneys.

ca:AB 1793.title: Cash payments: calculation.
ca:AB 1793.summary: Enacts the California Common Cents Act, requiring merchants to round cash transaction totals to the nearest five cents, with rounding disregarded for tax calculations.

ca:AB 1860.title: School facilities: design-build: alternative design-build: county superintendents of schools.
ca:AB 1860.summary: Authorizes county superintendents of schools to use design-build and alternative design-build contracts on the same terms as school districts, with exclusive authority to award them for county offices of education.

ca:AB 1876.title: Health care coverage: nondiscrimination.
ca:AB 1876.summary: Bars health plans and insurers from excluding, denying benefits to, or discriminating against enrollees based on race, color, national origin, age, disability, or sex, with sex defined to include sex characteristics, pregnancy and gender identity.

ca:AB 1881.title: California Indian Freedom Act of 2026.
ca:AB 1881.summary: Enacts the California Indian Freedom Act of 2026, barring governmental agencies from substantially burdening California tribes' religious practices or sacred site access on state lands without a compelling interest, starting January 1, 2028.

ca:AB 1883.title: Workplace surveillance tools.
ca:AB 1883.summary: Bars employers, including governmental entities, from using AI workplace surveillance tools that collect neural data or recognize emotional states, with exceptions; the Labor Commissioner or public prosecutors enforce, with civil penalties up to $500 per violation.

ca:AB 1886.title: Wards: probation.
ca:AB 1886.summary: Applies the 12-month probation limit to wards placed in out-of-home placements, lets courts extend probation but bars new conditions during the extension, and exempts wards committed to secure youth treatment facilities.

ca:AB 1940.title: Unlawful practices: discrimination: menopause.
ca:AB 1940.summary: Adds perimenopause, menopause, postmenopause and related medical conditions to the definition of sex in the Fair Employment and Housing Act and the Unruh Civil Rights Act.

ca:AB 1944.title: Zero-emission transit buses: axle weight.
ca:AB 1944.summary: Until January 1, 2032, sets higher axle weight limits, up to 25,000 pounds, for zero-emission transit buses procured through solicitations issued between 2027 and 2031.

ca:AB 1997.title: Land use: housing development approvals: timelines and processes.
ca:AB 1997.summary: Requires a local agency to approve or disapprove a housing development project within 30 days after certification of its environmental impact report, under specified conditions.

ca:AB 2038.title: Residential property insurance: cancellations and nonrenewals.
ca:AB 2038.summary: Raises from two to three annual periods (36 months) the renewal period insurers must offer after a disaster-caused total loss of a primary structure, and from one to two years the ban on cancelling or non-renewing policies in or next to a fire perimeter.

ca:AB 2065.title: Rates: prohibited cost recovery.
ca:AB 2065.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to find prohibited cost recovery when a utility records ratepayer-excluded costs, to disallow those costs and fine the utility one to three times the amount, and requires annual utility reports on instances.

ca:AB 2076.title: The Parent's Accountability and Child Protection Act: online marketplaces: nitrous oxide.
ca:AB 2076.summary: Adds nitrous oxide to products online sellers must verify age for, bars paying for such products with gift cards, and lets courts raise penalties to up to $250,000 per violation for businesses with over $25 million in annual revenue.

ca:AB 2084.title: Corporation Tax Law: tax-exempt organizations: revocation of tax-exempt status.
ca:AB 2084.summary: Lets the Franchise Tax Board, at its discretion, keep a nonprofit's state tax exemption after its federal exemption is suspended or revoked, if the cause was not fraud, fund misuse, failure to file, or other reporting or governance breaches.

ca:AB 2128.title: Housing authorities: term limits and work requirements.
ca:AB 2128.summary: Bars housing authorities and similar providers from imposing term limits or work requirements as a condition of housing eligibility or rent subsidy, unless federal law requires them, while allowing voluntary job training programs.

ca:AB 2222.title: Personal Income Tax Law and Corporation Tax Law: credits: local news outlets: business expense deduction: excessive employee remuneration.
ca:AB 2222.summary: Creates a tax credit for 2027 through 2031: $20,000 per full-time qualifying journalist (up to five), $15,000 for each beyond five, $7,500 per part-time journalist, and an extra $15,000 per new full-time journalism position.

ca:AB 2263.title: Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority: employee housing: transit-oriented joint development projects.
ca:AB 2263.summary: Authorizes the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority to acquire property for employee housing projects serving its employees and the public, and to build affordable rental and for-sale housing for employees, with an annual report to the Legislature.

ca:AB 2313.title: Gas corporations: gas distribution service line replacements: alternatives.
ca:AB 2313.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to have each gas utility, by January 1, 2028, offer certain residential customers whose gas service line is to be replaced a monetary incentive to end gas service instead; emergency replacements are exempt.

ca:AB 2405.title: Mental health.
ca:AB 2405.summary: Requires peace officers taking a person to a designated mental health facility for assessment to take them to the closest appropriate facility, and lets the person state a facility preference.

ca:AB 2493.title: Electrical corporations: interconnection: Public Utilities Commission: transmission development monitor.
ca:AB 2493.summary: Requires large electrical utilities and transmission owners to submit project schedules for transmission projects needing Public Utilities Commission approval, and requires the commission to create a transmission development monitor by October 1, 2027 to review progress.

ca:AB 2499.title: Health care coverage: claims payments.
ca:AB 2499.summary: As passed by the Assembly, requires the state occupational safety division to propose a heat standard for prison workers by July 1, 2027, and the corrections department to set interim relief measures for excessive weather by April 1, 2027 and run a temperature-monitoring pilot.

ca:AB 2563.title: Sex discrimination: scope.
ca:AB 2563.summary: Requires that state laws banning sex or gender discrimination be interpreted to prohibit sex discrimination, defined to include discrimination based on actual or perceived characteristics, including degree of conformity to sex or gender stereotypes.

ca:AB 2595.title: San Mateo Electric Bicycle Safety Pilot Program.
ca:AB 2595.summary: Until January 1, 2031, lets San Mateo County and its local authorities ban children under 12 from riding class 1 or 2 electric bicycles, with a warning for 60 days and then a $25 fine.

ca:AB 2601.title: Planning and zoning: housing development: streamlined approval and subdivisions.
ca:AB 2601.summary: Makes a housing development of up to two units in a single-family zone eligible for processing alongside an urban lot split parcel map, and lets local agencies condition permits on first recording that map.

ca:AB 2647.title: Energy: nuclear powerplants: assessment.
ca:AB 2647.summary: Requires the Energy Commission to complete by January 1, 2028 an assessment of advanced nuclear technology for critical infrastructure and whether new in-state nuclear plants could meet electricity needs.

ca:AB 2656.title: Public employees: notice: artificial intelligence performing service within scope of work.
ca:AB 2656.summary: Requires certain public employers to give a recognized employee organization 45 days' written notice before developing, buying, or requiring generative AI to perform work within that union's job classifications.

ca:AB 2724.title: Insurance: distressed areas.
ca:AB 2724.summary: Requires the Department of Insurance, by July 1, 2027 and yearly, to update distressed areas based on wildland-urban interface changes and hold a public meeting on FAIR Plan factors, and to publish a list of wildland-urban interface ZIP Codes by January 1, 2028.

ca:AB 40.title: California Environmental Quality Act: environmental impact reports: coal handling, storage, and export.
ca:AB 40.summary: Requires an environmental impact report before approving a large-volume bulk coal facility (over 5 million short tons yearly), and bars relying on an existing report when capacity or coal type changes.

ca:AB 635.title: Mobilehome Residency Law Protection Program: Attorney General.
ca:AB 635.summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to refer alleged Mobilehome Residency Law and park closure violations to a nonprofit legal services provider within five days, and lets it refer local ordinance violations to enforcement agencies.

ca:AB 801.title: Nondiscrimination.
ca:AB 801.summary: Enacts the California Fair Lending Examination Act, requiring the financial regulator to examine certain banks and credit unions at least every four years for compliance with mortgage-lending nondiscrimination laws, and to add that check to mortgage lender examinations.

ca:SB 1049.title: Health care claims reimbursement.
ca:SB 1049.summary: Gives claimants at least 90 days to submit a corrected claim after a health plan or insurer denies a claim or sends an overpayment notice over a fixable defect, and bars denying it as late.

ca:SB 1099.title: State and local public benefits.
ca:SB 1099.summary: Clarifies that cities', counties' and hospital districts' existing authority to aid people who would otherwise qualify but for a federal welfare law's limits counts as authorization to provide a state or local public benefit under that law.

ca:SB 1111.title: Digital replicas.
ca:SB 1111.summary: Clarifies that a person's voice or likeness includes computer-generated digital replicas for right-of-publicity claims and false impersonation law, and removes a rebuttable presumption for employee likenesses in advertisements.

ca:SB 1130.title: Invasion of privacy: wearable recording devices.
ca:SB 1130.summary: Bars using a wearable recording device to capture sound or video of others in areas of a business where they expect privacy, without their explicit consent, and bars disabling its recording indicator, with exemptions for hearing and communication aids.

ca:SB 1209.title: Insurance: examination of insurers.
ca:SB 1209.summary: Requires insurers examined by the Insurance Commissioner to correct violations identified in the report, subjects non-correcting insurers to penalties, and lets the commissioner issue show-cause orders to compel compliance.

ca:SB 1237.title: Civil Rights Department.
ca:SB 1237.summary: Raises the penalty for repeat failures to file employer pay data reports to up to $1,000 per employee, and requires the Civil Rights Department to publish the number of reports submitted each year.

ca:SB 1246.title: Autonomous vehicles.
ca:SB 1246.summary: Requires autonomous vehicle makers to maintain capacity for peak concurrent remote assistance sessions, keep remote drivers in the U.S. with California-valid licenses, and immediately dispatch local incident technicians after crashes or emergency-official requests.

ca:SB 1255.title: Postsecondary education: Designation of California Hispanic-Serving Institutions.
ca:SB 1255.summary: Establishes, upon appropriation, a California Hispanic-Serving Institutions designation and governing board, with the California State University Chancellor's office managing applications for campuses serving Latino students.

ca:SB 1359.title: Natural Gas Ratepayer Protection Act.
ca:SB 1359.summary: Requires gas utilities to report annually on gas pipeline replacement spending, and requires the Public Utilities Commission to consider a depreciation framework that reflects expected declines in gas demand.

ca:SB 1369.title: Recall petitions.
ca:SB 1369.summary: Requires paid petition signature gatherers to orally tell each person they are paid, and sets a 120-day deadline to submit recall petitions for superior court judges in jurisdictions with 50,000 or more registered voters.

ca:SB 1379.title: County of Riverside: separation of county offices: in-custody reports.
ca:SB 1379.summary: Requires Riverside County to separate the sheriff and coroner offices by July 1, 2027, create a medical examiner office to handle death investigations, and publish information on in-custody persons online.

ca:SB 1406.title: Sales and Use Tax Law: vehicles: shell companies.
ca:SB 1406.summary: Treats a partnership as a California resident for the vehicle, vessel and aircraft use-tax presumption if 50% of its interests are held by residents, treats shell companies with a resident owner as residents, and makes shell company officers and owners personally liable for unpaid tax.

ca:SB 1417.title: Mutual water companies: assessments and water charges: notice.
ca:SB 1417.summary: Bars mutual water companies from billing shareholders' tenants for water costs, with exceptions, and requires those operating public water systems to give notice and hold a public meeting before an assessment or a water charge increase above 20%.

ca:SB 503.title: Health care services: artificial intelligence.
ca:SB 503.summary: Requires developers and deployers of AI clinical decision support systems to identify risks of biased impacts, and developers to provide statements of intended uses, known risks, and documentation to deployers.

ca:SB 577.title: Public entities.
ca:SB 577.summary: Shortens from 5 to 3 years the discovery-based filing window for childhood sexual assault claims from before 2024, and requires plaintiffs 40 or older suing public entities over them to prove by clear and convincing evidence that the entity knew of misconduct.

ca:SB 677.title: Housing financing: joint powers agreements: bond approvals: subdivisions: tentative and final maps: appeals.
ca:SB 677.summary: States that a joint powers authority's jurisdiction covers the combined area of its members, and lets the State Treasurer join such authorities without Department of General Services approval to give federal tax approvals for certain rental housing bonds.

ca:SB 685.title: Special education: nonpublic schools and agencies.
ca:SB 685.summary: Removes the requirement that nonpublic special education schools be nonsectarian, while barring public funds from paying for religious instruction and barring religious instruction for pupils placed by local education agencies.

ca:SB 811.title: Hazardous materials: metal shredding facilities.
ca:SB 811.summary: Creates a permit system run by the Department of Toxic Substances Control for metal shredding facilities, with application requirements, public meetings, and operating and transport rules, separate from hazardous waste law.

ca:SB 868.title: Electricity: portable solar generation devices.
ca:SB 868.summary: Until January 1, 2030, exempts portable solar generation devices from interconnection requirements and bars utilities from charging customers fees for using them.

ca:SB 903.title: Mental health professionals: artificial intelligence.
ca:SB 903.summary: Limits use of artificial intelligence in psychotherapy to administrative or supplementary support, and requires patients be informed and consent before AI records, transcribes, or screens them for psychotherapy.

ca:SB 905.title: Electricity.
ca:SB 905.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to consider reduced returns on equity for certain utility capital costs, open a rulemaking on alternative financing with a report by December 31, 2028, and require large electric utilities to publish grid utilization data.

ca:SB 913.title: Resource adequacy: aggregated distributed energy resources.
ca:SB 913.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission, by June 30, 2028, to improve pathways for aggregated distributed energy resources to count as resource adequacy capacity, without duplicate compensation for net metering customers.

ca:SB 938.title: Peace officers: training requirements.
ca:SB 938.summary: Provides that service as a federal immigration inspection, border enforcement, or removal officer, and its training, does not alone qualify for a Regular Basic Course Waiver for peace officer training.

ca:SB 941.title: Private detention facilities: canteens.
ca:SB 941.summary: Caps the price of commissary items at private for-profit detention facilities at a 35 percent markup above the vendor price.

ca:SB 944.title: Medi-Cal: acupuncture.
ca:SB 944.summary: Makes acupuncture a covered Medi-Cal benefit subject to utilization controls and federal funding, instead of covered only when federal matching funds are provided, and covers it subject to appropriation if federal funds are unavailable.

ca:SB 947.title: Employment: automated decision systems.
ca:SB 947.summary: Beginning July 1, 2027, bars employers from relying solely on an automated decision system for discipline or termination, requires human corroboration, written notice and employee access to their data used, and bars retaliation; the Labor Commissioner enforces.

ca:SB 951.title: Employment: technological displacement: notice.
ca:SB 951.summary: Requires employers giving mass layoff notice due to AI or automation to describe the affected job functions, directs the state to publish summaries of such notices, and requires a report to the Legislature on AI's hiring effects by 2028.

ca:SB 996.title: Manufactured housing: conformity.
ca:SB 996.summary: Changes the state definition of manufactured home to a structure built on or after June 15, 1976, with or without a foundation, matching the federal definition.

ct:HB 5001.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ABSENTEE VOTING FOR ALL AND VARIOUS OTHER REFORMS RELATED TO THE ADMINISTRATION OF ELECTIONS.
ct:HB 5001.summary: As amended, allows no-excuse absentee voting, consolidates absentee ballot envelopes, sets a process to cure unsigned ballots, requires risk-limiting audits, and bars law enforcement, and anyone wearing a mask, from within 250 feet of election sites, with exceptions.

ct:HB 5004.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CHILD WELFARE ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY.
ct:HB 5004.summary: Requires the Department of Children and Families to make emergency placements with relatives or close family friends when conditions are met, allows appeal of foster license denials, creates caregiver grants (maximum $625) and after-school grants, and requires a public online dashboard.

ct:HB 5039.title: AN ACT REQUIRING TRANSPARENCY AND ADDITIONAL OVERSIGHT OF THE DISTRIBUTION OF CERTAIN LEGISLATIVELY DIRECTED FUNDS AND APPROPRIATIONS FOR OTHER EXPENSES.
ct:HB 5039.summary: Limits state agencies from funding entities at the General Assembly's direction unless legislation or budget sheets name the recipient, requires uniform Office of Policy and Management procedures and recipient and agency reports, and restricts certain uses of agencies' Other Expenses appropriations.

ct:HB 5043.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONVERTIBLE PISTOLS, UNFINISHED FRAMES OR UNFINISHED LOWER RECEIVERS, VOLUNTARY RELINQUISHMENT OF FIREARMS AND AMMUNITION AND REFUNDABILITY OF PERMITS FOR SALE AT RETAIL OF FIREARMS AND FOR CARRYING OF PISTOLS AND REVOLVERS.
ct:HB 5043.summary: Makes it a class D felony to knowingly sell or import convertible pistols made on or after October 1, 2026, bars unpermitted sales of unfinished frames and receivers, allows voluntary surrender of firearms to police, and requires $70 pistol permit refunds when deadlines are missed.

ct:HB 5127.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CREDIT CARDS AND HEALTH AND VETERINARY CARE SERVICES.
ct:HB 5127.summary: As amended, starting January 1, 2027, bars health care and veterinary providers from promoting third-party financing in certain ways, completing applications, or charging a financing account before the service date; requires a written disclosure before discussing financing terms.

ct:HB 5143.title: AN ACT REQUIRING TRAINING FOR HOMEMAKER-COMPANION AGENCY EMPLOYEES.
ct:HB 5143.summary: Requires homemaker-companion agencies to provide at least eight hours of paid training yearly starting January 1, 2027, and registries to ensure referred workers complete approved training.

ct:HB 5145.title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE PUBLIC UTILITIES REGULATORY COMMISSION TO REPORT ON THE REVIEW PROCESS FOR CERTAIN WATER COMPANIES THAT REQUEST TO CEASE OPERATIONS.
ct:HB 5145.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority to report by January 15, 2027 on water company requests to cease operations or discontinue service over the past two years, including docket timelines and materials used.

ct:HB 5208.title: AN ACT CONCERNING DATA SECURITY, PAYROLL PROCESSING, CONSUMER FRAUD PROTECTION, MORTGAGE LOANS AND EMPLOYEE CREDIT RATES.
ct:HB 5208.summary: As amended, requires Department of Banking-regulated entities to adopt written data security programs; requires licensees, banks and credit unions to report data security incidents to the department within three business days; orders a payroll-check study and a fraud working group; narrows flood-insurance notice duties.

ct:HB 5211.title: AN ACT CONCERNING COMMERCIAL FINANCING.
ct:HB 5211.summary: Starting July 1, 2027, applies disclosure and registration rules to all sales-based financing, removing the $250,000 exemption, and requires an estimated APR disclosure; from October 1, 2026, voids confidentiality clauses in new financing contracts.

ct:HB 5229.title: AN ACT CONCERNING GAMING.
ct:HB 5229.summary: Makes gaming changes, including requiring a toll-free help line for online wagering licensees, limiting gaming ads aimed at minors or on college campuses, and requiring a study of prediction markets.

ct:HB 5244.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT'S RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING THE AGENCY FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE CAP AND EMPLOYMENT PROMISSORY NOTES.
ct:HB 5244.summary: Raises from $10 million to $25 million the two-year cap on financial assistance for a business project without legislative approval, and lets employers with over 25 employees require employees to sign promissory notes repaying employer-paid H-1B visa fees.

ct:HB 5256.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE PROCESS FOR INITIATING LOCAL LEGISLATION IN THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY.
ct:HB 5256.summary: Eliminates the requirement that a town or district seeking a change to its special act powers file its request with the secretary of the state 10 days before the legislative session.

ct:HB 5259.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE EDUCATION OF HOMELESS CHILDREN AND YOUTH.
ct:HB 5259.summary: Ties the existing requirement that boards of education serve homeless children and youth under the federal McKinney-Vento Act to the law as it stood on December 23, 2022.

ct:HB 5281.title: AN ACT CONCERNING PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT.
ct:HB 5281.summary: As amended, raises from 10,000 to 20,000 the population ceiling for distressed or environmental justice towns where voters may petition for a referendum reversing a state permit approval or denial for a new waste incinerator or similar facility.

ct:HB 5288.title: AN ACT CONCERNING UTILITY CONNECTIONS FOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS.
ct:HB 5288.summary: Applies the as-of-right accessory dwelling unit zoning rules to towns exercising zoning power under special acts, and bars investor-owned water companies from requiring separate utility connections or imposing connection fees or capacity charges for such units.

ct:HB 5332.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CERTAIN BOATING REGULATIONS.
ct:HB 5332.summary: Changes boating rules: requires operators to bar passengers from sitting on the gunwale with legs outside or standing on it above slow-no-wake speed, requires owner contact information on boats not registered in a state or federally, and raises abandoned-boat fines to $750-$1,000.

ct:HB 5333.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE REGULATION OF STRIPED BASS FISHING IN THE STATE, A WORKING GROUP CONCERNING THE WILDLIFE CONSERVATION PROGRAM AND PROCEDURES CONCERNING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF FISH PASSAGES.
ct:HB 5333.summary: Limits striped bass fishing to catch and release from December 1 to March 31, sets fines of $150 to $500 for violations, creates a wildlife conservation program working group, and lets people petition for fish passages at certain hydroelectric dams.

ct:HB 5336.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ADVANCED NUCLEAR ENERGY.
ct:HB 5336.summary: Requires the Council for Advancing Nuclear Energy Development to study skilled-labor needs in advanced nuclear energy, consulting building-trades and apprenticeship groups, with a progress report due February 15, 2027 and a final report February 1, 2028.

ct:HB 5350.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CANNABIS, HEMP AND INFUSED BEVERAGE REGULATION.
ct:HB 5350.summary: Renames "marijuana" as "cannabis" in state law, lets qualifying out-of-state medical patients buy medical cannabis, bars retailers from keeping age-verification data over 24 hours without written consent, limits retailer credit from producers to 30 days, and creates a cannabis regulatory working group.

ct:HB 5374.title: AN ACT CONCERNING HEALTH COVERAGE MANDATES FOR CERTAIN HEALTH CONDITIONS.
ct:HB 5374.summary: Starting January 1, 2027, requires state-regulated health plans to cover PANDAS/PANS treatment, athletic prosthetic devices, scalp cooling systems during chemotherapy, and infertility diagnosis and treatment under a broader definition of infertility.

ct:HB 5406.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ASSORTED MEASURES RECOGNIZING AND HONORING THE HEROISM OF VETERANS AND MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES AND MAKING VARIOUS REVISIONS TO STATUTES RELATED TO VETERANS' AND MILITARY AFFAIRS.
ct:HB 5406.summary: As amended, creates a veterans dental care program (up to $3,000 per veteran yearly, $1 million per fiscal year), extends some DMV grace periods for armed forces members from 60 to 90 days, waives original license and ID fees for verified veterans, and adds tax deductions.

ct:HB 5467.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DESIGNATION OF A DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT EMPLOYEE FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING CONCIERGE SERVICES TO SMALL BUSINESSES.
ct:HB 5467.summary: Requires the Department of Economic and Community Development commissioner to designate an existing department employee to provide concierge services to small businesses, including information and help with the department's programs. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

ct:HB 5468.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE PROVISION OF PARENT-MANAGED LEARNING.
ct:HB 5468.summary: Starting with the 2028-29 school year, requires parents to file an annual form stating whether their child will attend public school, nonpublic school or parent-managed learning (homeschooling), and requires in-person withdrawal with a child-abuse records check for adults in the home.

ct:HB 5514.title: AN ACT CONCERNING VARIOUS REVISIONS TO THE PUBLIC HEALTH STATUTES.
ct:HB 5514.summary: Makes public health changes, including a working group on assisted living communities, written patient notice of medical records retention periods, and letting nonprofits give free eyeglasses to a person's authorized representative.

ct:HB 5567.title: AN ACT CONCERNING HEALTH CARE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTION FACILITIES.
ct:HB 5567.summary: Requires the Department of Correction to provide incarcerated people health care free of charge and in a timely way and to implement electronic health records, and requires the correction ombuds to hire a mental health clinician.

ct:SB 137.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE OFFICE OF EARLY CHILDHOOD.
ct:SB 137.summary: Adds a pediatrician to the Early Childhood Cabinet, raises Smart Start grant limits, requires youth camps to give contact information and receive emergency notifications, and expands background-check and child abuse registry notification rules for child care providers.

ct:SB 147.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A STUDY ON THE NEED FOR EXTENDED PRODUCER RESPONSIBILITY FOR ELECTRONIC NICOTINE DELIVERY SYSTEMS AND VAPOR PRODUCTS AND INCLUDING AEROSOL PAINTS UNDER THE PAINT STEWARDSHIP PROGRAM.
ct:SB 147.summary: Expands Connecticut's paint recycling program to include aerosol coating products and bans selling paint products from producers that do not join the program. Allows the environment department to charge the program operator an annual fee of up to $50,000.

ct:SB 191.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE PSYCHEDELIC-ASSISTED THERAPY PILOT PROGRAM.
ct:SB 191.summary: Opens the state psychedelic-assisted therapy pilot to Connecticut residents 18 or older meeting clinical criteria, rather than only veterans, retired first responders and health care workers, and removes the requirement to end it if the DEA approves MDMA and psilocybin.

ct:SB 196.title: AN ACT CONCERNING HOSPITAL SALE-LEASEBACK TRANSACTIONS AND ATTESTATIONS CONCERNING LACK OF A CONTROLLING INTEREST OF A HOSPITAL OR OF INTERFERENCE WITH THE PROFESSIONAL JUDGMENT AND CLINICAL DECISIONS OF CERTAIN HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS OF A HOSPITAL BY A PRIVATE EQUITY ENTITY.
ct:SB 196.summary: Bans hospital sale-leasebacks of main campus property starting July 1, 2027, and requires hospitals to attest annually to the Department of Public Health that no private equity entity controls them, with fines up to $2,000 for failing to attest.

ct:SB 220.title: AN ACT CONCERNING STUDENT LITERACY, ASPIRING EDUCATORS, AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE AS PART OF THE WORLD LANGUAGES CURRICULUM AND THE PARAEDUCATOR HEALTH BENEFIT PLAN SUBSIDY PROGRAM.
ct:SB 220.summary: Requires state reading-intervention guidance, opens the educator scholarship to "aspiring educators" from underrepresented groups with no alliance-district high school requirement, creates an American Sign Language education working group, and makes paraeducator health care subsidies permanent, adding charter schools.

ct:SB 268.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMPTROLLER TO WITHHOLD PAYMENT FOR VIOLATIONS OF THE PREVAILING WAGE STATUTES.
ct:SB 268.summary: Requires the comptroller, after a labor commissioner's prevailing-wage stop-work notice, to warn the contractor, and lets the comptroller withhold payment if it stays noncompliant 10 business days later, until the order is released, penalties are paid, or a settlement is final.

ct:SB 298.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE REALLOCATION OF CERTAIN STATE FUNDS AND VARIOUS PROVISIONS RELATING TO EDUCATION, PUBLIC SAFETY, GENERAL GOVERNMENT, ELECTIONS, INTERMEDIATE CARE FACILITIES AND WAREHOUSE DISTRIBUTION CENTERS.
ct:SB 298.summary: Reallocates state funds; creates a state Seal of Civics Education for diplomas; limits UConn Health neuromodulation center treatment to disabled veterans; bars active-assailant simulations in school crisis drills; creates a 15-member working group on antisemitism in schools.

ct:SB 306.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND COMPREHENSIVE ENERGY STRATEGY.
ct:SB 306.summary: Requires the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection commissioner to consult other state officials, including economic development, housing, transportation and the consumer counsel, when preparing the comprehensive energy strategy, and to send it to the Commerce Committee.

ct:SB 319.title: AN ACT CONCERNING BATTERY-POWERED LAWN EQUIPMENT FUNDING FOR MUNICIPALITIES, REGIONAL SCHOOLS AND COMMERCIAL LANDSCAPERS.
ct:SB 319.summary: Requires the Connecticut Green Bank to create loan products by January 31, 2028 to help commercial landscapers buy or lease battery-powered lawn equipment, and requires DEEP to reactivate a fund for municipalities and regional schools starting October 1, 2027.

ct:SB 342.title: AN ACT CONCERNING HEALTH COVERAGE.
ct:SB 342.summary: As amended, requires health carriers that use software or AI to automatically downcode or deny provider claims to send the provider electronic notice within ten days, with a clinical rationale; lets providers appeal within 60 days; requires annual reports to the Insurance Commissioner.

ct:SB 346.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE MODIFICATIONS TO THE GOVERNOR'S WORKFORCE COUNCIL.
ct:SB 346.summary: Raises the governor's business-representative appointments to the Governor's Workforce Council from 24 to 30, adds labor and vocational rehabilitation members, and caps the council at 62 members.

ct:SB 369.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING VARIOUS REQUIREMENTS REGARDING ELEVATORS.
ct:SB 369.summary: Requires owners of residential buildings with elevators to maintain them, give tenants advance notice of maintenance and of outages, and give local building officials repair plans; sets fines of up to $250 for a first violation and $500 for later ones.

ct:SB 423.title: AN ACT CONCERNING OVERSIGHT OVER HIGHER EDUCATION.
ct:SB 423.summary: Changes reporting on the community college consolidation, moving the annual report due date to August 1 and sending it to the Government Oversight Committee, and requires a December 31, 2026 report comparing state college system staffing levels in 2011, 2019 and 2026.

ct:SB 444.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING CERTAIN MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEES TO SERVE ON MUNICIPAL BOARDS OF FINANCE.
ct:SB 444.summary: Lets municipal employees serve on their town's board of finance if any stipend they receive is under $10,000 in a rolling 12-month period.

ct:SB 452.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE RELEASE OF LIGHTER-THAN-AIR BALLOONS.
ct:SB 452.summary: Bans knowingly releasing helium or other lighter-than-air balloons into the atmosphere, replacing the nine-balloon allowance, and from 2027 requires retailers to attach weights to balloons they sell, with a $20 civil penalty per violation.

ct:SB 457.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE STATE'S BOTTLE BILL.
ct:SB 457.summary: Sets misdemeanor or felony penalties, by volume from 5,000 containers, for willfully collecting refunds on containers not bought in Connecticut, and ends reduced redemption-center handling fees by July 1, 2027 or once scanning technology is used.

ct:SB 470.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE LEGISLATIVE COMMISSIONERS' RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TECHNICAL AND MINOR REVISIONS TO THE GOVERNMENT ADMINISTRATION STATUTES.
ct:SB 470.summary: Allows certain contracts of state higher-education units made or amended after passage, rather than after July 1, 2026, to include either the state nondiscrimination contract text or a nondiscrimination affirmation, and makes technical changes to government administration statutes.

ct:SB 478.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONSUMER SAFEGUARDS FOR LONG-TERM CARE POLICIES.
ct:SB 478.summary: Requires long-term care insurers and the Insurance Department to report annually on policy losses, and lets the insurance commissioner investigate and discipline insurers that violate long-term care insurance laws.

ct:SB 90.title: AN ACT REVISING AND CONSOLIDATING THE HATE CRIMES STATUTES.
ct:SB 90.summary: Combines Connecticut's bias-crime laws into one protected-category framework, labels bias-motivated offenses as hate crimes, extends persistent-offender status to them, and allows hate-crimes diversion programs for offenders.

de:HB 133.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FINES, FEES, RESTITUTION, AND OTHER COURT-RELATED MONETARY OBLIGATIONS.
de:HB 133.summary: Lets courts waive, suspend, or modify criminal fines and fees, including mandatory ones, and creates a hardship-waiver process. Defendants on public benefits or represented by the Office of Defense Services presumptively qualify; people already sentenced may apply later.

de:HB 141.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 11 AND 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FIREARMS.
de:HB 141.summary: Requires licensed firearm dealers, importers, and manufacturers to give buyers a state-published Firearm Responsibilities Notice and have them sign a form acknowledging receipt before a sale; dealers keep the signed forms at least three years.

de:HB 145.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO REVERSE LOCATION AND REVERSE KEYWORD SEARCHES AND COURT ORDERS.
de:HB 145.summary: Prohibits government entities from seeking, and courts from issuing, orders or requests identifying unnamed people who searched a keyword, except for certain listed serious felonies when the search returns five or fewer hits; unlawfully obtained evidence is inadmissible.

de:HB 150.title: AN ACT AMENDING TITLE 10 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CIVIL ARRESTS.
de:HB 150.summary: Bars civil (non-criminal) arrests of people going to, attending, or leaving courthouses and Industrial Accident Board hearing offices, unless a judicial order authorizes the arrest or officers give the judge or board advance written notice.

de:HB 188.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 15 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PRIMARY ELECTIONS.
de:HB 188.summary: As amended, allows registered voters unaffiliated with a political party to vote in a party primary of their choice starting January 1, 2028; their party-ballot choice becomes public record but does not change their registration.

de:HB 222.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 3 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT.
de:HB 222.summary: Raises the fine range for State Nutrient Management Program violations from $25-$1,000 to $125-$5,000 per violation.

de:HB 233.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LARGE ENERGY USE FACILITIES.
de:HB 233.summary: Requires Commission-regulated electric utilities to set a separate rate class for large energy-use facilities, with Commission-approved agreements, so costs of serving them are assigned to those facilities rather than other customers.

de:HB 300.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A TITLE IX COORDINATOR WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION.
de:HB 300.summary: Creates a Title IX Coordinator position in the Department of Education to train and assist schools, collect compliance data, maintain model policies, and support Title IX compliance in grades 6 through 12 athletics.

de:HB 310.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 30 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO BUSINESS TAX CREDITS AND DEDUCTIONS.
