de:HB 310.summary: As amended, excludes large energy-use facilities from the "qualified facility" definition for the employment and investment tax credit and license fee reduction, unless they produce or procure 100% of annual energy from clean generation in Delaware or nearby PJM zones.

de:HB 326.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THEFT BY IMPERSONATION OF A FAMILY MEMBER.
de:HB 326.summary: Creates the felony of theft by impersonating a victim's family member, graded by victim and amount stolen, from class F up to class B for $100,000 or more.

de:HB 332.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO KRATOM.
de:HB 332.summary: Bans selling, providing or marketing kratom products to anyone under 21 as a class B misdemeanor, and requires a report on kratom testing capabilities and retailer licensing by January 1, 2027.

de:HB 338.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO HEALTH CARRIER COVERAGE OF IMMUNIZATIONS AND PREVENTIVE SERVICES.
de:HB 338.summary: Ties the preventive services and immunizations that health insurers must cover without cost-sharing to task force, CDC immunization committee, and HRSA recommendations in effect on January 1, 2025, and removes language letting carriers drop coverage when recommendations change.

de:HB 344.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 15 AND 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CAMPAIGN FINANCE.
de:HB 344.summary: As amended, requires written documentation of loans to political committees, bars candidates from charging interest on loans to their own committees, extends record retention to five years, adds biennial training, and has the election commissioner refer alleged violations monthly to the Department of Justice's public trust division.

de:HB 347.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE UNIFORM PUBLIC SCHOOL REGISTRATION PROCESS.
de:HB 347.summary: Removes the requirement that parents provide a birth certificate to register a child for public school; other proof of age or birth date is accepted instead.

de:HB 348.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ELECTRIC VEHICLES.
de:HB 348.summary: Removes the $2,500 all-electric and $1,000 plug-in hybrid rebate caps and the $50,000 vehicle price limit from Delaware's electric vehicle rebate program, lets DNREC set rebates by household income and vehicle type, and adds businesses, nonprofits, and governments as eligible.

de:HB 355.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 10 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SEXUAL ASSAULT, HARASSMENT, AND DISCRIMINATION.
de:HB 355.summary: As amended, bars civil liability for communications about sexual assault, harassment or discrimination made without malice (knowing falsity or reckless disregard) by those who experienced or witnessed it, and says a prevailing defendant in a related suit may be awarded attorneys' fees and costs.

de:HB 356.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PFAS IN FIREFIGHTING FOAM AND EQUIPMENT.
de:HB 356.summary: Bars manufacturers from making, selling, or distributing Class B firefighting foam with intentionally added PFAS from January 1, 2028, with five-year exemptions for bulk petroleum facilities; requires recalls and sets civil penalties of up to $5,000, then $10,000.

de:HB 368.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT AND COOPERATION.
de:HB 368.summary: As amended, bars law enforcement from holding anyone solely on an immigration detainer or civil immigration warrant, except people convicted of a violent felony, registered sex offenders, people with 2 or more DUI convictions and domestic violence perpetrators; limits other civil immigration cooperation; requires annual reports.

de:HB 369.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF GUN VIOLENCE PREVENTION AND COMMUNITY SAFETY.
de:HB 369.summary: Establishes in state law the Office of Gun Violence Prevention and Community Safety within the Department of Safety and Homeland Security, created by a 2025 executive order, to coordinate state, county, and municipal efforts on gun violence and community safety.

de:HB 374.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LARGE PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACTS.
de:HB 374.summary: Requires the Office of Management and Budget to issue an annual report, due each February 1, on workers hired for state public works projects costing $3 million or more, including demographics, home zip code, union status, craft trade, and hours worked.

de:HB 376.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF MILLVILLE.
de:HB 376.summary: Reorganizes the Town of Millville charter into articles, removes provisions superseded by state law and the town's own assessment process, and adds a tie-breaker for municipal elections: a drawing by lot after three recounts.

de:HB 380.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 6 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PERSONAL DATA PRIVACY.
de:HB 380.summary: Lowers the Delaware Personal Data Privacy Act's coverage thresholds from 35,000 to 10,000 consumers (10,000 to 5,000 if over 20% of revenue comes from selling data), narrows financial-law exemptions to banks and insurers, and adds contract rules for third-party data sharing.

de:HB 383.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PAY FOR DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION EMPLOYEES.
de:HB 383.summary: Requires Department of Transportation employees in 20 listed job titles, such as Administrative Specialist and Engineering Technician, to be paid time-and-a-half after 37.5 hours a week, starting July 1, 2026.

de:HB 384.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO OPEN-END CONTRACTING FOR HIGHWAY CONSTRUCTION AND RECONSTRUCTION.
de:HB 384.summary: Raises the maximum length of Department of Transportation open-end highway construction contracts from three to five years and allows bid bonds of 10% and performance bonds of 100% of expected maximum work.

de:HB 388.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE LOSS OF DRIVERS' LICENSES DUE TO MEDICAL ISSUES.
de:HB 388.summary: Lets people disqualified from driving for a medical condition keep their physical driver's license for identification by signing an affidavit that they may not drive, instead of surrendering it.

de:HB 390.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION OF BIDS AND BID OPENINGS FOR ELECTRONIC BIDDING.
de:HB 390.summary: Lets state agencies choose electronic-only or combined bid submission on a platform of their choice, but paper bids must be accepted for some purchases under $500,000; requires posting results within two business days; drops newspaper ads when advertised on the electronic procurement system.

de:HB 404.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EXTENDED REALITY IN SCHOOLS PILOT PROGRAM.
de:HB 404.summary: As amended, creates a pilot program in which the Department of Education invites 6 to 12 schools to use artificial intelligence and extended reality products recommended by a committee, collects school data, and reports to the Governor and General Assembly by September 30, 2031.

de:HB 406.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES IN AUTOMOBILE INSURANCE.
de:HB 406.summary: Extends the existing ban on insurers requiring a particular facility, individual, or business for repair or replacement work as a condition of claim payment from auto glass work to all auto repair and replacement work.

de:HB 408.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO TRAFFICKING AN INDIVIDUAL, FORCED LABOR AND SEXUAL SERVITUDE.
de:HB 408.summary: Makes obtaining or purchasing a minor for commercial sexual activity an offense under Delaware's trafficking and sexual servitude statutes even when no third party is involved.

de:HB 409.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PROSTITUTION.
de:HB 409.summary: Adds operating, conducting, and advertising a prostitution business to the ways of promoting prostitution in the second degree, expressly covers illicit massage establishments, and defines them as establishments that facilitate prostitution under cover of a massage business.

de:HB 413.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO USE OF REVOLVING OR FLASHING GREEN LIGHT.
de:HB 413.summary: Extends the green revolving or flashing light allowance from state and municipal snow removal equipment to vehicles and equipment, including farm tractors and construction equipment, used for road or bridge work, traffic control, or emergency or inclement-weather operations.

de:HB 418.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FIREARMS.
de:HB 418.summary: Lets people who lawfully possessed unserialized firearms or unfinished frames or receivers before the Act keep them if, within six months, a licensed dealer or manufacturer serializes them or they are made permanently inoperable; defines "permanently inoperable."

de:HB 420.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO MASSAGE AND BODY WORK.
de:HB 420.summary: Lets massage and bodywork therapists complete pre-licensing education in a hybrid format as set by the Board, and removes references to certified massage technician licenses the Board no longer issues.

de:HB 423.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DEFERRED COMPENSATION.
de:HB 423.summary: Automatically enrolls newly hired state employees in the state's 457(b) deferred compensation plan at a predetermined percentage of pay, with an opt-out before deductions begin at 90 days and refunds available until 120 days after hire.

de:HB 424.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 RELATING TO AUTISM SURVEILLANCE AND REGISTRATION.
de:HB 424.summary: Repeals Delaware's autism surveillance and registration program, which requires health practitioners to report autism cases to the state or face a $100 fine per violation.

de:HB 425.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO EMPLOYEES AND SALARY SUPPLEMENTS.
de:HB 425.summary: Raises the salary supplement for nationally certified school counselors and nurses from 6% to 12%, adds school social workers, and lets the Department of Education identify additional eligible positions by regulation.

de:HB 426.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 30 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO STATE AID TO MUNICIPALITIES FOR STREETS.
de:HB 426.summary: Removes requirements that reports under the State Aid to Municipalities for Streets program be notarized and printed, allows electronic submission, and requires the annual report to also go to the Department of Transportation.

de:HB 427.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO OFFENSES INVOLVING DEADLY WEAPONS AND DANGEROUS INSTRUMENTS.
de:HB 427.summary: As amended, lets 16- and 17-year-olds possess BB guns, projectile weapons or firearms without direct adult supervision while target practicing or hunting if a parent permits it and they completed hunter education; hunting also requires a valid Delaware hunting license.

de:HB 429.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE STEP THERAPY EXCEPTION PROCESS.
de:HB 429.summary: Allows insurers, under the step therapy exception law, to require patients to try an interchangeable biological product or a biosimilar, as well as an AB-rated generic, before covering the brand-name drug.

de:HB 431.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 9 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO COMPOSTING.
de:HB 431.summary: As amended, requires counties to allow commercial composting of yard waste, food residuals and other organic materials on private properties zoned Agricultural Conservation, outside the growth zone, of 4 acres or more; counties may limit the area but must allow at least 5,000 square feet.

de:HB 437.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 4, TITLE 11, TITLE 14, TITLE 16, TITLE 18, TITLE 20, TITLE 21, TITLE 24, TITLE 25, TITLE 29, THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF DEWEY BEACH, THE CHARTER OF THE CITY OF HARRINGTON, THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF HOUSTON, THE CHARTER OF THE CITY OF MILFORD, AND THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF MILLSBORO RELATING TO TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS.
de:HB 437.summary: Makes technical corrections to the Delaware Code across many titles and to municipal charters, including changes identified by the Code Revisors and edits conforming to the Legislative Drafting Manual.

de:HB 439.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE SALE OF ELECTRIC MOPEDS AND ELECTRIC MOTORCYCLES.
de:HB 439.summary: Bars commercial sellers from advertising electric mopeds and motorcycles as electric bicycles, requires written disclosures about classification, power and registration, treats missing disclosures as unlawful, and bars mopeds from public pathways, bike lanes and sidewalks.

de:HB 444.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 15 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE JOHN LEWIS VOTING RIGHTS ACT.
de:HB 444.summary: As amended, establishes the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act, effective July 1, 2027, which directs that election laws be construed in favor of access to voting and allows challenges to election policies or practices that cause voter suppression or vote dilution affecting protected-class members.

de:HB 445.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 AND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LARGE ENERGY USE FACILITIES.
de:HB 445.summary: As amended, bars large energy-use facilities, including data centers, from operating unless they produce or procure 100% of annual energy from clean generation in Delaware or nearby PJM zones; a 10-year plan option allows phased compliance with curtailment and backup-power conditions.

de:HB 447.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CHILD CARE.
de:HB 447.summary: Directs the Interagency Resource Management Committee to coordinate planning, programs and funding for child care affordability, including voluntary cost-sharing partnerships among the state, employers, community sponsors and families.

de:HB 448.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 15 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CAMPAIGN EXPENDITURES.
de:HB 448.summary: Makes security expenses for a candidate's safety, such as home or office security systems and personal security, an authorized campaign expenditure, excluding firearms purchases, and requires the Commissioner to adopt rules within three months.

de:HB 452.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE INTERSCHOLASTIC ATHLETIC ASSOCIATION AND BACKGROUND CHECKS FOR CHILD-SERVING ENTITIES.
de:HB 452.summary: Requires Delaware Interscholastic Athletic Association regulations to mandate background checks for sports officials, diversity and anti-discrimination training for officials, annual sportsmanship and anti-harassment training for student athletes, and member-school cooperation with investigations.

de:HB 462.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SCHOOL TAXES.
de:HB 462.summary: Continues authority for non-vocational school districts in New Castle County to set separate residential and non-residential school tax rates, with the non-residential rate between 1 and 1.85 times the residential rate.

de:HB 465.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO VIRTUAL CURRENCY.
de:HB 465.summary: Adds virtual currency to the criminal code's money laundering definition and gives the state authority to return virtual currency to victims, with Superior Court disposing of funds that cannot be returned.

de:HB 475.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE NURSING ADVANCEMENT FUND.
de:HB 475.summary: Creates a Delaware Nursing Advancement Fund, financed by a $10 fee on Board of Nursing applications and renewals plus disciplinary fines, to fund a nonprofit studying and promoting the nursing workforce.

de:HB 476.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF FREDERICA.
de:HB 476.summary: Changes the Town of Frederica's charter to require at least one regular council meeting each month instead of two set meetings, and makes adopted ordinances take effect immediately unless a date is specified.

de:HB 59.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO RELEASE AND PUBLICATION OF THE NAME AND PHOTOGRAPH OF INDIVIDUALS CHARGED WITH CRIMES OR DELINQUENCY.
de:HB 59.summary: As amended, bars law enforcement from releasing or publishing the name or photograph of an adult charged with a crime unless the person is charged with a felony and release is necessary for public safety, extending the existing limit for juveniles; takes effect 90 days after enactment.

de:HB 63.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FIREWORKS.
de:HB 63.summary: Raises fireworks-law fines, requires retailers to get a State Fire Marshal permit for each sales location and period, requires wholesalers to hold a license, and requires warnings in fireworks ads and written safety notices at sale.

de:HB 84.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 19 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO EMPLOYER-SPONSORED MEETINGS OR COMMUNICATIONS.
de:HB 84.summary: Makes it an unlawful employment practice to penalize employees who decline employer meetings or communications about the employer's political or religious views, including on joining unions; exempts legally required or job-related communications and certain religious and political organizations.

de:HB 94.title: AN ACT AMENDING TITLES 10 AND 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LAW ENFORCEMENT COOPERATION IN FEDERAL IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT.
de:HB 94.summary: Bars state and local law-enforcement officers from directly participating with federal agencies in civil immigration enforcement at child-serving entities, colleges, places of worship, and health-care facilities unless an exigent circumstance exists, in which case a written report is due within 48 hours.

de:HJR 13.title: DIRECTING THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR TO STUDY THE CREATION OF A DELAWARE HEALTHCARE APPRENTICESHIP DEGREE PROGRAM AND TO REPORT FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS TO THE GOVERNOR AND THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY.
de:HJR 13.summary: Directs the Department of Labor, with Education and Health and Social Services, to study a healthcare apprenticeship degree program placing trainees in paid clinical jobs, and to report findings to the Governor and General Assembly.

de:SB 116.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 25 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO RIGHT OF REDEMPTION.
de:SB 116.summary: As amended, lets tenants facing eviction for unpaid rent stop it by paying all past-due rent, costs and fees before the eviction is carried out; not available after two possession judgments for unpaid rent within 18 months.

de:SB 161.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 16 AND 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH.
de:SB 161.summary: Establishes a statutory framework for licensing, oversight, enforcement, client rights, incident reporting and investigations of behavioral health treatment provider organizations, with licensing authority held by the Division of Substance Abuse and Mental Health.

de:SB 179.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE SENTENCING GUIDELINES AND ACCOUNTABILITY COMMISSION.
de:SB 179.summary: Repeals the Delaware Sentencing Accountability Commission's current statute and re-establishes it elsewhere in Title 11 with a modernized mission, set membership, defined powers and a required annual data report.

de:SB 189.title: ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO UNFAIR PRACTICES IN THE INSURANCE BUSINESS.
de:SB 189.summary: As amended, lets an injured person without an attorney rescind a motor vehicle accident injury release signed within 30 days of the accident, within 15 days, if they return any payment; requires such releases to carry notice of this right.

de:SB 211.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATED TO AGRICULTURE.
de:SB 211.summary: As amended, increases the Governor's Council on Agriculture from 7 to 9 members, requiring at least one livestock or poultry producer and one farmer aged 40 or younger.

de:SB 223.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE RETENTION OF PERSONNEL RECORDS.
de:SB 223.summary: Requires the Department of Education's regulations on personnel records to cover charter schools, and makes technical corrections to conform to the Legislative Drafting Manual.

de:SB 232.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CRIMINAL MISCHIEF.
de:SB 232.summary: As amended, makes criminal mischief a class F felony when someone intentionally damages an authorized emergency vehicle, causing $5,000 or more in losses and leaving the vehicle temporarily unable to respond to emergencies.

de:SB 233.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE REMOVAL OF ICE AND SNOW FROM VEHICLES.
de:SB 233.summary: Requires drivers to clear accumulated ice and snow from vehicles before operating them ($25 to $75 civil penalty), and sets civil penalties of $200 to $1,500 when ice or snow dislodging from a moving vehicle causes property damage or injury.

de:SB 249.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 AND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SUBSTANCE USE HARM REDUCTION.
de:SB 249.summary: Creates a regulatory framework with legal immunities for substance use harm reduction programs, changes the definition of drug paraphernalia, and decriminalizes paraphernalia possession by people who use drugs while keeping bans tied to manufacturing and distribution.

de:SB 255.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO TINTING OF MOTOR VEHICLE WINDSHIELD, WINDOWS, OR SIDE WINGS.
de:SB 255.summary: Lowers the minimum visible light transmission for front side window tint from 70% to 50%, states that rear side and rear windows have no minimum, and exempts vehicles operated by law-enforcement officers.

de:SB 26.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 19 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO UNEMPLOYMENT COMPENSATION.
de:SB 26.summary: Lets workers in a non-lockout labor dispute collect unemployment benefits after two weeks, with no wait if the employer breaches a contract or a wage, hours, or working-conditions law, or hires a permanent replacement.

de:SB 27.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE OFFICE OF NEW AMERICANS.
de:SB 27.summary: Establishes the Office of New Americans in the Department of State, led by a director the Secretary appoints, to coordinate information, services and policy recommendations for immigrants, and creates an advisory committee to the office.

de:SB 274.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 AND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DELAWARE MEDICAL ORDERS FOR SCOPE OF TREATMENT.
de:SB 274.summary: Renames the Delaware Medical Orders for Scope of Treatment as Delaware Portable Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST), keeps existing forms valid, and revises rules on completing the orders and patient representatives' authority.

de:SB 281.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 31 AND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO TECHNICAL UPDATES FOR THE DELAWARE HOSPITAL FOR THE CHRONICALLY ILL.
de:SB 281.summary: Renames the Delaware Hospital for the Chronically Ill the Eleanor Cain Center, removes terms such as "inmates" for residents, and updates the statute to reflect its operation as a skilled nursing facility.

de:SB 290.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PUBLIC BODIES.
de:SB 290.summary: Clarifies that quorum does not determine the identity of a public body, which instead depends on the governing document creating the body and the public business being conducted, for purposes of the Freedom of Information Act.

de:SB 297.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 6 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CONSUMER PROTECTION.
de:SB 297.summary: Clarifies that the Consumer Fraud Act's "in connection with" language covers unfair or deceptive acts and practices occurring before, during and after the sale, lease, receipt or advertisement of merchandise.

de:SB 300.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11, TITLE 16, AND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DEADLY WEAPONS DEALERS.
de:SB 300.summary: Requires firearm dealers to hold a state license, sets eligibility, security, recordkeeping, background check and training requirements for licensees, and adds State Police inspections, civil penalties and possible license revocation.

de:SB 305.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SPECIAL LICENSE PLATES.
de:SB 305.summary: Creates a special license plate for Delaware State University to support student access, academic excellence and university programs.

de:SB 308.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE LOAD FORECAST ACCOUNTABILITY ACT.
de:SB 308.summary: As amended, directs the Public Service Commission to investigate and review electric utilities' load forecasts submitted to PJM, coordinate with PJM and other states, access relevant materials, and report to the General Assembly each May 1.

de:SB 311.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 3 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO AGRICULTURE.
de:SB 311.summary: Changes Department of Agriculture licensing rules by requiring certified private pesticide applicators to keep records open to inspection, expanding the definition of landscaper, and removing a character-evidence requirement for grain inspector licenses.

de:SB 312.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 9, TITLE 22, AND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DATA CENTERS.
de:SB 312.summary: Prohibits state agencies, counties and municipalities from signing nondisclosure agreements that restrict public access to information about proposed or actual data centers using 100 megawatts of power or more.

de:SB 317.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 1 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO VETERANS MONTH.
de:SB 317.summary: Designates May as Veterans Month in Delaware.

de:SB 318.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SPECIAL LICENSE PLATES.
de:SB 318.summary: Discontinues the Delaware State Education Association centennial special license plate and replaces it with an updated association plate, while previously issued centennial plates remain valid.

de:SB 319.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18, TITLE 29, AND TITLE 31 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO COVERAGE FOR DIAGNOSTIC SERVICES AND TREATMENT FOR MENOPAUSE, PERIMENOPAUSE, AND MENOPAUSE AND PERIMENOPAUSE SYMPTOMS.
de:SB 319.summary: Requires individual, group and state employee health plans and Medicaid to cover medically necessary diagnosis and treatment for menopause and perimenopause, including FDA-approved hormone therapy, consultations, testing and non-hormonal treatments.

de:SB 320.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 AND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PHARMACY AND PHARMACISTS.
de:SB 320.summary: As amended, lets pharmacists prescribe over-the-counter products, opioid antagonists, and FDA-labeled drugs for minor, self-limiting or test-guided conditions, plus opioid use disorder medications under a standing order; bars prescribing other controlled substances.

de:SB 321.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATED TO UTILITY BILLING.
de:SB 321.summary: Requires electric utilities to offer consolidated billing for community energy subscriptions, netting subscription charges against bill credits and paying them to subscription coordinators; it is the default for new facilities, and older facilities may opt out.

de:SB 322.title: ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LOCAL SCHOOL TAXES.
de:SB 322.summary: Repeals school districts' ability to raise tax rates up to 10% after a reassessment, instead capping collections based on prior revenue and property growth, and lets districts raise referendum-approved taxes up to 2% a year without a referendum under conditions.

de:SB 328.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SCHOOL BUILDING SAFETY.
de:SB 328.summary: Requires the Department of Education to set the school facilities evaluation instrument through regulation rather than guidance, and clarifies that the hazardous materials repair standard includes lead.

de:SB 340.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LONG TERM CARE FACILITIES
de:SB 340.summary: As amended, requires nursing facilities, assisted living facilities and group homes for persons with mental illness (not state-run) to carry general and professional liability insurance of at least $1 million per claim and $3 million aggregate each, including abuse coverage, effective 180 days after enactment.

de:SB 341.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE HEALTH INFORMATION NETWORK.
de:SB 341.summary: Names the Delaware Health Information Network as the state's sanctioned health data utility provider, clarifies its authority to contract with organizations, and aligns its data uses for analytics and research with federal law.

de:SJR 18.title: DESIGNATING AUGUST 31, 2026, AS "INTERNATIONAL OVERDOSE AWARENESS DAY" IN THE STATE OF DELAWARE AND REQUIRING THE STATE FLAG TO BE FLOWN AT HALF-STAFF IN OBSERVANCE.
de:SJR 18.summary: Designates August 31, 2026 as International Overdose Awareness Day in Delaware and requires the state flag to be flown at half-staff that day.

de:SJR 20.title: DIRECTING THE DIVISION OF MEDICAID AND MEDICAL ASSISTANCE TO EVALUATE ASSESSMENTS FOR INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES.
de:SJR 20.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Social Services to evaluate using independent assessment tools and assessors to determine support needs for people eligible for home and community-based services, reporting by March 1, 2027.

fl:HB 1073.title: Public Education
fl:HB 1073.summary: Creates a District School Board Members' Bill of Rights giving members access to district documents (requests unrelated to a noticed meeting filled within 10 business days) and budget information, and bars districts from requiring or incentivizing employees to sign nondisclosure agreements.

fl:HB 1087.title: Pub. Rec./Office of Financial Regulation
fl:HB 1087.summary: Reenacts public records exemptions for virtual currency kiosk businesses, qualified stablecoin issuers, and gold and silver coin custodians, with updated public necessity statements.

fl:HB 1121.title: Aging and Disability Services
fl:HB 1121.summary: Revises state aging and disability services: sets a pre-enrollment list for long-term care, caps Area Agency on Aging chief executive pay at 150% of the Elderly Affairs secretary's, and changes guardian continuing-education and discipline rules.

fl:HB 1175.title: Safety Design Standards for Office Surgery Suites
fl:HB 1175.summary: Directs the Florida Building Commission and State Fire Marshal to adopt, by January 1, 2027, safety design standards for office surgery suites that let physicians treat up to six patients at once on an outpatient basis.

fl:HB 1329.title: Local Government Finances
fl:HB 1329.summary: Lengthens county and city budget website posting (tentative budgets 5 days before hearings instead of 2, final budgets 5 years instead of 2), requires budget reduction workshops, and sets new requirements for impact fee increases beyond phase-in limits.

fl:HB 1389.title: Affordable Housing
fl:HB 1389.summary: Extends Live Local Act affordable-housing zoning preemptions to land owned by counties, cities, or school districts and to religious-institution property over 3 acres with a worship house for 10 years, and bars setbacks or stepbacks that restrict project height.

fl:HB 145.title: Claims Against the Government
fl:HB 145.summary: Raises limits on state and local government payment of tort claims without further legislative action from $200,000 per person and $300,000 per incident to $350,000 and $500,000, and revises deadlines for some claims.

fl:HB 1451.title: Utility Services
fl:HB 1451.summary: Requires public meetings before municipal utilities approve out-of-city service agreements, ends the 25% surcharge on outside water and sewer customers (phased out by 2029 where bonds require), cuts the allowed rate gap from 50% to 25%, and preempts a 2025 Gainesville utility-authority charter amendment.

fl:HB 175.title: Payment Stablecoin
fl:HB 175.summary: Creates a licensing framework for state-qualified payment stablecoin issuers, modeled on the federal GENIUS Act, requiring a money services business license or a trust company certificate of approval from the Office of Financial Regulation, effective October 1, 2026.

fl:HB 177.title: Offices of Criminal Conflict and Civil Regional Counsel
fl:HB 177.summary: Lets a court appoint a different regional counsel office, before private counsel, to represent an indigent defendant in a death penalty case when the original regional counsel office has a conflict.

fl:HB 271.title: Foreign and Alien Bail Bond Insurers
fl:HB 271.summary: Requires foreign and alien bail bond insurers to report bail bond premiums to the Office of Insurance Regulation as domestic insurers do, with direct written premiums of at least 6.5% of the consideration received.

fl:HB 273.title: Special District Funding
fl:HB 273.summary: As passed by the House, adds certain special districts to state agreements allowing agencies to pay invoices for verified performance as due, and for downtown development districts requires voter approval of added territory, caps administrative costs at 10% of budget, and requires municipal approval of budgets.

fl:HB 397.title: Violations of Pretrial Release Conditions for Violent Crimes
fl:HB 397.summary: Makes it a first degree misdemeanor to willfully violate a no-contact pretrial release order when the arrest was for violent offenses such as murder, assault, stalking, or sexual battery; repeat violations are third degree felonies.

fl:HB 4005.title: City of Naples Airport Authority, Collier County
fl:HB 4005.summary: Changes the City of Naples Airport Authority from appointed to elected members: five seats (three city residents, two county residents outside the city) elected countywide starting in 2026, with candidates needing five years in financial management, small business or aerospace.

fl:HB 4027.title: Hillsborough County Public Schools, Hillsborough County
fl:HB 4027.summary: Provides for an elected, rather than appointed, Hillsborough County school superintendent, elected in a partisan election to four-year terms from 2028, subject to approval in a countywide referendum at the 2026 general election.

fl:HB 4041.title: Compensation for Health Care Services for Inmates in Indian River County
fl:HB 4041.summary: Caps payments to providers without county contracts for treating Indian River County jail inmates at 110 percent of the Medicare rate (125 percent for some with negative operating margins), sets trauma-center payment for trauma-alert inmates at 175 percent, and caps ambulance payments at 110 percent.

fl:HB 4051.title: Pace Fire Rescue District, Santa Rosa County
fl:HB 4051.summary: Bars the Pace Fire Rescue District from levying non-ad valorem assessments on tax-exempt churches and religious institutions, bases commercial and industrial assessments on total parcel square footage, and revises the maximum residential, commercial and industrial assessment rates.

fl:HB 4055.title: City of Lake Wales, Polk County
fl:HB 4055.summary: Lets alcohol vendors licensed for on-premises consumption in Lake Wales' Arts, Culture and Entertainment District allow patrons to carry open containers out and drink within the district.

fl:HB 4059.title: Compensation for Health Care Services for Inmates in Polk County
fl:HB 4059.summary: Caps payments to health care providers without county contracts for treating Polk County jail inmates at 110 percent of the Medicare rate (125 percent for some with negative operating margins), and caps ambulance payments at 110 percent.

fl:HB 4061.title: Hillsborough County
fl:HB 4061.summary: Creates the Land Reserve Stewardship District, an independent special district of about 3,707 acres in Hillsborough County with a five-member board that can issue bonds and levy special assessments; the board starts under landowner control.

fl:HB 4105.title: Port St. Joe Port Authority, Franklin, Gadsden, Gulf, and Liberty Counties
fl:HB 4105.summary: Expands the Port St. Joe Port Authority, now covering Gulf County, to include Franklin, Gadsden and Liberty Counties, with a six-member governor-appointed board (a Port St. Joe chair, two Gulf County members, one from each other county) serving four-year terms.

fl:HB 429.title: Criteria for Determining Criminal Gang Membership
fl:HB 429.summary: Changes the criteria for identifying a criminal gang member, including admission in person or online, being claimed by a gang, being identified by a parent, guardian, or spouse living with the person, and using defined gang-related language online; effective October 1, 2026.

fl:HB 491.title: Faith-based Content in Batterers' Intervention Programs
fl:HB 491.summary: Allows batterers' intervention programs to offer supplemental faith-based activities, while prohibiting programs from requiring participation in them.

fl:HB 5001E.title: General Appropriations Act
fl:HB 5001E.summary: Appropriates money for state agency operations, capital outlay and other purposes for the fiscal year July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, plus supplemental appropriations for the period ending June 30, 2026.

fl:HB 5003E.title: Implementing the 2026-2027 General Appropriations Act
fl:HB 5003E.summary: Implements the 2026-27 General Appropriations Act by revising education funding calculations, authorizing agencies to submit budget amendments, making many provisions expire July 1, 2027, and requiring the Department of Financial Services to replace the FLAIR state accounting system.

fl:HB 5201E.title: Collective Bargaining
fl:HB 5201E.summary: Provides that 2026-27 collective bargaining issues at impasse between the state and certified representatives of state employee bargaining units are resolved under instructions in the General Appropriations Act and its implementing legislation.

fl:HB 5203E.title: Government Administration
fl:HB 5203E.summary: Creates the Florida Accountability Office within the Legislature, including a division that handles complaints and investigates appropriations projects; revises Auditor General duties, audit procedures, whistle-blower provisions, and budget transfer and amendment rules.

fl:HB 5207E.title: Department of Management Services
fl:HB 5207E.summary: Charges state agencies a monthly health insurance assessment for each vacant position, repeals minority business enterprise certification, renames the Office of Supplier Diversity the Office of Supplier Development, changes state employee prescription drug rules, and sets Legislature space rules in the Capitol Complex.

fl:HB 5501E.title: Documentary Stamp Tax Distributions
fl:HB 5501E.summary: Raises the cap on documentary stamp tax proceeds credited to the State Transportation Trust Fund from $360.08 million to $420.08 million, adds a 14 percent Florida Rail Enterprise share, lowers other program shares, and bars South Florida Regional Transportation Authority funding from rail enterprise money.

fl:HB 5601E.title: Higher Education
fl:HB 5601E.summary: Transfers University of South Florida Sarasota/Manatee campus property and related liabilities to New College of Florida, lets university boards of trustees set out-of-state fees for nonresident students, and removes the nonresident undergraduate block tuition requirement.

fl:HB 6515.title: Relief/Lourdes Latour and Edward Latour/Miami-Dade County
fl:HB 6515.summary: Directs Miami-Dade County to pay $500,000 to Lourdes and Edward Latour under a settlement of a negligence claim, with attorney fees limited to 25% of the award.

fl:HB 7031.title: Internal Revenue Code
fl:HB 7031.summary: As passed by the House, updates corporate income tax to the federal code as of 2026 with listed exceptions, requires vacation rental advertising platforms to collect taxes, adds sales tax exemptions for home hardening products, firearm accessories, and hunting, fishing, and camping goods, and lowers slot machine and cardroom taxes.

fl:HB 7031E.title: Taxation
fl:HB 7031E.summary: Changes Florida taxes, including requiring vacation rental advertising platforms to collect and remit taxes, a refund-based sales tax exemption for home-hardening products, lower slot machine and cardroom tax rates, estimated property taxes on online home listings from February 2027, and new tax credits.

fl:HB 757.title: School Safety
fl:HB 757.summary: Lets employees and faculty at public postsecondary institutions serve as armed school guardians, requires those institutions to have threat management teams, risk assessments, and active-assailant plans, and makes discharging a firearm within 1,000 feet of a school during school hours a second-degree felony, with exceptions.

fl:HB 867.title: Dry Needling by Occupational Therapists
fl:HB 867.summary: Authorizes occupational therapists to perform dry needling and requires the licensing board to set standards, including two years of practice, 50 hours of training, patient consent, and no delegation to others.

fl:HB 925.title: Clerks of the Court
fl:HB 925.summary: Lets court clerks keep all revenue collected above the state's projection instead of 50%, keep 10% of school-bus stop-signal civil penalties and more municipal traffic fees, and publish real-property legal notices on a website.

fl:HJR 1F.title: Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes
fl:HJR 1F.summary: Adds to the proposed constitutional amendment a requirement that the Legislature give local governments any funds needed for public safety services, including law enforcement, fire, emergency medical services, and corrections, if the amendment leaves a local government unable to fully fund them.

fl:SB 1028.title: Citizens Property Insurance Corporation
fl:SB 1028.summary: Requires Citizens Property Insurance Corporation to create, by January 1, 2027, two clearinghouses diverting commercial applicants and policyholders to authorized or surplus lines insurers; risks receiving comparable offers become ineligible for Citizens coverage.

fl:SB 1074.title: One-cent Piece
fl:SB 1074.summary: Allows sales tax dealers to round cash transactions to the nearest nickel if the penny is no longer produced, without changing the sales price or tax collected.

fl:SB 124.title: Florida Virtual School
fl:SB 124.summary: Removes priority course access for certain Florida Virtual School students, lets the school contract with public and private entities, and requires most of its employees to be state employees for retirement-system purposes.

fl:SB 1332.title: Career Offender Registration
fl:SB 1332.summary: Changes the Florida Career Offender Registration Act to align with sexual offender rules, requiring in-person registration within 48 hours of release, more reported information, and reporting address and vehicle changes within 48 hours.

fl:SB 14.title: Relief of Jose Correa by Miami-Dade County
fl:SB 14.summary: Directs Miami-Dade County to pay Jose Correa $4.1 million for injuries from a county bus driver's negligence, with attorney and lobbying fees capped at 25% of the award.

fl:SB 1434.title: Infill Redevelopment
fl:SB 1434.summary: Creates the Infill Redevelopment Act, requiring administrative approval of housing on contaminated or brownfield parcels of at least 5 acres in counties over 1.475 million people, at up to 25 units per acre or the area's average zoning density if lower, with a 20-foot buffer.

fl:SB 1568.title: Use of Digital Currency by the Department of Financial Services
fl:SB 1568.summary: Creates a voluntary pilot program letting the Department of Financial Services accept designated payment stablecoins for government fees and convert them to U.S. currency, with any yield credited to the state.

fl:SB 1602.title: Housing for Veterans
fl:SB 1602.summary: Creates a pilot program in Broward, Escambia, Hillsborough, and Santa Rosa counties funding landlords who hold vacant units for veterans for up to 45 days.

fl:SB 1668.title: Florida Birth-Related Neurological Injury Compensation Association
fl:SB 1668.summary: Revises the Florida Birth-Related Neurological Injury Compensation Association: puts dental, guardianship legal-cost, and expanded family mental-health benefits into law, requires participants to obtain health coverage, and lets the plan pay premiums and out-of-pocket costs.

fl:SB 394.title: Reinsurance Intermediary Managers
fl:SB 394.summary: Exempts from reinsurance intermediary manager licensing an underwriting manager of facultative risks when that business is under 10% of the reinsurer's assumed annual gross written premium.

fl:SB 436.title: Felony Battery
fl:SB 436.summary: Adds resisting an officer with violence to the prior offenses that can make a misdemeanor battery a felony, and adds battery on a law enforcement officer causing injury to the prison releasee reoffender offense list.

fl:SB 538.title: Extracurricular Activities
fl:SB 538.summary: Lets home-schooled students, and students whose school lacks an activity, join that activity at a school in their district, charging non-enrolled students the greater of the enrolled fee or a cost-based fee up to $400, and changes athletic transfer eligibility.

fl:SB 688.title: Naturopathic Medicine
fl:SB 688.summary: Reestablishes licensing of naturopathic doctors, creating a Board of Naturopathic Medicine, licensure by exam or endorsement, and a scope of practice that generally excludes prescribing legend drugs; telehealth is allowed.

fl:SB 7002.title: OGSR/Department of Military Affairs/United States Department of Defense
fl:SB 7002.summary: Delays from October 2, 2026, to October 2, 2031, the repeal of a public records exemption for certain Department of Military Affairs records tied to Department of Defense systems.

fl:SB 7008.title: OGSR/Florida Gaming Control Commission
fl:SB 7008.summary: Extends the Florida Gaming Control Commission's public meeting and records exemptions for closed portions of meetings discussing confidential information, which would otherwise expire October 2, 2026.

fl:SB 7014.title: OGSR/Social Media Platform Investigations
fl:SB 7014.summary: Delays from October 2, 2026, to October 2, 2031, the repeal of two public records exemptions for investigations into social media platforms.

fl:SB 7022.title: Public Records/Examination and Assessment Instruments
fl:SB 7022.summary: Extends the public records exemption for exam and assessment instruments to public schools, school boards, and the education boards, and allows sharing among covered agencies.

fl:SB 7024.title: OGSR/Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Operational Technology Information
fl:SB 7024.summary: Consolidates agency-specific cybersecurity public records and meeting exemptions into the general agency cybersecurity exemption, covering all state and local agencies.

fl:SB 7040.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund/Executive Office of the Governor
fl:SB 7040.summary: Re-creates the Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund in the Governor's office through July 1, 2028, bars using it to buy aircraft, boats, or motor vehicles, holds federal reimbursements in a separate account, and adds cash-balance and cash-flow reporting.

fl:SB 800.title: Engineering
fl:SB 800.summary: Sets escalating fines for repeat unlicensed practice of engineering: $10,000 for a second violation, $15,000 third, $20,000 fourth, and $25,000 for fifth and later.

fl:SB 820.title: Problem-solving Court Reports
fl:SB 820.summary: Requires the state courts administrator's annual problem-solving court report to include added data such as treatment compliance and program completion.

fl:SB 824.title: School District Unimproved Real Property
fl:SB 824.summary: Requires school districts to annually submit to the Department of Education an inventory of all unimproved real property they own, with details such as location, acreage, acquisition date, and current use.

fl:SB 962.title: Affordable Housing
fl:SB 962.summary: Excludes farms and farm operations, including on-site sale of their products, from the commercial, industrial, or mixed-use zoning definitions that trigger required local approval of affordable housing developments under the Live Local Act.

fl:SJR 2F.title: Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes
fl:SJR 2F.summary: Amends the proposed property tax constitutional amendment to take effect January 1, 2027 and expire December 31, 2031, after which Article VII, sections 4, 6 and 9 revert to their December 31, 2026 text, preserving other adopted amendments.

hi:HB 1618.title: RELATING TO CESSPOOL CONVERSIONS.
hi:HB 1618.summary: Creates a cesspool conversion revolving loan fund; the Hawaii Green Infrastructure Authority offers low-interest or forgivable loans to eligible households to upgrade cesspools or connect to sewers, with funding the health department may provide from the water pollution control revolving fund.

hi:HB 1740.title: RELATING TO THE HAWAII HOUSING FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION.
hi:HB 1740.summary: Removes the income and ability-to-pay tests for qualified residents of Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corporation projects, lets them own a majority interest in one dwelling property if disposed of within two years, and revises exemptions for certain corporation-developed projects.

hi:HB 1741.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
hi:HB 1741.summary: Treats county inclusionary housing mandates as impact fees and, from July 1, 2029, requires an approved needs assessment study before a county adopts or changes one. Mandates above 10% of units also need nexus findings and a financial feasibility determination.

hi:HB 1753.title: RELATING TO SOCIAL MEDIA.
hi:HB 1753.summary: Requires social media platforms with one million or more monthly users nationwide or $25 million or more in annual revenue to let Hawaii users delete accounts, delete their personal information within 90 days, and not obstruct deletion.

hi:HB 1961.title: RELATING TO HEALTH CARE.
hi:HB 1961.summary: Makes it unlawful to obstruct access to a health care facility, make repeated calls to impede its phone lines, or threaten injury to its staff or patients; sets petty misdemeanor penalties (first offense: at least $250 fine and 24 hours jail); allows civil suits.

hi:HB 1969.title: RELATING TO COLORECTAL CANCER.
hi:HB 1969.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to fund colorectal cancer screenings, as appropriated, for uninsured residents, residents with cost-sharing coverage, and certain noncitizens ineligible for Medicaid; requires insurers to cover follow-up colonoscopies after positive tests without cost sharing.

hi:HB 2021.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
hi:HB 2021.summary: Bars exhibition riding such as wheelies and stunts on electric bicycles on public streets, bars high-speed electric devices (motor over 750 watts and capable of over 28 mph) from public roads and areas, and requires e-bike labels, point-of-sale signs and written legality disclosures.

hi:HB 2023.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
hi:HB 2023.summary: Directs the transportation director to certify speed-limiting devices (active intelligent speed assistance systems) and select one installer; makes tampering a misdemeanor; requires installation during license suspension or revocation for excessive speeding and repeat high-speed racing, which courts may extend.

hi:HB 2344.title: RELATING TO SCHOOL FACILITIES.
hi:HB 2344.summary: Creates a temporary nine-member commission to recommend public school consolidations, realignments or closures; the governor, then the legislature in 2028, approves or disapproves the whole report, and approved recommendations are implemented by the education board and department.

hi:HB 2385.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
hi:HB 2385.summary: Transfers approval of general excise tax exemptions for housing projects under county assistance programs from the counties to the Hawaii housing finance and development corporation starting January 1, 2027; at least half the units must serve households at or below 100% of median income.

hi:SB 2169.title: RELATING TO THE AGRIBUSINESS DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION.
hi:SB 2169.summary: Allows the Agribusiness Development Corporation to acquire real property by condemnation for its immediate or future use if it determines the property is necessary, excluding public lands.

hi:SB 2401.title: RELATING TO REGIONAL SHORELINE MITIGATION DISTRICTS.
hi:SB 2401.summary: Directs the Office of Planning and Sustainable Development to identify regional shoreline mitigation districts and coordinate communities, property owners and agencies on shoreline adaptation pathways plans, which the Board of Land and Natural Resources may adopt.

hi:SB 2544.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
hi:SB 2544.summary: Creates a five-year Hawaii Builds pilot program in the housing finance corporation, letting it spend up to $20 million a year from the dwelling unit revolving fund on predevelopment and construction equity for housing projects, with expedited agency review.

hi:SB 2568.title: RELATING TO OFFENSES AGAINST PUBLIC SERVANTS.
hi:SB 2568.summary: Raises harassment from a petty misdemeanor to a misdemeanor when committed against a public servant, defined to include officials, judges and any federal, state or county employee, because of or while the servant performs official duties.

hi:SB 2599.title: RELATING TO DEVELOPMENT.
hi:SB 2599.summary: Redesignates the stadium development district as the Halawa community development district, makes the Hawaii Community Development Authority its zoning and entitlement agency, and creates a special fund for district revenues and assessments.

hi:SB 2721.title: RELATING TO THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE.
hi:SB 2721.summary: Amends various chapters of the Hawaii Penal Code and related statutes to carry out the recommendations of the Judicial Council's 2025 advisory committee on penal code review; takes effect September 1, 2026.

hi:SB 3253.title: RELATING TO CONSERVATION.
hi:SB 3253.summary: Recognizes a nonprofit as the State of Hawaii Conservation Sanctuary to run endangered-species and wildlife sanctuaries, with power to operate for-profit enterprises, hold or lease property, and operate in agricultural districts; exempts state funds it receives from chapter 42F standards.

ia:HF 1028.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the department of management, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:HF 1028.summary: Raises from 50 to 100 percent the yearly cap on interdepartmental transfers into a non-entitlement appropriation, directs Technology Reinvestment Fund spending to Department of Management information technology projects, and sets required and prohibited terms in state IT contracts.

ia:HF 2200.title: A bill for an act relating to activities in the administration of alcoholic beverage control by the department of revenue, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2200.summary: As introduced, broadens the alcohol-industry interests that no more than two commission members may hold, bars members from using their office to promote political views or candidates, and bars revenue employees from licensing or enforcing alcohol laws against businesses they have an ownership interest in.

ia:HF 2254.title: A bill for an act relating to the prohibition of noncompete clauses in certain employment contracts entered into by the university of Iowa hospitals and clinics, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2254.summary: Directs the Board of Regents to develop a policy barring University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics from including noncompete clauses in employment contracts with physicians, advanced nurse practitioners, licensed practical nurses, pharmacists, physician assistants, and registered nurses.

ia:HF 2297.title: A bill for an act relating to radon mitigation in residential buildings.
ia:HF 2297.summary: Requires the state building code to require a passive radon mitigation method listed in the 2021 International Residential Code in new single-family and two-family homes built after the requirement is adopted.

ia:HF 2329.title: A bill for an act relating to interest rates and charges on regulated loans, and consumer credit transaction service charges.
ia:HF 2329.summary: Sets the maximum rate on regulated loans at 3 percent per month, ends the banking superintendent's authority to change rates, and changes the consumer credit service charge cap from the lesser of 10 percent or $30 to the lesser of 3 percent or $100.

ia:HF 2337.title: A bill for an act relating to fraudulent practices involving academic credentials or professional or occupational licenses, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2337.summary: Makes falsely claiming an academic degree or credentials to get a job or other personal gain a simple misdemeanor, and falsely claiming a license regulated under Iowa Code chapter 272C an aggravated misdemeanor.

ia:HF 2490.title: A bill for an act relating to public meetings and records, including public notice requirements for meetings of a governmental body, supervision and fees associated with examining and copying public records, employment separation information for certain government employees, contractors, or appointees, and injunctions to restrain vexatious requesters.
ia:HF 2490.summary: As introduced, requires governmental bodies to give meeting notice by posting it prominently and on any associated website, and to mark amended agendas "AMENDED" and issue a new notice.

ia:HF 2493.title: A bill for an act relating to the statewide preschool program by modifying provisions relating to eligibility, funding, and compulsory attendance and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2493.summary: As introduced, extends the state preschool program and its funding to five-year-olds who turn five between March 15 and September 15, starting with school budget years beginning July 1, 2027.

ia:HF 2501.title: A bill for an act relating to the conduct of elections.
ia:HF 2501.summary: Requires agencies investigating election misconduct to notify the State Commissioner of Elections, cancels voter registrations left incomplete, pending, or unconfirmed for 90 days without resolution, ends voter attestation of another voter's identity, and changes public measure recount rules.

ia:HF 2514.title: A bill for an act making children of child care workers in this state eligible for the state child care assistance program.
ia:HF 2514.summary: As passed by the House, makes children of child care workers eligible for state child care assistance if the parent works an average of 32 hours weekly providing child care at a participating facility and does not own it; copayments set by rule.

ia:HF 2531.title: A bill for an act relating to interests in minerals owned by counties and cities, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2531.summary: Requires counties and cities to convey mineral interests they own to the surface owner within five years, except on land they own outright, and requires counties to convey delinquent-tax mineral interests if the owner does not pay within 90 days of notice.

ia:HF 2542.title: A bill for an act relating to habitual offenders, and providing penalties.
ia:HF 2542.summary: Raises the minimum prison term for habitual offenders (class C or D felony after two prior felonies) from three to seven years, bars earned time from reducing it, raises the maximum from 15 to 20 years, and bars deferred or suspended sentences.

ia:HF 2602.title: A bill for an act relating to the licensure of massage establishments, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2602.summary: Requires massage therapy establishments, other than sole practitioners and certain exempt locations, to hold a Board of Massage Therapy license starting January 1, 2027, with possible inspections and fingerprint background checks.

ia:HF 2615.title: A bill for an act relating to thoroughbred and quarter horse racing seasons.
ia:HF 2615.summary: As introduced, requires thoroughbred and quarter horse racing seasons to be separate, non-overlapping meets, unless the breed associations and the Polk County track licensee agree in writing to mixed meets.

ia:HF 2617.title: A bill for an act relating to abandoned vehicles.
ia:HF 2617.summary: As passed by the House, rewrites Iowa's abandoned-vehicle law: sets who may tow and impound, requires notice to owners within ten days giving 20 days to reclaim the vehicle or retrieve belongings, and sets rules for selling unclaimed vehicles and distributing proceeds.

ia:HF 2635.title: A bill for an act relating to health carriers standards of conduct; utilization review organizations, artificial intelligence, audits, and prior authorizations; certificate of need processes; and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2635.summary: As passed by the House, sets audit deadlines for health insurers' utilization review, bars carrier penalties for out-of-network referrals, requires qualified reviewers for prior authorization denials, exempts some cancer screenings from prior authorization, and raises certificate-of-need dollar thresholds.

ia:HF 2667.title: A bill for an act relating to project design standards and specifications, including by providing for a statewide urban design and specifications board and requiring certain reports to city councils regarding noncompliant projects.
ia:HF 2667.summary: As passed by the House, creates a statewide urban design and specifications board to publish design and specifications manuals, and requires a cost report to the city council before it approves a city street project that does not match Department of Transportation standards.

ia:HF 2670.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to summative testing in schools and the educational program provided to students enrolled in kindergarten through grade twelve, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2670.summary: Requires a social studies assessment in grades 8 and 11 starting in 2027-2028, moves the grade 10 science assessment to grade 11, has the state board set social studies core indicators, and requires summative tests to align with Iowa standards.

ia:HF 2676.title: A bill for an act relating to health-related matters, including health-related professions, nutrition, medication, and education, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2676.summary: Requires nutrition continuing education for some physicians and physician assistants and nutrition coursework in medical school, bars certain ingredients in school meals from 2027, limits kindergarten-through-grade-5 digital instruction to 60 minutes daily, and allows over-the-counter ivermectin.

ia:HF 2694.title: A bill for an act relating to the regulation of certain places and activities by the governor.
ia:HF 2694.summary: As passed by the House, bars the governor from closing or regulating places or practices of worship; bars disaster-emergency measures that change election rules without legislative approval, regulate conduct in private residences or require vaccination; and bars requiring private businesses to close in public health disasters.

ia:HF 2706.title: A bill for an act relating to judicial officers, including magistrate appointments in judicial election districts, senior magistrates, and judicial officer compensation, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2706.summary: Changes judicial officer rules, including appointing magistrates by judicial election district instead of by county, and addressing senior magistrates and judicial officer compensation.

ia:HF 2707.title: A bill for an act relating to alignment of delivery of health and human services programs and services, aging and disability services, and volunteer services, and including applicability and effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2707.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to divide the state into districts, initially matching the existing behavioral health districts, and changes behavioral health, aging and disability, and volunteer guardian and conservator services.

ia:HF 2724.title: A bill for an act requiring the board of educational examiners to establish additional endorsements and authorizations.
ia:HF 2724.summary: As passed by the House, requires the board of educational examiners to adopt fine arts, math and science teaching endorsements requiring a bachelor's degree, an instructional strategist II endorsement without a master's requirement, and an activities administration authorization.

ia:HF 2757.title: A bill for an act relating to nuclear electric generation facilities by creating sales and use tax exemptions and refunds, making appropriations to the state board of regents for establishing and maintaining a nuclear energy workforce, making penalties applicable, and including applicability and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2757.summary: Exempts property and services used to build, expand, repair, or restart nuclear power plants from sales and use tax until commercial operation, if the facility pays $2,200 per megawatt of capacity annually, up to four years, into a Board of Regents nuclear workforce fund.

ia:HF 2766.title: A bill for an act relating to captive insurance companies and life captive reinsurance companies, and including civil penalties.
ia:HF 2766.summary: Makes gross premiums tax returns of insurance and captive insurance companies confidential, with a serious misdemeanor for state employees who publish them, and changes rules for captive insurance and life captive reinsurance companies.

ia:HF 2768.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations for state government administration and regulation, including the department of administrative services, auditor of state, ethics and campaign disclosure board, offices of governor and lieutenant governor, department of inspections, appeals, and licensing, department of insurance and financial services, department of management, Iowa public employees’ retirement system, public information board, department of revenue, secretary of state, treasurer of state, and utilities commission.
ia:HF 2768.summary: Appropriates state money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to general government agencies, including the auditor, governor's office, revenue, insurance, secretary of state, treasurer, and utilities commission, and redirects some fee deposits to the Licensing and Regulation Fund.

ia:HF 2770.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations to the justice system, providing fees, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2770.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to the departments of justice, corrections, public safety and public defense and other justice agencies, raises state-paid appointed counsel pay by $4 per hour from July 1, 2026, and creates an attorney loan repayment program.

ia:HF 2771.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations involving state government entities associated with agriculture, natural resources, and environmental protection, and including contingent effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2771.summary: Appropriates state money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to the departments of agriculture and natural resources, the Iowa Finance Authority, and Iowa State University and the University of Iowa, and makes Iowa Code changes.

ia:HF 2779.title: A bill for an act relating to authorizations to conduct advance deposit wagering.
ia:HF 2779.summary: Requires the racing and gaming commission to authorize entities meeting simulcasting licensure rules, instead of the Polk County racetrack licensee, to run advance deposit wagering, and bars phone or electronic wagers within five miles of a racetrack without the track's agreement.

ia:HF 2780.title: A bill for an act relating to alcoholic beverage control by providing for certificates of compliance and the issuance of class “A” wine permits to nonnative wine manufacturers, permitting cities to create social districts for the consumption of alcoholic beverages, and providing fees.
ia:HF 2780.summary: Changes alcohol permit rules by removing the distiller's certificate requirement for some brand resellers, allowing class A wine permits for nonnative wine makers, and letting cities create social districts for drinking alcohol in certain public places.

ia:HF 2781.title: A bill for an act relating to allocations of moneys from the juvenile detention home fund.
ia:HF 2781.summary: Changes how the juvenile detention home fund is divided, giving each home $150,000 first and sharing the rest based on each home's share of the prior year's costs.

ia:HF 2785.title: A bill for an act extending the biodiesel blended fuel tax credit.
ia:HF 2785.summary: Extends the repeal date of the biodiesel blended fuel promotion tax credit for retail dealers, for individual and corporate income taxes, from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2033.

ia:HF 2786.title: A bill for an act modifying the sales or use tax refund for biodiesel production.
ia:HF 2786.summary: Raises the sales or use tax refund for biodiesel producers from 4 to 5 cents per gallon produced in Iowa and moves the refund's repeal date from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2031.

ia:HF 2787.title: A bill for an act prohibiting warrant resolution clinics, including enforcement mechanisms, providing penalties, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2787.summary: Bans warrant resolution clinics, advertised events letting people with outstanding arrest warrants resolve them without immediate arrest, and bars public funds or facilities for them; knowing violations are simple misdemeanors, with civil penalties up to $10,000 for private organizers.

ia:HF 2799.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the economic development authority, the utilities commission, and the department of education, including creation of the headquarters expansion and development for growth and employment program, and the business incentives for growth program training fund; repeal of the new jobs tax credit program; the major economic growth attraction program; load forecasting and analysis of electric transmission system expansion plans; creation of the electric transmission system expansion planning and analysis and load forecasting fund; the industrial new jobs training program; and establishing the new jobs training program interim study committee; and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2799.summary: Creates the EDGE headquarters tax incentive program and a training fund, repeals the New Jobs Tax Credit, has the economic development authority commission an Iowa State University electricity load forecast every two years, and changes industrial new jobs training.

ia:HF 2801.title: A bill for an act modifying the major economic growth attraction program, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2801.summary: Lets the economic development authority award either a tax credit of up to 5 percent of qualifying investment to up to two businesses, or up to 10 percent, paid over 10 years, to one business in a rural county.

ia:HF 523.title: A bill for an act relating to the ability of peace officers to file a petition for emergency protective orders on behalf of persons seeking relief from domestic abuse.
ia:HF 523.summary: As introduced, lets a peace officer file a petition for a 72-hour emergency protective order for a person who says they are in present danger of domestic abuse and asks the officer to file it.

ia:HF 571.title: A bill for an act relating to protections for medical practitioners and health care institutions, including those related to the exercise of conscience, whistleblower activities, and free speech, and providing penalties.
ia:HF 571.summary: Allows medical practitioners and health care institutions to refuse to participate in or pay for health care services that violate their conscience, bars discrimination for refusing, bars retaliation for whistleblowing, and limits licensing penalties for protected speech.

ia:HF 703.title: A bill for an act concerning information regarding certain state and federal student loan programs.
ia:HF 703.summary: Requires the Iowa College Aid Bureau to compare estimated rates on federal Direct PLUS loans with state college family and partnership loans, publish a statement if the state loans may be lower, and notify Iowa colleges, which must include it in aid offers.

ia:HF 766.title: A bill for an act relating to motor vehicle window tint, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 766.summary: As introduced, bars driving with front windshields under 70 percent light transmittance or side windows beside or ahead of the driver under 50 percent, replacing the state transportation department's rulemaking authority over window tint.

ia:HF 960.title: A bill for an act relating to the sales tax exemption for the purchase of central office equipment or transmission equipment used by certain entities primarily in the furnishing of telecommunications services on a commercial basis.
ia:HF 960.summary: Expands the sales tax exemption for telecommunications central office and transmission equipment by dropping "primarily" and adding internet access services, for carriers, cable operators, utilities, cooperatives, and mobile radio providers.

ia:HF 990.title: A bill for an act relating to the issuance of medical cannabidiol registration cards and licensure of medical cannabidiol dispensaries.
ia:HF 990.summary: Removes the Iowa residency requirement for a medical cannabidiol registration card and lets the Department of Health and Human Services license up to 10 medical cannabidiol dispensaries instead of 5.

ia:HF 992.title: A bill for an act relating to the fee for duplicates or other evidence of interstate fuel use tax permits or licenses.
ia:HF 992.summary: As introduced, raises the fee for a duplicate or other evidence of an interstate fuel permit or license from 50 cents to $1.

ia:SF 176.title: A bill for an act relating to participation in cocurricular and extracurricular activities offered by school districts by pupils who open enroll for purposes of receiving educational instruction and course content primarily over the internet.
ia:SF 176.summary: As introduced, lets students who open enroll in online instruction take part in their home district's extracurricular activities only if the online school's own attendance center does not sponsor those activities.

ia:SF 2039.title: A bill for an act providing for intervention by members of the general assembly in proceedings for judicial review of agency action under the Iowa administrative procedure Act. Effective date: 07/01/2026.
ia:SF 2039.summary: Allows the majority and minority leaders of the Senate and the speaker and minority leader of the House to each intervene in court reviews of state agency actions, and lets other legislators join a motion to intervene.

ia:SF 2187.title: A bill for an act relating to the verification of citizenship and immigration status of persons who apply for or renew a driver’s license or nonoperator’s identification card, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2187.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to use the federal SAVE system to verify citizenship or immigration status of driver's license and ID card applicants and renewers who do not prove citizenship, and bars issuing or renewing if lawful presence cannot be verified.

ia:SF 2201.title: A bill for an act relating to school funding by establishing the state percent of growth and the categorical state percent of growth for the budget year beginning July 1, 2026, modifying provisions relating to property tax replacement payments, transportation equity aid funding, funding for school district budget adjustments, and school district enrollment, establishing an education support personnel salary supplement, making appropriations, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2201.summary: As amended by the House, sets the state percent of growth for school funding at 2.0 percent for the budget year beginning July 1, 2026, caps transportation equity payments at $1 million per district, appropriates $7 million for education support staff pay, and changes enrollment counts and payment timing.

ia:SF 2207.title: A bill for an act relating to the submission of proposed legislation by the governor and state departments and agencies.
ia:SF 2207.summary: Moves the deadline for state departments and agencies to submit proposed bills and resolutions to the Legislative Services Agency from 45 to 60 days before a session, and applies it to the governor except in the year of initial inauguration.

ia:SF 2218.title: A bill for an act relating to state regulatory compliance and eligibility requirements, including by modifying provisions related to the verification of the identity and employment eligibility of individuals by the board of educational examiners, school districts, accredited nonpublic schools, charter schools, and innovation zone schools; the provision of a false social security number to an employer, prospective employer, or a potential employee; qualifications for employment, professional licensure, voter registration, and bail; making penalties applicable; and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2218.summary: Requires work authorization proof for teacher licenses, E-Verify by public employers, and SAVE checks for professional licenses and voter rolls; bars unauthorized aliens from registering to vote; fines employers knowingly employing workers using another's Social Security number; sets pretrial detention presumptions.

ia:SF 2219.title: A bill for an act requiring boards of directors of school districts, governing boards of charter schools, and authorities in charge of accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies related to exempting student absences for school-sponsored activities, programs, competitions, and projects.
ia:SF 2219.summary: Requires school districts, charter schools, and accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies granting exempt absences, with make-up of missed classwork, for students involved in school-sponsored activities, programs, competitions, or projects.

ia:SF 2220.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the Iowa statewide assessment of student progress and programs for gifted and talented children, and by requiring school districts to develop an advanced mathematics pathway and implement procedures for subject acceleration and whole-grade acceleration, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2220.summary: Moves the statewide science assessment from grade 10 to grade 11, requires school districts to set uniform procedures for identifying and serving gifted and talented students, and requires advanced math pathways and procedures for subject and whole-grade acceleration.

ia:SF 2263.title: A bill for an act relating to the carrying, transportation, and possession of weapons, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2263.summary: Allows dangerous weapons in locked, out-of-sight private vehicles in public nonsecure parking lots, bars foster care rules from prohibiting lawful firearms in vehicles carrying foster children, and bars state and local enforcement of "red flag" firearm seizure laws, with $50,000 civil penalties per occurrence.
