ms:SB 2001.summary: Creates youth court divisions in chancery courts, abolishes county-court youth divisions unless counties opt out, opens youth court hearings to the public with exceptions, authorizes expungement of delinquency records, and creates a Family Services Forum.

mt:HB 182.title: Provide grant funding for senior citizen centers
mt:HB 182.summary: Creates a senior citizen center grant program, with up to $5 million in grants to nonprofits for construction, repair and equipment, with matching funds required for grants of $25,000 or more.

mt:HB 2.title: General Appropriations Act
mt:HB 2.summary: Appropriates money to state agencies for the two-year period ending June 30, 2027.

mt:HB 202.title: Generally revise laws related to the unlawful use of aircraft for hunting
mt:HB 202.summary: Adds game birds to species protected from aircraft-assisted hunting, lengthens the waiting period after aircraft use, bans possessing drones while hunting, and raises fines to $3,000-$10,000.

mt:HB 283.title: Revise laws for hunting licenses lotteries
mt:HB 283.summary: Lets the Fish and Wildlife Commission issue its one annual male mountain sheep license and one Shiras moose license by lottery as well as by auction.

mt:HB 339.title: Fund 6th graders in middle school at high school ANB rates along with 7th and 8th graders
mt:HB 339.summary: Funds 6th graders in accredited middle school or junior high programs at the midpoint between elementary and high school per-student rates, as 7th and 8th graders are, and adds funding for career and technical education.

mt:HB 340.title: Establish Montana's BEST program to bolster educator support and training
mt:HB 340.summary: Creates the Montana B.E.S.T. program giving training and support to teachers in their first three years, including mentor stipends, with a $1 million a year appropriation.

mt:HB 368.title: Generally revise water supply requirements for coal-fired generating units
mt:HB 368.summary: Creates the Town of Colstrip Water Infrastructure Mitigation Account, funded with $2 million a year of coal severance tax revenue, to pay for a town water supply if the nearby coal-fired generating unit closes and the town cannot access water.

mt:HB 4.title: Appropriations by budget amendment
mt:HB 4.summary: Appropriates money normally handled by budget amendment to state agencies for fiscal 2025, lets some appropriations continue into 2026 and 2027, and provides for fund transfers.

mt:HB 419.title: Implementing cost reporting for certain Medicaid service provider types
mt:HB 419.summary: Establishes a standardized cost reporting process for certain Medicaid service providers and appropriates $600,000 in state and $600,000 in federal funds for the related rate-adequacy report.

mt:HB 456.title: Provide best beginnings scholarships to child care workers
mt:HB 456.summary: Expands the Best Beginnings child care scholarship program to child-care workers at licensed day-care centers and registered family or group day-care homes with household income under twice the state median, appropriating $5.5 million a year.

mt:HB 499.title: Extend the grow your own grant program
mt:HB 499.summary: Extends the Grow Your Own grant program, makes postsecondary institutions eligible, revises high school credit requirements, and appropriates $500,000.

mt:HB 5.title: Long-range building appropriations
mt:HB 5.summary: Appropriates money for major repair and capital development projects for the biennium ending June 30, 2027, and raises certain long-range building program value thresholds from $150,000 to $300,000.

mt:HB 511.title: Provide grant funding for firefighting training facilities
mt:HB 511.summary: Creates a firefighting training facility grant program, with up to $5 million in grants to local firefighting authorities for construction, repair and equipment, requiring one-to-one matching funds.

mt:HB 551.title: Eliminate reduced-price copayments for school lunch and breakfast
mt:HB 551.summary: Creates a state program, funded at $600,000 a year, to replace funding for school districts that eliminate reduced-price copayments for school lunch and breakfast.

mt:HB 585.title: Revise provider rate laws for physical therapists, speech-language pathologists, and occupational therapists
mt:HB 585.summary: Sets Medicaid fees for physical, speech-language and occupational therapist services as a conversion factor ($39.56 in fiscal 2026) times relative value units; the department may raise the factor later in line with the medical care price index.

mt:HB 610.title: Revise preauthorization laws relating to healthcare
mt:HB 610.summary: Bars the health department from requiring Medicaid prior authorization for FDA-approved antipsychotic drugs, for approved uses, for members 18 and older.

mt:HB 628.title: Revise early literacy targeted intervention laws
mt:HB 628.summary: Expands the early literacy targeted intervention program to include scholastic literacy and lets school districts opt in to enrolling on-target students, up to one per five eligible students, in some interventions.

mt:HB 643.title: Revise reimbursement costs to detention centers holding inmates in state custody
mt:HB 643.summary: Redefines the 'actual costs' counties charge for holding other agencies' inmates as the greater of a private-facility daily rate less 10% or $82, and appropriates $6 million to reimburse counties for holding people awaiting mental evaluation or placement.

mt:HB 722.title: Provide a retention period for electronic communications after a public employee's employment ends
mt:HB 722.summary: Requires public agencies to keep a public employee's email account communications for at least one year after the employee's last day of employment.

mt:HB 762.title: Require the department of fish, wildlife, and parks to publish a report on river usage
mt:HB 762.summary: Requires the Department of Fish, Wildlife and Parks to publish a biennial river-use report, paid from the state park account, and appropriates $2.6 million.

mt:HB 810.title: Revise tenant landlord laws
mt:HB 810.summary: Specifies acceptable forms of rent payment (cash, check, electronic or other agreed forms) and bars landlords from charging extra fees based on payment type, except to recoup an electronic bank fee for electronic payments.

mt:HB 831.title: Increase elderly homeowner and renter income tax credit
mt:HB 831.summary: Increases the elderly homeowner and renter income tax credit, changes the definition of household income and the credit phaseout, and adds an inflation adjustment to the phaseout income level.

mt:HB 832.title: Establish PTSD nonmedication therapy training grant program
mt:HB 832.summary: Creates a grant program to train providers in posttraumatic stress disorder therapies that do not use medication, appropriating $600,000.

mt:HB 850.title: Provide licensing and regulation of community health workers
mt:HB 850.summary: Requires community health workers to be licensed by the Department of Labor and Industry; applicants must be 18 or older, complete a training program and supervised experience or show equivalent experience, and pay fees, with requirements set by rule.

mt:HB 860.title: Provide for veterinary training loan program
mt:HB 860.summary: Creates a veterinary training loan program giving loans up to $100,000 to students who commit to practicing in underserved Montana areas, with repayment if they do not, and with forgiven loans not counted as income.

mt:HB 861.title: Provide statewide access to a K-12 digital toolkit
mt:HB 861.summary: Appropriates money for statewide access to a K-12 digital toolkit, $1.1 million a year to the Office of Public Instruction and $750,000 a year to the Department of Labor and Industry.

mt:HB 901.title: Create a fire department health and safety grant program
mt:HB 901.summary: Creates a fire department health and safety grant program funded by charitable donations, with grants up to $10,000 per department and a $10 application fee.

mt:HB 924.title: Generally revise state finance laws
mt:HB 924.summary: Creates the Montana Growth and Opportunity Trust funded by transfers of volatile revenue, accounts for property tax relief, water development, local bridges and early childhood, a property tax credit for certified primary residences, and pension and housing funds.

mt:HB 952.title: Authorizing governor to enter into agreements with tribal governments relating to marijuana
mt:HB 952.summary: Authorizes the governor to enter agreements with tribal governments on marijuana regulation and appropriates $1,000.

mt:SB 167.title: Provide funding for noxious weed trust
mt:SB 167.summary: Transfers $10 million from the general fund to the noxious weed management trust fund and requires one-quarter of the fund's interest and income to stay in the trust fund.

mt:SB 188.title: Revising solar energy policy laws
mt:SB 188.summary: Requires utilities to interconnect shared solar facilities of 50 kilowatts to 5 megawatts and to give subscribing customers on-bill credits, and distinguishes shared solar subscribers from net metering customers.

mt:SB 232.title: Revise state procurement laws related to entitles that are exempt from the RFP process.
mt:SB 232.summary: Applies the Montana Procurement Act to the Board of Investments, except for purchases of securities, and changes the act's list of exempt contracts.

mt:SB 244.title: Revise laws related to health insurance coverage of behavioral health screening
mt:SB 244.summary: Requires individual health insurance policies, HMOs, state employee plans and certain multiple employer plans to cover optional behavioral health screenings and assessments at no out-of-pocket cost to the insured.

mt:SB 394.title: Provide for workers' compensation coverage of PTSD for first responders
mt:SB 394.summary: Allows firefighters, law enforcement officers and emergency care providers to file workers' compensation claims for posttraumatic stress disorder when diagnosed under the DSM and arising from their employment.

mt:SB 40.title: Revise supreme court public records laws by opening deliberations and files to the public
mt:SB 40.summary: Requires the Montana Supreme Court to record its closed deliberation meetings and keep a written record, and makes both available to the public after the case is final, though the court may redact confidential information.

mt:SB 410.title: Provide for Montana genomic security act
mt:SB 410.summary: Bars Montana medical and research facilities from using genetic sequencers or software made by a foreign adversary, bans storing Montanans' genetic data outside the U.S., and requires written consent for remote access from outside the U.S.

mt:SB 422.title: Generally revise laws relating to insurance coverage relating to cancer
mt:SB 422.summary: Bars health insurers that cover advanced or metastatic cancer from requiring an insured person to fail, or prove a history of failing, a different drug before covering an FDA-approved prescription drug that follows national cancer guidelines.

mt:SB 424.title: Revising the disabled veteran property tax assistance program
mt:SB 424.summary: Extends the disabled veteran property tax assistance program to veterans rated 80% to 90% disabled, with property tax rate multipliers of 70% to 90% depending on income.

mt:SB 437.title: Revise definition of sex in Montana law
mt:SB 437.summary: Defines sex in state law by reproductive anatomy as male or female only, defines male, female, man, woman, father and mother on that basis, and says "gender" used alone is a synonym for sex rather than gender identity.

mt:SB 472.title: Revise penalties for violations under 310 permit process
mt:SB 472.summary: Raises the daily civil penalty for violating the 310 stream-permit law from $500 to $5,000, with total limits of $100,000 for a first violation and $250,000 for a second, none after; exempts forest practices allowed under state law.

mt:SB 536.title: Revise contractor gross receipts tax
mt:SB 536.summary: Lets 100%-employee-owned (ESOP) contractors claim refunds of the contractor's gross receipts tax credit, extends the credit carryforward from 5 to 7 years, and lets the credit offset certain real property taxes.

mt:SB 537.title: Generally revise marijuana tax laws
mt:SB 537.summary: Changes how marijuana tax revenue is divided, including 20% to a new habitat legacy account, 31% to law enforcement grants and 6.5% to drug and alcohol prevention, and creates accounts for wildlife highway crossings and land and wildlife stewardship.

mt:SB 72.title: Provide presumptive eligibility for Medicaid coverage of home and community-based services
mt:SB 72.summary: Allows presumptive Medicaid eligibility for certain home and community-based services for people with physical disabilities and older adults after a screening and functional assessment, once per 12 months, with a full application due within 30 days.

mt:SB 96.title: Establish working animal protection act
mt:SB 96.summary: As introduced, bars local governments from enacting ordinances or resolutions that ban, or create an undue hardship for, the use of working animals or animal enterprise in commerce or service.

nc:HB 1035.title: Various Local Election Changes III.
nc:HB 1035.summary: Moves municipal elections to even-numbered years for all municipalities in Catawba and McDowell Counties and several towns starting in 2028, and New Bern in 2030. Also extends some town officers' terms from two to four years and changes New Bern's election method.

nc:HB 1089.title: Constitutional Amendment Property Tax Levy Limit.
nc:HB 1089.summary: Puts a question on the ballot on amending the state constitution to require the General Assembly to pass laws limiting how much counties and cities can raise their property tax levies.

nc:HB 1104.title: Improve Involuntary Commitment Process and Enhance Public Safety.
nc:HB 1104.summary: Changes involuntary commitment law, including outpatient commitment criteria and treatment plans; sets capacity restoration services for defendants found incapable to proceed; and orders studies of commitment and of behavioral health care in jails.

nc:HB 1173.title: Jaleeyah's Law.
nc:HB 1173.summary: Changes the definitions of criminal gang member and gang leader, makes it a crime for a gang member to use or carry a firearm during a serious felony, and raises criminal court costs by $30 for costs assessed on or after December 1, 2026.

nc:HB 133.title: NC Farmland and Military Protection Act.
nc:HB 133.summary: Bars foreign parties tied to adversarial governments from acquiring or holding interests in agricultural land or land within 50 miles of a military installation. Holdings before April 1, 2027 may continue but must be registered; later acquisitions must be sold within one year.

nc:HB 162.title: Parking Lot Reform/Stormwater Control.
nc:HB 162.summary: Bars most local governments outside the coastal area from requiring a minimum number of off-street parking spaces, and lets local governments offer optional incentives for extra stormwater controls. Also changes stormwater rules for existing impervious surface.

nc:HB 198.title: ABC Omnibus of 2026.
nc:HB 198.summary: Allows the ABC Commission to borrow up to $310 million for a new warehouse, creates a service business permit for complimentary malt beverages and wine, lets on-premises permit holders sell up to six original-container drinks per patron at once, and makes other alcohol permit changes.

nc:HB 308.title: 2026 Criminal Law Changes.
nc:HB 308.summary: Raises penalties for assault causing serious bodily injury and for strangulation, splits indecent liberties with a child into separate offenses by age and conduct, creates offenses for retail theft tools and approaching a first responder after a warning, and makes other criminal law changes.

nc:HB 315.title: Prohibit Litigation Investments/Amend Workers' Compensation Benefits.
nc:HB 315.summary: Makes it unlawful to provide or engage in litigation investment in civil cases, doubles the maximum workers' compensation payments for disfigurement and loss of body parts, and raises the minimum weekly total-disability rate from $30 to $50.

nc:HB 328.title: Regulate Hemp-Derived Consumables.
nc:HB 328.summary: Creates a licensing and regulation system for hemp-derived consumables, bans sales to people under 21 and sales without a license, requires child-proof exit packaging, and removes school discretion to allow such products on campus.

nc:HB 377.title: 2026 Court Changes.
nc:HB 377.summary: Changes court laws, including when juvenile records may be disclosed, giving any attorney of record access to the trial file in indigent appeals, assigning superior court judges to districts with a county over 1 million people, and Judicial Standards Commission definitions.

nc:HB 437.title: Drug-Free Zones/Unauthorized Public Camping.
nc:HB 437.summary: Creates drug-free zones around homeless shelter and transitional housing providers, and bars local governments from allowing public camping or sleeping on public property except property designated and certified for up to one year.

nc:HB 517.title: Modify Nonprofit Corporations Act/Charitable Organizations.
nc:HB 517.summary: Changes the nonprofit corporation law: allows new kinds of mergers and asset sales, requires annual reports to the Secretary of State, allows domestication, requires new nonprofit boards to have at least 3 natural persons, and aligns charity disclosures with federal rules.

nc:HB 56.title: 2026 Budget Technical Corrections.
nc:HB 56.summary: Makes technical and clarifying changes to the 2026 budget act and other acts, including Hurricane Helene fund transfers, school facility funding cross references, and the principal salary schedule.

nc:HB 562.title: Budget Technical Corrections Modifications.
nc:HB 562.summary: Adjusts the 2026 budget act: redirects several directed grants, moves authorization of the America's Semiquincentennial license plate into GS 20-63, delays an insurance regulatory charge change to 2027, and appropriates $225,000 for State Fire Marshal and $300,000 for Labor Department positions.

nc:HB 727.title: Limit Medicaid Reimb. for Facility Fees.
nc:HB 727.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to stop Medicaid from reimbursing facility fees unless the service is provided at a hospital's main building or nearby structures, a facility with an emergency department, or an ambulatory surgical facility.

nc:HB 832.title: Education Omnibus.
nc:HB 832.summary: As amended by the Senate, makes K-12 changes, including adding English Language Arts to advanced courses with automatic enrollment for top test scorers, removing limits on school units contracting with private providers, creating a Community Eligibility meal incentive program, and changing principal licensing.

nc:HB 87.title: Educational Choice for Children Act (ECCA).
nc:HB 87.summary: Opts North Carolina into the federal tax credit for donations to scholarship granting organizations, and directs the State Education Assistance Authority to list qualifying organizations and carry out the state's participation.

nc:HB 936.title: Robocall Solicitation Modifications.
nc:HB 936.summary: Applies state telephone solicitation rules to robocalls and text messages, requires prior express written consent for solicitations, bans impersonating government officials in them, and counts civil penalties per violation within a single solicitation.

nc:HB 958.title: Election Law Changes.
nc:HB 958.summary: Changes election law, including shortening early voting for primaries and runoffs, requiring county boards to remove deceased voters within a week of receiving federal lists, and making other-state voter data non-public.

nc:HB 96.title: Expedited Removal of Unauthorized Persons.
nc:HB 96.summary: Lets a property owner start an expedited court process to remove an unauthorized person occupying residential property, with a hearing no later than 48 hours after service.

nc:SB 1047.title: Regulatory Reform Act of 2026.
nc:SB 1047.summary: Makes environmental and procurement changes, including Environmental Management Commission approval of DEQ fee adjustments, cutting the underground petroleum tank annual fee from $498 to $100, and authorizing job order contracting.

nc:SB 1057.title: Required Disclosures/Proxy Advisory Services.
nc:SB 1057.summary: Requires proxy advisors to make certain disclosures to shareholders and company boards when they recommend against company management or policy, under a new Proxy Advisor Transparency Act.

nc:SB 1082.title: NC Right to Work Amendment.
nc:SB 1082.summary: Puts a constitutional amendment on the 2026 general election ballot declaring that the right to work may not be denied or abridged because of membership or nonmembership in a labor union or organization.

nc:SB 1092.title: 2026 Senate and House Appointments.
nc:SB 1092.summary: Appoints people to state boards and commissions on the recommendation of the Senate leader and House Speaker, including community college trustees, the 911 Board and a special superior court judge, and shortens one earlier appointment.

nc:SB 177.title: Continuing Budget Adjustments.
nc:SB 177.summary: Appropriates $500 million a year in recurring funds for Medicaid, funds for the State Auditor and State Board of Elections, and about $714 million for capital projects, and exempts the State Board of Elections from the state information technology department's article.

nc:SB 257.title: 2026 Appropriations Act.
nc:SB 257.summary: Enacts the Appropriations Act of 2026, making base budget appropriations for current operations of state agencies, departments and institutions, effective July 1, 2026, in place of the bill's earlier contents.

nc:SB 474.title: Adjust Counties/Reappraisal Moratorium.
nc:SB 474.summary: Adjusts which counties are subject to the property tax reappraisal moratorium, adding an exemption for Hurricane Helene disaster counties that adopt a rate at or below their revenue-neutral rate.

nc:SB 484.title: Clarify Tourism-Related Expenditures.
nc:SB 484.summary: Bars local occupancy tax proceeds labeled tourism-related expenditures from paying for services normally funded by a local government's general fund, such as trash collection, police, emergency services, affordable housing or education, unless a local act allows it.

nc:SB 528.title: Health and Human Services Revisions.
nc:SB 528.summary: Makes several health and human services changes, including wider access to birth certificate data for research and public health, a veterans brain-stimulation pilot program, crisis-line information at schools and colleges, and insurance coverage of prosthetics.

nc:SB 69.title: Various Local Provisions V.
nc:SB 69.summary: Removes Haywood County from a special statute so the standard process fills commissioner vacancies, moves Jackson County school board elections to partisan elections, and bars Jacksonville from using planning powers beyond its corporate limits.

nc:SB 808.title: Board of Cosmetic Art Examiners Amendments.
nc:SB 808.summary: As passed by the Senate, replaces the natural hair care specialist license with a 10-hour infection control certification, cuts the cosmetologist training requirement from 1,500 to 1,200 hours, creates a hair designer license, and allows mobile cosmetic art shops.

nc:SB 858.title: GSC Add Member from High Point Law School.
nc:SB 858.summary: Adds a 14th member to the General Statutes Commission, appointed by the dean of the High Point University School of Law, with a first term from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2029.

nc:SB 876.title: Various Local Provisions X.
nc:SB 876.summary: Makes local law changes, including moving Kannapolis to even-year partisan elections, letting Moore County spend up to $500,000 on storm-damaged areas, and abolishing Southport's historic preservation commission.

nc:SB 992.title: Truth in Taxation.
nc:SB 992.summary: Requires local governments to follow added notice and hearing steps to adopt a property tax rate above the revenue-neutral rate in a reappraisal year, and raises the monthly late fee for reinstating real estate appraiser credentials from $10 to $12.

nd:HB 1003.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the attorney general; to amend and reenact sections 31-01-16, 54-12-11, 54-12-30, and 54-27-25 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to compensation and mileage and travel expenses for witnesses, the salary of the attorney general, twenty-four seven sobriety program fees, and the tobacco settlement trust fund; to provide for a report; to provide for a transfer; and to provide an exemption.
nd:HB 1003.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $118.6 million to the Attorney General for 2025-27, including human trafficking victim and forensic nurse examiner grants, creates an electronic smoking device directory and manufacturing fee, and sets witness pay and the Attorney General's salary.

nd:HB 1004.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the state auditor; and to amend and reenact section 54-10-10 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the state auditor.
nd:HB 1004.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $18.5 million to the State Auditor for 2025-27 and sets the State Auditor's salary.

nd:HB 1005.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the state treasurer; to amend and reenact section 54-11-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the state treasurer; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1005.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $5.8 million to the State Treasurer for 2025-27, moves unclaimed property administration from the Commissioner of University and School Lands to the State Treasurer, and sets the State Treasurer's salary.

nd:HB 1006.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the office of the tax commissioner and for payment of state reimbursement under the homestead tax credit, disabled veterans' tax credit, and primary residence credit; to amend and reenact section 57-01-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the state tax commissioner; to provide an exemption; and to provide for a transfer.
nd:HB 1006.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $126.3 million from all funds to the Tax Commissioner for 2025-27, including reimbursement of the homestead and disabled veterans' tax credits, and sets the Tax Commissioner's salary.

nd:HB 1008.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the public service commission; to amend and reenact sections 49-01-05 and 57-43.2-19 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salaries of the public service commissioners and deposits of special fuels excise taxes; and to provide loan authorization.
nd:HB 1008.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $23.3 million to the Public Service Commission for 2025-27, sets commissioners' salaries, and authorizes a loan of up to $900,000 for a rail rate complaint case.

nd:HB 1009.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the agriculture commissioner; to amend and reenact section 4.1-01-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the agriculture commissioner; to provide for a transfer; to provide for a report; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1009.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $53.2 million to the Agriculture Commissioner for 2025-27, including several fund transfers, and sets the commissioner's salary.

nd:HB 1010.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the insurance commissioner; to create and enact a new section to chapter 26.1-23.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a government self-insurance pool report; to amend and reenact subsection 8 of section 10-04-10 and section 26.1-01-09 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to fees charged by the securities division and the salary of the insurance commissioner; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:HB 1010.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $17.2 million to the Insurance Commissioner for 2025-27, requires government self-insurance pools to report to the Legislative Management every even-numbered year, and sets the commissioner's salary.

nd:HB 1013.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the department of public instruction, the center for distance education, the state library, the school for the deaf, and North Dakota vision services - school for the blind; to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the collection of free or reduced-price meal eligibility information; to amend and reenact sections 15.1-02-02 and 15.1-27-16 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the superintendent of public instruction and administrative cost-sharing; to provide for a transfer; to provide a report; to provide an exemption; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1013.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $3.03 billion to the Department of Public Instruction for 2025-27, plus funds for the Center for Distance Education, state library and schools for the deaf and blind, including $4.5 million in grants for free meals for students at or below 225% of the poverty guideline.

nd:HB 1015.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the various divisions under the supervision of the director of the office of management and budget; to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-44 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a state facility maintenance fund; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 10-30.5-02 of the North Dakota Century Code and section 9 of House Bill No. 1012, as approved by the sixty-ninth Legislative Assembly, relating to the North Dakota development fund and infant and toddler care provider support payments; to repeal section 11-38-08 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to county achievement days; to provide for a transfer; to authorize a line of credit; to provide an exemption; to provide for a report; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1015.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $110 million to the Office of Management and Budget for 2025-27, including a $40 million deferred maintenance pool, and sets guidelines for state employee raises averaging 3% a year.

nd:HB 1016.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the office of the adjutant general; to provide a statement of legislative intent; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1016.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $345 million to the Adjutant General for 2025-27, and states intent to buy up to 1,600 acres and lease the rest, up to 6,000 acres total, for Camp Grafton without using eminent domain.

nd:HB 1018.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the state historical society; to amend and reenact section 55-01-02.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to jurisdiction of the heritage center; to authorize a Bank of North Dakota line of credit; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1018.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $123.4 million to the State Historical Society for 2025-27, including $82.9 million for a military gallery expansion, and authorizes a $20 million Bank of North Dakota line of credit for that project.

nd:HB 1019.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the parks and recreation department; to create and enact a new section to chapter 55-08 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the creation and naming of state parks; to provide for a transfer; to provide for a report; and to provide an exemption.
nd:HB 1019.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $69.5 million to the Parks and Recreation Department for 2025-27, including about $3.9 million for projects at the International Peace Garden.

nd:HB 1022.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the retirement and investment office.
nd:HB 1022.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $16.5 million from special funds to the Retirement and Investment Office for 2025-27, with 35 full-time positions.

nd:HB 1027.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 26.1-01-03, 26.1-22-01, 26.1-22-02, 26.1-22-02.1, 26.1-22-03.1, 26.1-22-09, 26.1-22-10, 26.1-22-11, 26.1-22-14, 26.1-22-16, 26.1-22-17, 26.1-22-21, and 26.1-22-22, subdivisions a and c of subsection 1 of section 26.1-23.1-01, and section 37-03-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to changing the administration of the state fire and tornado fund from the insurance commissioner to the office of management and budget; to repeal sections 26.1-22-03, 26.1-22-05, 26.1-22-06, 26.1-22-06.1, 26.1-22-08, 26.1-22-10.1, 26.1-22-13, 26.1-22-15, 26.1-22-18, 26.1-22-19, and 26.1-22-21.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the administration of the state fire and tornado fund; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide a continuing appropriation.
nd:HB 1027.summary: As passed by the House, moves administration of the state fire and tornado fund from the Insurance Commissioner to the Office of Management and Budget and repeals several related sections.

nd:HB 1032.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 27-05-06 and chapter 40-18.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to jurisdiction of district courts and municipal court requirements, jurisdiction, procedures, and processes; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 29-07-01.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to indigent defense; and to repeal sections 40-11-10, 40-11-11, 40-11-12, and 40-11-13 and chapter 40-18 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to ordinance violations and municipal judges.
nd:HB 1032.summary: Replaces the municipal court law with a new chapter letting cities set up or share municipal courts with elected judges, makes them courts of record from July 1, 2026, and gives district courts ordinance cases in cities under 5,000 without a municipal court.

nd:HB 1053.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 24-01-01.2 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the length of the state highway system.
nd:HB 1053.summary: As amended by the Senate, repeals the law limiting the state highway system to 7,700 miles.

nd:HB 1119.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study regarding child care provider licensing; to provide for a program evaluation regarding child care services; and to create a child care services licensing advisory committee.
nd:HB 1119.summary: As passed by the House, directs the Legislative Management to consider studying laws, rules and policies on early childhood services and child care, including licensing requirements, assistance programs, staff training, child-to-provider ratios and square footage requirements.

nd:HB 1126.title: AN ACT to create and enact eleven new sections to chapter 43-11 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to salon and school inspections, nursing home, basic care facility, and assisted living facility salons, military and military spouse reciprocity licensure, advanced esthetician licensing and late renewals for establishments and schools; to amend and reenact sections 43-11-01, 43-11-02, 43-11-03, 43-11-04, 43-11-05, 43-11-06, 43-11-08, 43-11-10, 43-11-11, 43-11-13, 43-11-14, 43-11-15, 43-11-16, 43-11-16.1, 43-11-19, 43-11-20.3, 43-11-21, 43-11-23, 43-11-24, 43-11-25, 43-11-26, 43-11-27, 43-11-28, and 43-11-29 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the practice and licensure of cosmetologists, estheticians, advanced estheticians, manicurists, and instructors; to repeal sections 43-11-11.1, 43-11-17, and 43-11-27.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the use of brush rollers, licenses issued for schools and salons, and esthetician and manicurist licensing qualifications and fees; to provide a penalty; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1126.summary: As passed by the House, changes cosmetology law to add salon and school inspections, services for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, license reciprocity for military members and spouses, an advanced esthetician license, and late renewals.

nd:HB 1130.title: A BILL for an Act to amend and reenact section 15.1-27-04.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the option for a school district to reduce its local contribution deduction in the school state aid formula by the percentage of the local contribution which comes from in lieu of revenue.
nd:HB 1130.summary: As passed by the House, lets a school district that levied sinking and interest mills in 2024 and uses the amount for capital projects or debt repayment reduce the revenue deducted from its state aid by either its 2024 sinking-and-interest mill share or its in-lieu-of-tax revenue share.

nd:HB 1139.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 57-39.2-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a sales tax exemption for fire departments; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1139.summary: Exempts sales to approved fire departments and fire districts, for fire protection services, from state sales tax, for sales after June 30, 2025.

nd:HB 1151.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study regarding the regulation of cell-cultured protein.
nd:HB 1151.summary: Directs the legislature's management committee to consider studying cell-cultured protein, including litigation in other states and the feasibility of a state prohibition, and to report to the next legislative assembly.

nd:HB 1160.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the use of personal electronic devices during instructional time.
nd:HB 1160.summary: As passed by the House, requires school district boards to adopt a policy governing student cellular telephone use during instructional and noninstructional time, which must include exceptions for medical accommodations, individual education plans and emergencies.

nd:HB 1168.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact two new sections to chapter 54-27, a new section to chapter 57-02, and a new section to chapter 57-15 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a legacy earnings fund, a legacy property tax relief fund, a primary residence certification, and a limitation on property tax levies without voter approval; to amend and reenact section 6-09.4-10.1, subsection 1 of section 21-10-06, sections 40-40-06, 54-27-19.3, and 57-02-01, subdivision c of subsection 1 of section 57-02-08.1, subdivision b of subsection 2 of section 57-02-08.1, section 57-02-08.8, section 57-02-08.9 as amended by section 1 of Senate Bill No. 2201, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, sections 57-02-08.10, 57-02-27, 57-02-27.1, 57-02-53, 57-09-04, 57-11-03, 57-12-06, 57-15-02.2, 57-15-14.2, and 57-20-07.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to funds invested by the state investment board, property tax definitions, the homestead tax credit and renters refund, the property tax credit for disabled veterans, the primary residence credit, property classifications, assessment and budget hearing notices to property owners, school district levies, and the property tax statement; to repeal sections 21-10-12 and 21-10-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to legacy fund definitions and the legacy earnings fund; to provide a statement of legislative intent; to provide for a legislative management study, to provide an appropriation; to provide an effective date; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1168.summary: As passed by the House, creates a legacy earnings fund fed by a 7% draw on the Legacy Fund. Limits yearly property tax levy increases to 3% for taxing districts other than school districts unless voters approve, and changes school aid formula provisions.

nd:HB 1176.title: AN ACT to create and enact two new sections to chapter 54-27, a new section to chapter 57-02, and a new section to chapter 57-15 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a legacy earnings fund, a legacy property tax relief fund, a primary residence certification, and a limitation on property tax levies without voter approval; to amend and reenact section 6-09.4-10.1, subsection 1 of section 21-10-06, sections 40-40-06, 54-27-19.3, and 57-02-01, subdivision b of subsection 2 of section 57-02-08.1, section 57-02-08.8, section 57-02-08.9 as amended by section 1 of Senate Bill No. 2201, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, sections 57-02-08.10, 57-02-27, 57-02-27.1, 57-02-53, 57-09-04, 57-11-03, 57-12-06, 57-15-02.2, 57-15-14.2, and 57-20-07.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to funds invested by the state investment board, property tax definitions, the renters refund, the property tax credit for disabled veterans, the primary residence credit, property classifications, assessment and budget hearing notices to property owners, school district levies, and the property tax statement; to repeal sections 21-10-12 and 21-10-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to legacy fund definitions and the legacy earnings fund; to provide for a legislative management study; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide an appropriation; to provide an exemption; to provide an effective date; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1176.summary: As passed by the House, creates a legacy earnings fund fed by a 7% draw on the Legacy Fund and a legacy property tax relief fund. Requires primary residence certification and limits property tax levies without voter approval.

nd:HB 1181.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 1-01-34 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to gender usage in the North Dakota Century Code.
nd:HB 1181.summary: As passed by the House, provides that words referring to an individual's gender in state law mean the individual's sex, and applies that rule to policies, records and forms of public schools, state colleges and state agencies unless federal law requires otherwise.

nd:HB 1193.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation to the attorney general for a peace officer and correctional officer appreciation grant program; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:HB 1193.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates $3.5 million to the Attorney General for grants to city and county law enforcement agencies, divided by their number of licensed peace officers and correctional officers.

nd:HB 1203.title: AN ACT to create and enact section 19-24.1-24.1 and a new subsection to section 19-24.1-36 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to regulating edible medical marijuana products; and to amend and reenact section 19-24.1-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to definitions of medical marijuana products.
nd:HB 1203.summary: As passed by the House, requires state approval before a manufacturing facility or dispensary makes or sells edible medical marijuana products, caps packages at 100 milligrams of THC, requires resealable child-resistant packaging and text-only labels, bars marketing to minors, and widens the edible definition to foods and drinks.

nd:HB 1209.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management report relating to a foreign adversary threat assessment conducted by the department of emergency services.
nd:HB 1209.summary: As passed by the House, requires the Department of Emergency Services to assess which sectors are most vulnerable to foreign adversary influence, including beyond land purchases, propose mitigation strategies and a state intelligence unit, and report to the Legislative Management by September 2026.

nd:HB 1214.title: AN ACT to create and enact section 15.1-27-31.2 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to transportation weighted student unit equivalents; to amend and reenact sections 15.1-31-05 and  15.1-27-31.2 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to open enrollment transportation; to repeal sections 15.1-27-26.1, 15.1-27-27.1, 15.1-27-28.1, 15.1-27-30.1, and 15.1-27-31.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to payments for school district transportation of students, special education students, and career and technical education students, the distribution of transportation payments in the event of school district closure, and state transportation payments to school districts; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1214.summary: Replaces several school transportation payment formulas with one formula that converts bus miles, bus runs, district size and school buildings into weighted student units, and revises open enrollment transportation payments.

nd:HB 1216.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 26.1-36 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to out-of-pocket expenses for prescription drugs; to amend and reenact section 26.1-36.6-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to self-insurance health care plans; to provide for application; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1216.summary: Requires health plans that cover prescription drugs to count amounts paid by or for the enrollee, including through cost-sharing assistance programs, toward the out-of-pocket maximum and cost-sharing for those drugs, to the extent federal law allows.

nd:HB 1218.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 61-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a temporary moratorium on conducting an economic analysis for assessment drain projects; to amend and reenact section 61-02-01.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to comprehensive water development plans; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:HB 1218.summary: Bars the State Water Commission and Department of Water Resources from conducting economic analyses for assessment drain projects from August 1, 2025 to July 31, 2027, bars requiring them for projects costing $1 million or less, and directs a study.

nd:HB 1226.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 12.1-31-15 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to wearing a mask in a public place.
nd:HB 1226.summary: As passed by the House, adds a ban on wearing a mask or face covering to conceal identity while congregating in public with others wearing them, despite a law enforcement request to unmask, except at Halloween, masquerade or similar celebrations.

nd:HB 1234.title: AN ACT to provide a transfer from the strategic investment and improvements fund to the public employees retirement system fund; and to provide for a statement of legislative intent.
nd:HB 1234.summary: As passed by the House, transfers $135 million from the strategic investment and improvements fund to the public employees retirement system fund to reduce the unfunded liability of its main defined benefit plan.

nd:HB 1279.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 57-60-02, 57-60-02.1, 57-60-02.2, 57-60-14, and 57-61-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a partial exemption from the coal conversion facilities tax and the imposition of a lignite research tax, allocation of the coal conversion facilities privilege tax and the lignite research tax, and an exemption from the coal severance tax; to repeal section 57-60-02.2 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the exemption from the coal conversion facilities tax and the imposition of a lignite research tax; to provide an effective date; to provide a contingent effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:HB 1279.summary: Extends from June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2036 the current coal conversion facility tax rules, including the 85% exemption with a lignite research tax of 5% of the exempted amount, and the related revenue allocation and coal severance tax provisions.

nd:HB 1300.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to legislative term limits.
nd:HB 1300.summary: Provides that years of service counted toward the constitutional legislative term limit begin to run when a person is first elected or appointed to the Legislature after November 7, 2022.

nd:HB 1307.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 11-09.1-04, 11-09.1-05, 40-05.1-05, 40-05.1-06, and 40-49-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to election laws in home rule counties and cities and nominating petition signature thresholds in park districts.
nd:HB 1307.summary: As passed by the House, makes ordinances of home rule counties and cities on elections void when they conflict with state law, and removes the charter power to provide for all matters pertaining to county and city elections.

nd:HB 1308.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 54-12-33 and 54-12-33.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to duties of the human trafficking commission and immunity for reporting human trafficking; to provide a continuing appropriation; and to provide a contingent effective date.
nd:HB 1308.summary: Adds legislator, school, tribal, prosecutor, child-welfare and governor's-office members to the state human trafficking commission. Gives lodging staff and licensed professionals who report suspected trafficking in good faith immunity from civil suits.

nd:HB 1318.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 28-01.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to pesticide labeling.
nd:HB 1318.summary: Provides that a pesticide label approved by the EPA, or consistent with its latest human health assessment or carcinogenicity classification, satisfies state-law duties to warn or label about health and safety, including common-law duties.

nd:HB 1322.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 23-27 and a new section to chapter 26.1-47 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to ambulance service balanced billing and provider reimbursement; to amend and reenact section 23-27-04.8 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to emergency medical services communication; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:HB 1322.summary: As passed by the House, bars non-air ambulance providers from billing patients more than in-network cost-sharing, requires insurers to pay out-of-network ambulance providers the lesser of 250% of the Medicare rate or billed charges, and directs the Legislative Management to consider studying delinquent-billing grants.

nd:HB 1329.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study regarding the establishment of a government spending database.
nd:HB 1329.summary: As passed by the House, directs the Legislative Management to consider studying whether to create a government spending database listing the amount, date, recipient and payer of each expenditure, plus training for school officials on it.

nd:HB 1332.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 4.1-01.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a value-added agriculture facility incentive program; to provide for a transfer; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1332.summary: As passed by the House, creates a grant program, capped at $30 million, for new value-added agriculture production facilities with at least $350 million in capital investment, paid from the agriculture diversification and development fund. The Act expires June 30, 2029.

nd:HB 1361.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 12.1-41 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to mandatory minimum sentences for human trafficking offenders; and to provide a penalty.
nd:HB 1361.summary: Sets mandatory minimum prison terms without parole for human trafficking offenders: 40 years for a class AA felony, 15 years for a class A felony and 7 years for a class B felony.

nd:HB 1363.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to cardiac emergency response plans for public and nonpublic schools and athletic events.
nd:HB 1363.summary: As passed by the House, requires public and nonpublic schools to adopt a cardiac emergency response plan from a state template, place and label defibrillators on school grounds and at athletic venues, and gives school staff and board members immunity from liability when carrying out the plan.

nd:HB 1382.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-27 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the creation of the city, county, and township road fund; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 39-04-19.2, section 54-27-19, subsection 1 of section 57-43.1-02, and subsection 1 of section 57-43.2-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle road use fee, the tax imposed on motor vehicle and special fuels, and the highway tax distribution fund; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1382.summary: As passed by the House, raises the annual electric vehicle road use fee from $120 to $150 and the plug-in hybrid fee from $50 to $60, raises the motor fuel tax from 23 to 26 cents per gallon, and creates a city, county and township road fund.

nd:HB 1417.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 12-59-15 and 12.1-01-04, subdivision b of subsection 3 of section 12.1-22-01, and sections 12.1-32-07, 12.1-32-08, and 29-07-01.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to parole and probation violations and court fees; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide a penalty.
nd:HB 1417.summary: As passed by the House, changes rules on parole and probation violations, indigent defense cost reimbursement and court fees, and directs the Legislative Management to consider studying court fines and fees.

nd:HB 1425.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 11-16, a new chapter to title 12, and two new sections to chapter 54-23.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to prosecution-led diversion programs, deflection process, and supervision for presentence programs; to provide for a legislative management study; to provide for a legislative management report; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:HB 1425.summary: As passed by the House, lets county state's attorneys run prosecution-led diversion programs, lets local agencies set up deflection processes for people with behavioral health conditions, sets up a corrections supervision pilot in three counties, and provides funding and a study.

nd:HB 1442.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-35 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the creation of a legislative task force on government efficiency; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1442.summary: As passed by the House, creates a legislative task force on government efficiency of state officials and legislators that reviews agency budgets, identifies unnecessary or duplicative programs, requests program audits, and reports annually to the Legislative Management.

nd:HB 1476.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the assessment of all public school buildings.
nd:HB 1476.summary: Allows the superintendent of public instruction to collect school districts' building assessments, record building inventories every four years, track repairs and maintenance, and contract for studies of school facility standards. Requires rules to implement this.

nd:HB 1485.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 50-24.1-02.6 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the personal needs allowance amount for eligible beneficiaries; to provide for an increase in the personal monthly needs allowance; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:HB 1485.summary: As passed by the House, requires the Department of Health and Human Services to provide a personal monthly needs allowance of at least $110 to Medicaid beneficiaries, adjusted annually for inflation.

nd:HB 1487.title: AN ACT to authorize the department of transportation to transfer real property to the office of management and budget; to provide an appropriation; to authorize a line of credit; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1487.summary: As passed by the House, directs the Department of Transportation to convey about 1.25 acres in Ward County to the Office of Management and Budget, and appropriates $4.9 million from the strategic investment and improvements fund to build a Minot facility leased to state agencies.

nd:HB 1489.title: AN ACT to create and enact chapter 14-07.7 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to civil protection orders; to amend and reenact sections 11-15-32 and 12-60-23, subsection 2 of section 12.1-17-13, section 14-05-23, subsection 4 of section 14-07.1-01, sections 14-07.1-02.1 and 14-07.1-11, subsection 1 of section 14-07.1-14, section 14-07.1-19, subdivision a of subsection 1 of section 14-07.6-01, subdivision b of subsection 1 of section 15.1-09-33.4, sections 16.1-02-07 and 29-01-15, subdivision g of subsection 1 of section 29-06-15, and subdivision a of subsection 2 of section 47-16-17.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to restraining orders and protection orders; to repeal sections 12.1-31-01.2, 12.1-31.2-01, 14-07.1-02, 14-07.1-03, 14-07.1-03.1, 14-07.1-04, 14-07.1-05, 14-07.1-05.1, 14-07.1-06, 14-07.1-07, and 14-07.1-08 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to sexual assault restraining orders and domestic violence protection orders; to provide a penalty; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1489.summary: As passed by the House, creates a single chapter of law for civil protection orders, replacing separate rules for disorderly conduct restraining orders, domestic violence protection orders and sexual assault restraining orders, and updates related laws to refer to it.

nd:HB 1498.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 15-20.2-07 and 15.1-09-33.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the powers and duties of center boards and the authority of a school board to pay a first-year signing bonus for teachers; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1498.summary: As passed by the House, lets school district boards and career and technology center boards offer a first-year signing bonus to licensed individuals who were not classroom teachers in the state the previous school year, outside the negotiated salary schedule.

nd:HB 1535.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact the new chapter to title 54 as created by section 1 of Senate Bill No. 2098, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, and section 54-35-23 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a state alert notice system and the committee on tribal and state relations; and to provide for a report.
nd:HB 1535.summary: As passed by the House, requires the Highway Patrol, with the Bureau of Criminal Investigation and state radio, to set up a feather alert system to broadcast bulletins on missing Indigenous individuals, and directs the Tribal and State Relations Committee to evaluate it.

nd:HB 1537.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 6-09.4-22 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to service agreement protection of service during the term of the loan; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1537.summary: As passed by the House, lets the public finance authority or another state lender void, on 30 days' written notice, agreements made before 2025 between political subdivisions over who provides a loan-funded service, if the lender is not a party or bond payments are not safeguarded.

nd:HB 1540.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new chapter to title 15.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an education savings account program for students who are not enrolled in public school or a homeschool program; to provide an appropriation; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1540.summary: As passed by the House, creates an education savings account program starting in 2026-27 for students who attend neither public school nor a home school, with the Bank of North Dakota depositing 50% of the statewide average per-student payment into each account, and appropriates $40 million.

nd:HB 1542.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 44-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to designating student applications for admission to an institution of higher education as exempt records; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1542.summary: Makes records of applications for admission to institutions under the State Board of Higher Education confidential, and requires them to be destroyed on request of the applicant or, for applicants under 18 at the time, a parent or guardian.

nd:HB 1566.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study relating to the potential uses of kratom and the implementation of regulations of kratom in the state.
nd:HB 1566.summary: Directs the legislature's management committee to consider studying potential uses of kratom and regulation of its production, manufacture, distribution and retail sale, and to report to the next legislative assembly.

nd:HB 1575.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact two new sections to chapter 54-27, two new sections to chapter 57-02, and a new subdivision to subsection 1 of section 57-55-10 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a legacy earnings fund, a legacy property tax relief fund, a state reimbursed taxable valuation reduction for residential, agricultural, and commercial property, limitations on taxable valuation increases, and voter-approved excess levy authority; to amend and reenact section 6-09.4-10.1, subsection 1 of section 21-10-06, section 54-27-19.3, subdivision c of subsection 1 of section 57-02-08.1, subdivision b of subsection 2 of section 57-02-08.1, and section 57-02-08.10, of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to funds invested by the state investment board, the homestead tax credit and renters refund, and the primary residence credit certification and state reimbursement; to repeal sections 21-10-12, 21-10-13, and 57-02-08.9 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to legacy fund definitions, the legacy earnings fund, and the primary residence credit; to provide an appropriation; to provide for a transfer; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:HB 1575.summary: Creates a legacy earnings fund fed by a 7% Legacy Fund draw. Cuts taxable valuation by 2.75% of assessed value for residential and 1.5% for agricultural and commercial property, with state reimbursement; caps yearly taxable value increases at 3%; requires voter approval of excess levies.

nd:HB 1580.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study relating to state employee compensation levels.
nd:HB 1580.summary: Directs the Legislative Management to consider studying the state employee compensation system, including pay grades and classifications, comparisons with private sector jobs, equity funding and bonuses, and prevailing wages on state projects.

nd:HB 1581.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation to the department of commerce for tribal tourism grants; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:HB 1581.summary: Appropriates $100,000 to the Department of Commerce for grants of up to $20,000 to tribal governments, matching their own funds, to promote tribal tourism.

nd:HB 1582.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study regarding a review of state laws relating to false accusations or false reports of a crime.
nd:HB 1582.summary: As passed by the House, directs the Legislative Management to consider studying the state's laws on false accusations and false reports of a crime, with input from state's attorneys and defense attorneys.

nd:HB 1584.title: AN ACT to create and enact four new sections to chapter 26.1-27.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to pharmacy benefits managers and a pharmacy benefit manager enforcement fund; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 26.1-01-07, sections 26.1-27.1-01, 26.1-27.1-02, 26.1-27.1-04, 26.1-27.1-06 and 26.1-27.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to pharmacy benefits managers; to repeal section 26.1-27-01.1 and chapter 26.1-36.10 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to pharmacy benefits managers and prescription drug costs; to provide a penalty; to provide an appropriation; to provide for a transfer; to provide an effective date; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1584.summary: Requires pharmacy benefit managers to be licensed, bars tying one pharmacy contract to another, requires opt-in contracts, and sets penalties up to $10,000 per violation. Creates an enforcement fund and appropriates $1.2 million to the insurance commissioner.

nd:HB 1600.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15-11 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the establishment of the immigration law clinic at the university of North Dakota school of law; to provide for a report; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:HB 1600.summary: As passed by the House, requires the University of North Dakota School of Law to employ one full-time attorney for an immigration law clinic, limited to 60 open matters at a time, allows nominal fees, and appropriates $400,000 for a grant to the university.

nd:HB 1621.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 15.1-21-01 and section 15.1-21-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to requiring the presidential physical fitness test in physical education courses in elementary, middle, and high schools and providing exceptions to the test; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1621.summary: Requires physical education courses in elementary, middle and high schools to include participation in the presidential physical fitness test, and lets the Superintendent of Public Instruction set exceptions.

nd:HB 1624.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact two new sections to chapter 15.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to offering school breakfast and lunch at no cost and the school meals fund; to provide an appropriation; to provide for a transfer; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1624.summary: Requires public schools to provide one breakfast and one lunch daily at no cost to any student who asks, with the state reimbursing the gap between federal reimbursement rates and amounts actually received.

nd:HB 1626.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact subdivision d of subsection 1 of section 57-02-08.9, section 57-20-09, and subsection 1 of section 57-55-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to application of the primary residence credit and discount for early payment of tax; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1626.summary: Requires the primary residence property tax credit to be applied after the early-payment discount, with matching changes for real estate and mobile home taxes.

nd:SB 2001.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the legislative branch of state government; to amend and reenact sections 48-08-04, 54-03-10, 54-03-20, and 54-35-10 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to use of legislative rooms and halls and legislative compensation; to provide a statement of legislative intent; to provide for a report; to provide an exemption; and to provide for application, transfer, and cancellation of unexpended appropriations.
nd:SB 2001.summary: Appropriates about $52.7 million from the general fund for the legislative branch for 2025-27, raises leadership per-day pay (e.g. $15 to $20 for the speaker and majority/minority leaders), and sets legislators' daily pay at $226 from July 2026.

nd:SB 2002.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the judicial branch; to provide an appropriation to the office of guardianship and conservatorship; to create and enact a new subsection to section 54-06-08.2 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to credit and debit card fees; to amend and reenact sections 27-02-02 and 27-05-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salaries of justices of the supreme court and salaries of district court judges; to provide for transfers; to provide for a report; and to provide an exemption.
nd:SB 2002.summary: Appropriates about $152.9 million to the judicial branch and the Office of Guardianship and Conservatorship for 2025-27, raises salaries for supreme court justices and district court judges, and lets the judicial branch charge a card-payment fee.

nd:SB 2004.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the ethics commission; to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-03 and two new sections to chapter 54-66 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to immunity and a defense for individuals voting on legislation, closure of a matter of the ethics commission, rules for complaint management time standards, and an ethics commission annual report; to amend and reenact sections 12.1-13-02, 54-66-01, 54-66-04, 54-66-05, 54-66-06, and 54-66-07, subsection 2 of section 54-66-08, and sections 54-66-09, 54-66-10, 54-66-12, and 54-66-18 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to immunity from criminal prosecution, definitions, ethics commission meetings, complaints, an informal resolution process, law enforcement referrals, findings, appeals, confidential information related to a complaint, and conflicts of interest; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2004.summary: Appropriates about $1.37 million to the Ethics Commission for 2025-27 and changes ethics law, including immunity from prosecution for legislators who follow conflict-disclosure rules when voting, a petition to dismiss complaints, complaint time standards and an annual report.

nd:SB 2009.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the state fair association; to repeal section 4.1-45-22.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to state fair facility operations and maintenance costs; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2009.summary: Appropriates about $2.2 million to the State Fair Association for 2025-27, including campground rest facility funding, and repeals the state fair facility operations and maintenance cost provision.

nd:SB 2013.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the commissioner of university and school lands; to provide for distributions from permanent funds; and to provide for a report.
nd:SB 2013.summary: Appropriates $11.96 million in special funds to the commissioner of university and school lands for 2025-27 and directs $617.3 million in distributions from permanent trust funds, including $584.7 million to common schools, to state institutions.

nd:SB 2014.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the industrial commission and the agencies under its control; to create and enact a new section to chapter 6-09 and a new subdivision to subsection 2 of section 38-08-04.5 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a rail revolving loan fund and uses of the abandoned oil and gas well plugging and site reclamation fund; to amend and reenact subsection 7 of section 6-08.1-02 and sections 6-09-35, 6-09-46.2, 6-09.7-05, 6-09.14-04, and 49-17.1-02.1, subsection 1 of section 54-17-40, and subdivision a of subsection 4 of section 54-17.7-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, and section 15 of chapter 14 of the 2023 Session Laws, relating to confidential and exempt records of the Bank of North Dakota, the rebuilders loan program, loan guarantees through the strategic investment and improvements fund, interest rate buydown limits for the partnership in assisting community expansion fund, department of transportation review and approval of rail projects, uses of the housing incentive fund, North Dakota pipeline borrowing authority, and a salt cavern underground energy storage research project; to repeal section 3 of Senate Bill No. 2188, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, relating to a transfer from the strategic investment and improvements fund to the clean sustainable energy fund; to provide a deficiency appropriation; to provide for a transfer; to provide an exemption; to provide for a legislative management study; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide for a report; to provide an effective date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2014.summary: Appropriates about $439 million to the Industrial Commission and the agencies it controls for 2025-27, creates a rail revolving loan fund, and sets uses for the abandoned oil and gas well plugging and site reclamation fund.

nd:SB 2018.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the department of commerce; to provide an appropriation to the attorney general; to provide an appropriation to the department of career and technical education; to provide an appropriation to the state fair association; to provide a contingent appropriation; to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-60 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to department of commerce grant reporting requirements; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 10-30.5-02, sections 54-60-09, 54-60-19, 54-60-28, 54-60-29, 54-60-29.1, and 54-60-31 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the purpose of the North Dakota development fund, duties and talent strategy of the division of workforce development, the uncrewed aircraft systems program, the uncrewed aircraft systems program fund, the beyond visual line of sight uncrewed aircraft system program, and changing the name of the office of legal immigration to the global talent office; to authorize a Bank of North Dakota line of credit; to provide for a transfer; to provide an application; to provide an exemption; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:SB 2018.summary: Appropriates about $158 million to the Department of Commerce for 2025-27, plus money for the Attorney General, career and technical education and the State Fair, and requires Commerce to report on grants.

nd:SB 2020.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the North Dakota state university extension service, northern crops institute, upper great plains transportation institute, main research center, branch research centers, and agronomy seed farm; to provide for a report; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2020.summary: Appropriates about $285.7 million from all funds for 2025-27 to the NDSU Extension Service, Northern Crops Institute, Upper Great Plains Transportation Institute, main research center, branch research centers and the agronomy seed farm.

nd:SB 2021.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the information technology department; to amend and reenact sections 54-35-15.1, 54-59-14, and 54-59-15 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to membership of the information technology committee and the information technology operating fund; to provide an exemption; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:SB 2021.summary: Appropriates $48.0 million from the general fund ($200.5 million total) to the Information Technology Department for 2025-27, adds a nonvoting health and human services member to the legislature's IT committee, and provides for interim studies of radio network fees and the state ERP system.

nd:SB 2023.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the North Dakota racing commission.
nd:SB 2023.summary: Appropriates $521,818 from the general fund ($699,042 total) to the North Dakota Racing Commission for 2025-27, including one-time funding for copier replacement and internships.

nd:SB 2025.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the department of veterans' affairs; to amend and reenact sections 37-15-03, 37-15-07, 37-15-16, 37-18-01, and 37-18-07, subsection 1 of section 37-18-12, and section 37-18.1-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the administrative committee on veterans' affairs; to provide for a transfer; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2025.summary: Appropriates $3.0 million from the general fund ($5.0 million total) to the Department of Veterans' Affairs for 2025-27, including $500,000 for homeless veterans' services, and makes the governor, not a committee, supervise the veterans' home.

nd:SB 2029.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 30.1-28-07 and chapter 54-68 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an office of guardianship and conservatorship and the removal of a guardian; to amend and reenact section 30.1-29-15 and subsection 1 of section 50-24.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the removal of a conservator and the recovery of medical assistance expenses; to repeal chapter 27-27 and section 54-68-02.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the task force on guardianship monitoring and transition requirements; to provide a penalty; to provide for a report; to provide an appropriation; to provide a continuing appropriation; to provide for a transfer; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2029.summary: Creates a state Office of Guardianship and Conservatorship that licenses guardians and conservators, lets courts list those removed for good cause on a registry that disqualifies them, and repeals the guardianship monitoring task force.

nd:SB 2037.title: AN ACT to create and enact three new sections to chapter 27-20.4 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to juvenile court petitions, fitness to proceed in juvenile court proceedings, and collateral consequences the juvenile court may order; to amend and reenact sections 12.1-04.1-01, 12.1-04.1-20, and 12.1-17-01.2, subsection 2 of section 12.1-17-07.2, section 12.1-20-01, subsections 2 and 6 of section 12.1-31-03, sections 12.1-32-15 and 15.1-09-33.4, subsection 6 of section 27-20.2-01, subsection 3 of section 27-20.2-09, subsection 5 of section 27-20.4-11, subsection 1 of section 27-20.4-18, subsection 1 of section 27-20.4-20, and section 62.1-02-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to lack of criminal responsibility, court jurisdiction, distribution of intimate images without consent, domestic violence, criminality of a child regarding sex offenses, sale and use of tobacco by an individual under the age of twenty-one, child registration requirements, restitution, probation of a delinquent child, extracurricular activities for students, and persons not allowed to possess a firearm; to repeal sections 27-20.4-12, 27-20.4-13, and 27-20.4-19 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to delinquency; to provide an appropriation; and to provide a penalty.
nd:SB 2037.summary: Lets children ten or older be assessed for lack of criminal responsibility, sets one-year court jurisdiction over a juvenile not adjudicated for that reason, appropriates $300,000 for evaluations, and revises other juvenile justice provisions.

nd:SB 2051.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 43-30-16 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to fees charged by the North Dakota private investigative and security board; to provide for a performance audit of the North Dakota private investigative and security board; and to declare an emergency.
