wi:AB 673.summary: Bars medical and research facilities that receive state money from using genetic sequencers or analysis software produced by companies in China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia or Maduro-ruled Venezuela, and restricts storing human genome data in those countries.

wi:AB 674.title: Relating to: prohibiting knowingly covering organ transplantation and related care under health insurance policies and the Medical Assistance program if the organ is transplanted in or originates from a country known to have participated in forced organ harvesting. (FE)
wi:AB 674.summary: Bars health insurance plans and Medical Assistance from knowingly covering organ transplants performed in, or with organs obtained from, China or other countries designated for forced organ harvesting, while allowing life-saving post-transplant care.

wi:AB 700.title: Relating to: an appropriation for refundable long-term care insurance assessment credits and making an appropriation. (FE)
wi:AB 700.summary: Provides a sum-sufficient appropriation to pay refundable long-term care insurance assessment credits created in a separate bill; the bill is void if that separate bill is not enacted.

wi:AB 759.title: Relating to: eligibility to receive occupational credentials for recipients of deferred action under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program. (FE)
wi:AB 759.summary: Allows people who first received DACA deferred action before the bill takes effect, and hold an unexpired work permit, to receive state occupational credentials if they meet other requirements; credentials last only while the work permit is valid.

wi:AB 793.title: Relating to: creating an Office of Internal Audit attached to the Department of Employee Trust Funds. (FE)
wi:AB 793.summary: Creates an Office of Internal Audit attached to the Department of Employee Trust Funds, with an internal auditor appointed by the Employee Trust Funds Board and reporting directly to the board instead of to the department secretary.

wi:AB 85.title: Relating to: recommendation to revoke extended supervision, parole, or probation if a person is charged with a crime. (FE)
wi:AB 85.summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to recommend revoking extended supervision, parole or probation when a person on release is charged with a crime.

wi:AB 87.title: Relating to: restitution orders following a conviction for human trafficking and restoration of the right to vote to a person barred from voting as a result of a felony conviction. (FE)
wi:AB 87.summary: Requires courts to order immediate restitution in human trafficking cases, with seizure of property if unpaid, and adds payment of all fines, fees, restitution and court-ordered community service to the conditions for restoring a felony-disqualified person's voting rights.

wi:AJR 10.title: Relating to: the freedom to gather in places of worship during a state of emergency (second consideration).
wi:AJR 10.summary: Proposes amending the state constitution to bar the state or local governments from closing places of worship or forbidding gatherings in them in response to a declared emergency, including a public health emergency. Second approval would send it to voters in November 2026.

wi:AJR 102.title: Relating to: prohibiting governmental entity discrimination (second consideration).
wi:AJR 102.summary: Proposes amending the state constitution to bar governments from discriminating against or giving preferential treatment to anyone based on race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin in public employment, education, contracting and administration. Second approval would send it to voters in November 2026.

wi:AJR 133.title: Relating to: legislative suspension of rules promulgated by state agencies (first consideration).
wi:AJR 133.summary: Proposes amending the state constitution to let the legislature suspend any state agency rule indefinitely or for a set period by a joint resolution adopted by a majority of all members of each house. First consideration.

wi:SB 10.title: Relating to: access to public high schools for military recruiters.
wi:SB 10.summary: Requires school boards and charter school governing boards to give military recruiters access to common areas of high schools, during the school day and at school-sanctioned events, though not to classrooms during instruction.

wi:SB 16.title: Relating to: participation in interscholastic athletics and application of the public records and open meetings laws to interscholastic athletic associations.
wi:SB 16.summary: Bars school districts from belonging to an interscholastic athletic association unless it elects to be covered by the state's public records and open meetings laws, with exceptions for records on individual referees or students.

wi:SB 176.title: Relating to: an income and franchise tax exemption for broadband expansion grants and for federal high-cost program funding for broadband expansion. (FE)
wi:SB 176.summary: As passed by the Senate, exempts from state income and franchise taxes broadband expansion grants from state, local, tribal or federal governments and federal high-cost universal service funding for broadband, and bars claiming this and the existing exemption for the same grant.

wi:SB 276.title: Relating to: challenges to the validity of administrative rules and making an appropriation. (FE)
wi:SB 276.summary: Requires a court that declares an administrative rule invalid to award reasonable attorney fees and costs to the party that challenged the rule.

wi:SB 277.title: Relating to: the expiration of administrative rules. (FE)
wi:SB 277.summary: Makes each chapter of the state administrative code expire after seven years unless the agency readopts it, with Legislative Council staff certifying that the readoption notice meets requirements; a legislative committee sets the expiration schedule for existing chapters.

wi:SB 291.title: Relating to: making certain child care expenditures eligible for the business development tax credit. (FE)
wi:SB 291.summary: Expands the refundable business development tax credit to cover up to 15 percent of an employer's costs of providing child care for employees, including operating costs, reimbursements and child care slots, rather than only capital expenditures.

wi:SB 36.title: Relating to: an income tax exemption for cash tips paid to an employee. (FE)
wi:SB 36.summary: Creates a state income tax exemption for qualified tips for tax years 2025 to 2028, up to $25,000, phasing out above $150,000 income ($300,000 for joint filers), and counts exempt tips as income for the homestead credit.

wi:SB 389.title: Relating to: the per pupil adjustment for school district revenue limits. (FE)
wi:SB 389.summary: Eliminates the $325 per-pupil adjustment in school district revenue limits beginning with the 2027-28 school year, so no per-pupil adjustment applies from then on.

wi:SB 405.title: Relating to: a civil cause of action for a minor injured by a gender transition procedure.
wi:SB 405.summary: Lets a person injured by a gender transition procedure performed as a minor sue the provider before age 33. Defense: two years of documented perceived gender, two providers certifying it is the only treatment for any mental health concern, and consent of minor and parent.

wi:SB 417.title: Relating to: visitation of a long-term care facility resident or hospital patient during a communicable disease outbreak.
wi:SB 417.summary: Requires nursing homes, assisted living facilities and hospitals that limit visitors during a communicable disease outbreak to allow visits by clergy and an essential visitor in situations such as end of life or grief, with listed grounds for denial.

wi:SB 420.title: Relating to: prohibiting rights of nature ordinances. (FE)
wi:SB 420.summary: Bars cities, villages, towns and counties from enacting 'rights of nature' ordinances that give natural resources legal rights to exist, to be free from pollution, or to maintain a healthy ecosystem.

wi:SB 432.title: Relating to: mandatory reporting requirements and referring cases of threatened or suspected child abuse to law enforcement. (FE)
wi:SB 432.summary: Requires county child welfare departments to refer generally all reports of threatened or suspected child abuse to police, and adds child welfare department employees who work directly with children or handle cases to the list of mandatory reporters.

wi:SB 498.title: Relating to: free speech and academic freedom at University of Wisconsin System institutions and technical colleges, due process in disciplinary proceedings at University of Wisconsin System institutions and technical colleges, and causes of action against the Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin System and technical college district boards. (FE)
wi:SB 498.summary: Bars UW and technical college institutions from restricting protected speech that does not materially disrupt operations, designating free speech zones, or requiring permits for expression (except to reserve exclusive space); sets disciplinary due-process rights; allows suits against the Board of Regents or district boards.

wi:SB 532.title: Relating to: course fees at University of Wisconsin System institutions. (FE)
wi:SB 532.summary: Bars UW institutions from charging an extra fee for online-only courses unless it covers added online costs or also applies to the in-person equivalent; requires listing each course's format and bars changing it after enrollment begins.

wi:SB 533.title: Relating to: intentionally disarming a correctional officer and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 533.summary: Extends the Class H felony for disarming a peace officer to taking weapons or equipment, such as restraints, keys or radios, from correctional and juvenile correctional officers.

wi:SB 610.title: Relating to: increasing the maximum penalty for certain controlled substances offenses if the violation occurs near a homeless shelter and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 610.summary: Adds homeless shelter premises and the area within 1,000 feet of them to the places where the maximum prison term for delivering or possessing with intent to deliver certain controlled substances increases by five years.

wi:SB 652.title: Relating to: race-based higher education programs and requirements. (FE)
wi:SB 652.summary: Changes higher-education programs aimed at minority students, such as the minority teacher loan, to serve 'disadvantaged' students instead, shown through a personal narrative and net worth statement, without regard to race or sex.

wi:SB 699.title: Relating to: alternative methods of providing pupil transportation services. (FE)
wi:SB 699.summary: Raises from nine to 14 the number of passengers other than the driver that a school board or private school may carry in a non-bus vehicle, and the emergency-transport threshold from 10 or more to 15 or more passengers.

wi:SB 76.title: Relating to:  dismissing or amending certain criminal charges and deferred prosecution agreements for certain crimes.
wi:SB 76.summary: Requires a prosecutor to get court approval to dismiss or amend charges for listed crimes, including domestic abuse, auto theft, sexual assault, crimes against children and certain firearm and driving offenses, and bars deferred prosecution agreements for them.

wi:SB 782.title: Relating to: intentionally sending false text messages to 911 and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 782.summary: Makes intentionally sending a false text message to 911 an offense, with the same penalties as a false 911 call: a $100 to $600 fine or up to 90 days in jail, and a Class H felony for repeats within four years.

wi:SB 799.title: Relating to: parental access to health records of minors.
wi:SB 799.summary: As amended by the Assembly, changes parents' access to minors' health records, removing the age-14 objection exception for developmentally disabled minors, allowing access to HIV test records, and requiring online access; also requires unanimous Milwaukee council votes to modify police and fire policies.

wi:SJR 116.title: Relating to: prohibiting the governor from using the partial veto to create or increase any tax or fee (second consideration).
wi:SJR 116.summary: Proposes amending the state constitution to bar the governor from using the partial veto on an appropriation bill to create or increase any tax or fee. Second approval would send it to voters in November 2026.

wv:HB 4005.title: Skills to work
wv:HB 4005.summary: Replaces most of the state list of occupations barred for minors with federal Hazardous Occupation Order limits for ages 16 and up, limits under-16 work to federal exceptions, and changes Youth Apprenticeship student rules. Titled the Workforce Development Act of 2026.

wv:HB 4007.title: Relating to industrial access roads
wv:HB 4007.summary: Lets the Industrial Access Road Fund pay for signage and safety upgrades, sets a 90-day deadline for road-location decisions, raises per-county or municipality caps to $800,000 unmatched and $300,000 matched, and allows up to $3 million in added State Road Fund transfers.

wv:HB 4009.title: Relating to the creation of the Portable Benefit Account Act
wv:HB 4009.summary: Allows hiring parties or independent contractors to fund voluntary portable benefit accounts for health, disability, life or retirement benefits. Allows state income tax subtractions for contributions from 2026, bars counting contributions in employment-classification decisions under several state laws, and authorizes rulemaking.

wv:HB 4025.title: Exempting certain employees from the classified civil service system
wv:HB 4025.summary: Exempts new hires and promoted employees in the Departments of Health Facilities, Human Services and Health from the classified civil service system and state grievance procedures starting July 1, 2026. Secretaries may restore coverage where federal law requires; bars nepotism and favoritism in decisions.

wv:HB 4087.title: To create a West Virginia-Ireland Education Alliance.
wv:HB 4087.summary: Establishes the West Virginia-Ireland Education Alliance, adds education to the Ireland Trade Commission's membership interests, and sets up partnerships between state and Irish colleges. Grants require a four-year and a two-year state institution to collaborate.

wv:HB 4089.title: Preservation of hair during chemotherapy.  Also known as the “Jessica Huffman Bill”
wv:HB 4089.summary: Requires health insurers, including public employee and Medicaid plans, to cover scalp cooling systems that preserve hair during cancer chemotherapy. Named Jessica Huffman's Law.

wv:HB 4106.title: Allowing constitutional carry for 18- to 20-year-olds
wv:HB 4106.summary: Lets people aged 18 to 20 who are U.S. citizens or legal residents and not prohibited from possessing firearms carry a concealed deadly weapon without a license; repeals the offense of carrying without a license for those under 21.

wv:HB 4191.title: Relating to providing child care generally
wv:HB 4191.summary: Changes child care rules: pays licensed programs subsidies by monthly enrollment, ends subsidy for parents whose child averages under 8 days a month, requires electronic attendance filing, lets the Department of Human Services phase out aid gradually, and amends employer child care tax credits.

wv:HB 4196.title: To offer long-acting reversible contraception to patients receiving methadone and suboxone at the treatment facility for the methadone and suboxone
wv:HB 4196.summary: Requires medication-assisted treatment programs to offer long-acting reversible contraception to patients recovering from addiction, with non-coercive counseling and medical eligibility screening. Programs without a trained provider or equipment must refer patients elsewhere to receive it.

wv:HB 4245.title: Authorizing Certain Agencies of the Department of Revenue to Promulgate Legislative Rules
wv:HB 4245.summary: Authorizes Department of Revenue agencies to promulgate legislative rules, including rules on private clubs, residential mortgage lenders and loan originators, bank communication terminals, joint accounts, the Fintech Regulatory Sandbox Program and insurance producer fingerprinting.

wv:HB 4416.title: Classifying forestry equipment for levy purposes
wv:HB 4416.summary: Classifies forestry equipment used in harvesting, processing or transporting forest products, when owned by the producer, as Class I property for property tax and exempts sales of forestry equipment from the consumers sales and service tax.

wv:HB 4418.title: Creating “The Tax Efficiency Act of 2026”
wv:HB 4418.summary: Creates the Tax Efficiency Act of 2026, authorizing the Tax Commissioner to design and implement an electronic data processing system for filing and collecting municipal business and occupation or privilege taxes.

wv:HB 4425.title: To repeal the provision allowing for students to transfer from one school to another without losing eligibility.
wv:HB 4425.summary: Repeals §18-2-25e of the Code, the section on athletic eligibility of students who transfer from one school to another.

wv:HB 4433.title: Prohibiting Human Smuggling and Trafficking
wv:HB 4433.summary: Creates crimes of human smuggling of an adult and of a minor, raises penalties for human trafficking offenses, allows civil asset forfeiture, and makes some offenders ineligible for parole. Exempts medical, mental health and legal services provided to unlawfully present people.

wv:HB 4452.title: To remove Mortmain restrictions on religious organizations
wv:HB 4452.summary: Repeals §35-1-8 of the Code, removing restrictions on property ownership by trustees of certain religious organizations.

wv:HB 4464.title: Relating generally to Underground Facilities Damage prevention
wv:HB 4464.summary: Revises the underground utility damage prevention law, including definitions and Underground Facilities Damage Prevention Board enforcement. Lets operators and excavators agree in writing to extend the 48-hour response time after a one-call notification.

wv:HB 4575.title: Making Supplemental Appropriation to State Board of Education
wv:HB 4575.summary: Appropriates $8 million of surplus General Revenue to the State Board of Education for a Hancock County Board of Education financial stability loan, transferred to the Temporary Shortfall Supplement Fund for county boards.

wv:HB 4577.title: Relating to driver’s licenses
wv:HB 4577.summary: Directs the Division of Motor Vehicles commissioner to seek reciprocal agreements with Ireland and Japan so their lawfully present citizens may drive in West Virginia on valid home licenses. Requires insurance compliance, allows fees, and says recognition does not register holders to vote.

wv:HB 4606.title: Relating to the meaning of residence for the purpose of bail
wv:HB 4606.summary: Requires judicial officers to consider a defendant's West Virginia or U.S. residency, community ties and flight risk in misdemeanor release decisions and residency in setting bail, and bars magistrates from releasing defendants charged with listed felonies on their own recognizance.

wv:HB 4625.title: Relating to quit claim deeds
wv:HB 4625.summary: Changes real property transfer tax exemptions: removes exemptions for gifts to charitable associations and quitclaim deeds, and adds exemptions for no-consideration deeds to wholly owned LLCs, transfers between siblings, mineral deeds, and confirmatory deeds; also amends definitions.

wv:HB 4638.title: Relating to registration of voters and voluntary registration of organ donors
wv:HB 4638.summary: Adds an option on voter registration applications to register as an organ donor in a national registry. Lets the Secretary of State run or contract for a donor registry, provided the Center for Organ Recovery and Education reimburses all costs.

wv:HB 4696.title: Authorize the Department of Environmental Protection to deposit funds granted pursuant to federal programs
wv:HB 4696.summary: Lets the Department of Environmental Protection deposit federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and STREAM Act money into the Acid Mine Drainage Abatement and Treatment Fund and Reclamation and Restoration Fund, and other federal abandoned mine land money into related state funds.

wv:HB 4755.title: Adding Aggravated Vehicular Homicide to the list of qualifying offenses
wv:HB 4755.summary: Adds aggravated vehicular homicide, DUI causing serious bodily injury, third-offense DUI, and obstructing officers or emergency personnel causing death to the offenses that trigger enhanced sentences for repeat offenders.

wv:HB 4801.title: Defining Permissible expenditures for municipalities and counties
wv:HB 4801.summary: Adds demolition of unsafe and unsanitary structures, and planning for reuse or improvement of property owned by municipalities and county commissions, to the permitted uses of hotel occupancy tax revenue by counties and cities.

wv:HB 4865.title: Providing for a program allowing election official trainees to be appointed as election officials
wv:HB 4865.summary: Lets election-appointing bodies set up a program to appoint junior or senior students as election officials, with grade-average, approval and training requirements and only one participant per political party per precinct. Students serving are not counted absent from school.

wv:HB 4869.title: Establish narrow, clearly bounded guaranteed-issue rights for Medicare Supplement policies in West Virginia.
wv:HB 4869.summary: Lets Medicare supplement policyholders replace a policy of 24+ months once a year, without health underwriting, with a same-or-lesser-benefit policy from the same or an affiliated insurer; guarantees issue to people 65 or older who lose Medicaid. Requires an annual premium trend report.

wv:HB 4951.title: Requiring MDs and DOs to complete continuing education
wv:HB 4951.summary: Requires physicians renewing their medical or osteopathic licenses to complete continuing medical education in nutrition, and authorizes rulemaking.

wv:HB 4982.title: Make West Virginia Healthy Act of 2026
wv:HB 4982.summary: Re-establishes the statewide Healthy Lifestyles Program and expands the Office of Healthy Lifestyles' authority. Creates a fund and wellness programs, coordinates state agencies, requires physical fitness in schools, and requires a report; repeals the earlier Healthy Lifestyles article.

wv:HB 4983.title: Authorizing the Department of Commerce to promulgate a legislative rule relating to certification of a microgrid district or certification as a high impact data center
wv:HB 4983.summary: Authorizes Department of Commerce agencies to promulgate legislative rules as filed and modified, including rules on Tourism Development Districts and on certifying a microgrid district or high impact data center.

wv:HB 4995.title: Require the use of video cameras in certain special education classrooms
wv:HB 4995.summary: Changes rules for cameras in self-contained special education classrooms: parents get notice of camera interruptions, a judge may give them custody of recordings, administrators review recordings every 30 days instead of 90, and recordings may be used in staff discipline. Named Oscar's Law.

wv:HB 4999.title: Relating to crimes against athletic officials
wv:HB 4999.summary: Sets penalties for assault ($250 to $500 fine or up to six months in jail) and battery ($500 to $1,000 or up to a year) against athletic officials and participants. Lets schools ban convicted offenders from school sports events for a year or more.

wv:HB 5065.title: Relating to hotel occupancy tax.
wv:HB 5065.summary: Specifies information online lodging marketplaces must record when collecting hotel occupancy tax, requires geofencing or similar tools and nine-digit postal codes so tax goes to the correct city or county, and names the county or municipal official who receives it.

wv:HB 5088.title: Relating to Natural Resource Police Officer Retirement
wv:HB 5088.summary: Raises the Natural Resources Police Officer Retirement System accrued benefit from 2.5% to 2.75% of final average salary per year of service for members retiring after July 1, 2029, and provides additional funding to the system.

wv:HB 5089.title: Relating to public school acceptance of student transcripts or other credentials
wv:HB 5089.summary: Requires public schools to accept public charter school transcripts and credentials, to record class, grade and source on each student's public school transcript, and to report to the Legislative Oversight Commission on Education Accountability.

wv:HB 5110.title: Amend section providing for waiver of tuition and fees for senior citizens auditing certain college classes
wv:HB 5110.summary: Lowers the minimum age for the senior reduced-tuition program at state colleges from 65 to 60, extends it to metro-area students, and caps nonresident differential tuition in the no-credit option at 50% of the resident rate.

wv:HB 5168.title: To increase funding for EMS first responders.
wv:HB 5168.summary: Clarifies that certified microgrids and high-impact data centers must pay county fire and ambulance fees. Creates two county EMS funds and moves $12 million a year of State Lottery net profits to three EMS funds ($6 million salary fund, $3 million each new fund).

wv:HB 5212.title: Relating to financial aid for post-secondary education.
wv:HB 5212.summary: Changes higher education financial aid and workforce grant programs: lets the Learn and Earn program use block grants, and revises the medical student loan, health sciences and mental health provider loan repayment programs, including paying awards directly to loan servicers.

wv:HB 5288.title: Supplemental Appropriation to the Department of Agriculture-West Virginia Spay Neuter Assistance Fund from Special Revenue
wv:HB 5288.summary: Increases the fiscal year 2026 current expenses appropriation of the Department of Agriculture's West Virginia Spay Neuter Assistance Fund by $200,000.

wv:HB 5317.title: Supplemental Appropriation to the Department of Commerce - Division of Natural Resources from the Unappropriated Surplus Balance.
wv:HB 5317.summary: Appropriates $10 million from the General Revenue surplus balance to the Division of Natural Resources for capital outlay, repairs and equipment in fiscal year 2026.

wv:HB 5323.title: Relating to indexing of license and stamp fees
wv:HB 5323.summary: Removes the January 1, 2021 cutoff on indexing hunting and fishing license and stamp fees, so the Natural Resources director may keep proposing rule increases tied to the Consumer Price Index, rounded down to the nearest dollar.

wv:HB 5353.title: To bring virtual currency kiosks within the purview of money transmission licensure and create disclosure requirements and daily transaction limitations for new and existing customers.
wv:HB 5353.summary: Requires virtual currency kiosk operators to hold a money transmission license, with disclosures, paper receipts, a law enforcement contact, daily limits of $1,000 for new customers and $10,000 for existing ones, and refunds of fraudulent transactions in a new customer's first 10 days.

wv:HB 5354.title: Relating to authorizing legislative rules regarding higher education
wv:HB 5354.summary: Authorizes legislative rules for higher education bodies, including rules on administrative exemptions, the mental health loan program and the STAND program. Also authorizes repeal of rules on purchasing efficiencies and the Research Trust Fund program.

wv:HB 5382.title: Relating to the Neighborhood Investment Program.
wv:HB 5382.summary: Extends the Neighborhood Investment Program tax credit, ending the program on July 1, 2031, with no credit for contributions to certified projects made after that date. Taxpayers who already qualified keep their credits.

wv:HB 5437.title: Creating the Vape Safety Act
wv:HB 5437.summary: Creates the Vape Safety Act, requiring a state license ($1,200 annual fee) for vape or smoke shops. Sets applicant qualifications, requires shops to be at least 300 feet from churches, schools and daycares, regulates signs and sales, and sets criminal and administrative penalties.

wv:HB 5441.title: Reforming State Personnel System
wv:HB 5441.summary: Ends the separate personnel systems for Transportation, the State Tax Division and Social Services, terminates the State Personnel Board and moves its duties to the Division of Personnel, and exempts new and promoted Transportation employees from classified civil service from July 2026.

wv:HB 5444.title: Relating to increasing the amount of fees to be paid by parolees for supervision.
wv:HB 5444.summary: Raises the monthly fee parolees pay toward the cost of supervision, to an amount based on ability to pay and not to exceed $50 per month, and makes technical corrections.

wv:HB 5459.title: Relating to a tax on managed care organizations
wv:HB 5459.summary: Replaces the managed care organization tax's tiered per-member-month rates with a 2.5% tax on certified HMOs' gross premiums written in the state, starting July 1, 2027 and subject to federal approval. Excludes Medicare Advantage and certain public and federal employee plans.

wv:HB 5462.title: Relating to Mine Subsidence
wv:HB 5462.summary: Changes mine subsidence insurance: requires payments for a covered loss go first to property damage, gives the mine subsidence fund setoff rights, and bars lawsuits against insurers over claims reported to the Board of Risk and Insurance Management.

wv:HB 5515.title: Relating to modernizing and updating workers’ compensation statutes.
wv:HB 5515.summary: Revises workers' compensation statutes, removing obsolete provisions and repealing several sections. Ends employers' right to notice and to respond in permanent total disability requests, drops vocational standards from disability benefits, and sets the Board of Review at three to five members.

wv:HB 5528.title: Relating to protection of personal residential information of certain public officials.
wv:HB 5528.summary: Requires government agencies, on written request, to remove or redact home addresses and personal phone numbers of judicial officers, prosecutors, public defenders, law enforcement officers, elected officials, campaign treasurers and their household members from public websites and databases. Creates a civil remedy; lists permitted disclosures.

wv:HB 5582.title: Extending program for drug screening of applicants for TANF
wv:HB 5582.summary: Makes West Virginia's drug screening program for cash assistance (TANF) applicants permanent by removing its expiration date, clarifies the definition of drug test, and clarifies the timeline for reporting.

wv:HB 5612.title: Relating to property valuations of properties located on the State Capitol Complex
wv:HB 5612.summary: Requires each state agency's four-year real property inventory report to designate unused or substantially underused properties, and removes the requirement to establish market value for state-owned or leased real property.

wv:HB 5682.title: Supplemental Appropriation to expire funds to surplus balance of General Revenue
wv:HB 5682.summary: Expires $35 million from the Governor's Civil Contingent Fund to surplus General Revenue and amends the Higher Education Policy Commission's fiscal year 2026 appropriation, including $72 million of surplus funds for biomedical research expansion at Marshall, West Virginia University and the osteopathic school.

wv:HB 5685.title: Relating to authorizing bonds for improvements to the West Virginia Science and Culture Center
wv:HB 5685.summary: Authorizes bonds for improvements to the West Virginia Science and Culture Center and other history-preserving state facilities, with debt paid from State Excess Lottery Revenue. Has the Economic Development Authority issue the bonds and creates a fund.

wv:HB 5686.title: Relating to the timing of payments of annually required deposit into an eligible recipient’s Hope Scholarship account
wv:HB 5686.summary: Requires Hope Scholarship deposits for each eligible student to be made in four equal quarterly installments, due by August 15, October 15, January 15 and April 15 each year, beginning July 1, 2026.

wv:HB 5689.title: Supplemental appropriation, Department of Homeland Security
wv:HB 5689.summary: Appropriates surplus General Revenue to the Division of Corrections and Rehabilitation for fiscal year 2026: about $6.6 million for information technology services and about $5.0 million for special services.

wv:HB 5690.title: Supplemental appropriation, Adjutant General
wv:HB 5690.summary: Appropriates $4,025,000 of surplus General Revenue to the Adjutant General (State Militia) for an Armory Board transfer in fiscal year 2026.

wv:HB 5691.title: Supplemental appropriation, Department of Health
wv:HB 5691.summary: Moves $2,981,132.08 from the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Recovery Fund to surplus General Revenue and appropriates the same amount to the Department of Health's Tobacco Education Program for fiscal year 2026.

wv:HB 5692.title: Supplemental appropriation, State Road Fund
wv:HB 5692.summary: Increases the fiscal year 2026 appropriation for Other Federal Aid Programs from the State Road Fund to the Division of Highways by $100 million.

wv:HB 5694.title: Supplemental appropriation to Department of Education, fund 0313.
wv:HB 5694.summary: Amends the 2026 budget's State Department of Education appropriations, funded from the unappropriated General Revenue surplus; the amended list includes $8,000,000 for a Hancock County Board of Education financial stability loan program.

wv:SB 1060.title: Providing WV certified thoroughbred eligibility and increase restricted race caps
wv:SB 1060.summary: Changes horse racing law: sets rules and purse calculations for West Virginia-certified thoroughbreds in restricted races, changes how interstate simulcast money is distributed, raises the $1 million cap on some tracks' restricted-race funding, and changes video lottery net terminal income distribution.

wv:SB 1064.title: Redefining "long-term substitute" as it relates to public school personnel
wv:SB 1064.summary: Redefines "long-term substitute" in public school personnel law as a substitute who fills a position for more than 30 consecutive instructional days, including positions expected to exceed that length, which must be filled by someone holding the appropriate credential.

wv:SB 243.title: Establishing disaster repair and recovery effort tax credit for taxpayers subject to severance and business privilege tax in certain circumstances
wv:SB 243.summary: Creates a severance tax credit of up to $500,000 of certified repair and recovery spending per disaster, usable against up to 20% of annual severance tax liability. Requires Department of Environmental Protection certification (capped at $5 million yearly); unused credit carries forward 10 years.

wv:SB 281.title: Authorizing Department of Homeland Security to promulgate legislative rules
wv:SB 281.summary: Authorizes legislative rules for Homeland Security agencies, including law-enforcement training and certification standards, the fire code, emergency planning and community right-to-know, and three State Police rules on career progression, contracted police or security services, and member grievances.

wv:SB 374.title: Authorizing Department of Commerce to promulgate legislative rules
wv:SB 374.summary: Authorizes Department of Commerce agencies to promulgate legislative rules, including rules on tourism development districts, managed timberland certification, child labor, coal mine safety programs, and several Division of Natural Resources rules such as small arms hunting and wildlife rehabilitation.

wv:SB 4.title: Relating to crimes against public justice
wv:SB 4.summary: Makes it a misdemeanor, after a verbal warning, to approach or stay within 30 feet of a first responder on lawful duty in a way that impedes or threatens them. Penalty is a $50 to $500 fine, up to one year in jail, or both.

wv:SB 553.title: Providing for transfer of license to contractor’s qualifying immediate family member
wv:SB 553.summary: Allows a contractor license holder to transfer the license to a qualifying immediate family member, who must pass any board-required exam within one year to keep it, by amending the Contractor Licensing Act's license transfer provisions.

wv:SB 556.title: Modifying priority of insurance coverage for drivers of certain vehicles provided by entities
wv:SB 556.summary: Changes which insurance pays first for vehicles supplied by dealers, repair shops and rental or leasing companies. A driver's own coverage is primary for a permitted replacement vehicle with no separate charge; an employee's coverage is secondary when driving for work.

wv:SB 586.title: Modifying requirements for public water systems
wv:SB 586.summary: Creates two classes of backflow prevention assemblies at public water systems: low-hazard assemblies may be inspected no more often than once every three years, and high-hazard assemblies must be inspected annually.

wv:SB 59.title: Relating to voter eligibility and residency requirements
wv:SB 59.summary: Requires voters to be legal residents of the state, county or municipality where they vote. Defines residency, lists factors and rules for determining it, and sets a process for challenging a person's residency.

wv:SB 659.title: Prohibiting certain restrictions on regulation of accessory dwelling units
wv:SB 659.summary: Bars municipalities from prohibiting at least one accessory dwelling unit by right on lots with a single-family home. Limits size to the lesser of 75% of the home or 1,000 square feet, and bars extra parking or matching-design requirements, except in historic districts.

wv:SB 690.title: Creating alternative DOH procurement procedure
wv:SB 690.summary: Expands the Division of Highways' design-build program, changes its dollar limits, and authorizes Construction Manager/General Contractor contracting, capped at $200 million per project. Requires rulemaking and reports to the Legislature on alternative project delivery.

wv:SB 741.title: Expanding pilot program to implement involuntary commitment process
wv:SB 741.summary: Adds Hampshire, Morgan, Raleigh and Wood counties to the involuntary commitment pilot program already in Cabell, Berkeley and Ohio counties, in which the Supreme Court, mental health facilities, law enforcement and state agencies may participate.

wv:SB 755.title: Removing state agencies' requirement to submit annual reports for certain businesses
wv:SB 755.summary: Removes the requirement that state agencies submit annual progress reports on small, women-owned and minority-owned business procurement to the Department of Administration.

wv:SB 821.title: Supplemental appropriation to Department of Administration, fund 2367
wv:SB 821.summary: Appropriates $21 million from the Board of Risk and Insurance Management's Premium Tax Savings Fund for fiscal year 2026, to be transferred to the Public Entity Insurance Trust Fund.

wv:SB 831.title: Supplemental Appropriation to Department of Human Services, fund 8794
wv:SB 831.summary: Moves $200,000 in federal funds within the Department of Human Services' Community Mental Health Services fund for fiscal year 2026, cutting the pandemic-related item and increasing personal services and employee benefits.

wv:SB 843.title: Supplemental Appropriation to Department of Health, fund 5144
wv:SB 843.summary: Increases the fiscal year 2026 personal services and employee benefits appropriation of the Department of Health's Vital Statistics Account by $330,000.

wv:SB 878.title: Creating Office of Entrepreneurship within Office of Secretary of State
wv:SB 878.summary: Creates the Office of Entrepreneurship within the Secretary of State's office, to help businesses. Lets state agencies share information with it, requires it to answer business requests within a set time and file annual reports, and creates a dedicated fund.

wv:SB 890.title: Changing certain school calendar requirements from days or months to hours
wv:SB 890.summary: Replaces the 180-instructional-day school requirement with a 900-instructional-hour minimum, requires three Educator Focus Days for teachers to improve instruction, limits use of teacher preparation days, and lets nonpublic schools count up to 25 hours of alternative instruction on closure days. Starts July 1, 2027.

wv:SB 899.title: Permitting certain teachers to be certified to work as school principals
wv:SB 899.summary: Allows teachers with at least 15 years' experience at the elementary, middle or high school level to be certified as principals at that level after completing a year-long Department of Education program in school administration, beginning July 1, 2026.

wv:SB 913.title: Removing annual report requirement for WV Research Trust Fund
wv:SB 913.summary: Repeals the annual reporting requirement for the West Virginia Research Trust Fund by removing §18B-18A-12 from the Code.

wy:HB 1.title: General government appropriations-2.
wy:HB 1.summary: Amends the 2026-2028 budget bill to authorize the Wyoming veterans' memorial museum renovation, create a task force of legislators, state officials and a veterans' representative, and appropriate $5 million from the tourism account.

wy:HB 10.title: Sexually explicit materials in libraries-requirements.
wy:HB 10.summary: As passed by the House, bars sexually explicit materials in children's sections of public libraries and school libraries accessible to minors, requires resident challenge processes with written decisions within 60 days, and creates civil penalties and lawsuits.

wy:HB 102.title: Protecting kids from deepfakes and exploitative images.
wy:HB 102.summary: Makes it a felony to distribute nonconsensual synthetic sexual images, use AI to create child sexual images, or knowingly develop or distribute AI systems designed for such material or to promote self-harm. Says using AI is no defense to a crime; limits developer liability.

wy:HB 103.title: Wyoming First Amendment Protection Act.
wy:HB 103.summary: Creates the Wyoming First Amendment Protection Act, granting immunity from lawsuits arising from petition, speech, assembly or religious activity (with listed exceptions), requiring attorney fees for those who successfully assert it, and creating a countersuit.

wy:HB 106.title: Smokebuster module leaders.
wy:HB 106.summary: Authorizes two state forestry division positions, effective April 2026 and April 2027, and appropriates $499,709 for the forestry conservation inmate crew program.

wy:HB 111.title: State funded capital construction.
wy:HB 111.summary: Appropriates about $228 million for state capital construction projects and $233.4 million from the general fund for major maintenance at state facilities, the University of Wyoming and community colleges. Limits spending to listed projects and amends a prior penitentiary land appropriation.

wy:HB 116.title: Destruction of water is not beneficial use.
wy:HB 116.summary: As introduced, declares that splitting water molecules to produce industrial hydrogen is not a beneficial use, and bars granting water permits or changes for that purpose, except for by-product water.

wy:HB 126.title: Human heartbeat act.
wy:HB 126.summary: Bars terminating a pregnancy when a fetal heartbeat is detectable or no heartbeat check was made, except in a medical emergency; knowing violations are a felony (up to 5 years, $10,000) with license revocation. Adds backup abortion rules if a court blocks the ban.

wy:HB 127.title: Voter approval for recreation mill levy.
wy:HB 127.summary: Requires county or school district recreation levies to be approved by voters at a general election for four-year terms; existing levies expire December 31, 2028 or when a levy question goes to voters, whichever is first.

wy:HB 128.title: Enhanced oil recovery-severance tax exemption.
wy:HB 128.summary: Exempts tertiary production from projects certified between July 1, 2026 and July 1, 2031 from severance tax for five years from first production, and requires annual reports through 2036 on qualifying production.

wy:HB 141.title: Fifth Amendment Protection Act.
wy:HB 141.summary: Amends the bill barring cities, towns and counties from requiring workforce or affordable housing fees or conditions on development, to exempt any fee or condition that bears an essential nexus and proportionality to the development's impacts.

wy:HB 144.title: Fire protection districts mill levies-amendments.
wy:HB 144.summary: As introduced, raises the maximum yearly property tax levy for fire protection district operations from 3 mills to 10 mills.

wy:HB 145.title: Removing triple taxation for resident EV drivers.
wy:HB 145.summary: Sets a 3.5-cent per kilowatt-hour tax on electricity sold at DC fast charging stations, adds a $100 annual plug-in hybrid decal, and refunds that tax to registered owners up to $100 (hybrid) or $200 (all-electric) a year.

wy:HB 147.title: Property tax exemptions-effect of people's initiative.
wy:HB 147.summary: As introduced, repeals the homeowner property tax exemption if voters approve a homeowner exemption initiative; if that initiative takes effect for tax year 2027, the existing exemption does not apply that year.

wy:HB 159.title: Safeguarding personal expression at K-12 schools.
wy:HB 159.summary: As introduced, bars public schools from penalizing students for religious, political or ideological speech, covers class work, gatherings, clubs and clothing on the same terms as other speech, and lets students sue for damages (at least $5,000 if they prevail).

wy:HB 178.title: Public unions-transparency and dues withdrawal limitations.
wy:HB 178.summary: Bars state and local public employers from deducting dues, fees or contributions for labor organizations, political committees or candidates from employees' pay; violations are misdemeanors. Leaves firefighter bargaining and existing contracts unchanged. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

wy:HB 19.title: Corner crossing clarification.
wy:HB 19.summary: As passed by the House, creates an exception to criminal and game-and-fish trespass for people who walk between two adjoining public parcels they may access at the point where the corners meet, without touching or damaging adjacent private land or property.

wy:HB 23.title: Participation in school activities.
wy:HB 23.summary: Expands activities open to school-age residents not enrolled full-time in the district (and not suspended or expelled) from association-sanctioned activities to any activity the district offers, starting 2026-27.

wy:HB 25.title: Wyoming's tomorrow scholarship program amendments.
wy:HB 25.summary: Removes the continuous enrollment requirement for keeping a Wyoming's Tomorrow scholarship.

wy:HB 28.title: Sexual exploitation of children-amendments.
wy:HB 28.summary: Adds lascivious exhibition of a female person's chest or breasts to the definition of "explicit sexual conduct" in Wyoming's child sexual exploitation law.

wy:HB 3.title: Wyoming pregnancy centers-autonomy and rights.
wy:HB 3.summary: Bars state and local governments from requiring pregnancy centers to offer, refer or counsel for abortion or contraception, post related information, or hire people who do not affirm their mission, or from restricting their services for declining to. Allows lawsuits for relief.

wy:HB 35.title: Firefighters-paid leave and hazard pay.
wy:HB 35.summary: Requires hazard pay and eligibility for paid time off for state forestry division wildland firefighters and correctional crew supervisors, based on federal firefighter standards the office monitors but need not follow, and appropriates $422,500 for hazard pay.

wy:HB 36.title: Forestry division wildland fire modules.
wy:HB 36.summary: As passed by the House, authorizes 24 forestry division positions and appropriates $5.14 million for two state wildland fire suppression modules, specialized teams for wildfire suppression and fuel reduction.

wy:HB 45.title: Long-term homeowner tax exemption-revisions.
wy:HB 45.summary: Revises the long-term homeowner property tax exemption for owners 65+ with 25 years of Wyoming property tax: sets a March 1 claim deadline, allows later-year reconfirmation by contacting the assessor, limits the 50% exemption to the first $3 million of value, and repeals the sunset.

wy:HB 52.title: Elections-hand counting for recounts.
wy:HB 52.summary: Requires hand-count recounts of federal, statewide and legislative races decided by under 2% in a county (under 1% statewide), lets candidates choose hand or machine recounts, requires county hand-count audits after the 2026 elections, and moves the August primary two weeks earlier.

wy:HB 56.title: Carbon capture mandate-repeal.
wy:HB 56.summary: Repeals the low-carbon energy standard requirements for electric utilities, except for projects and rate cases where the commission already approved carbon capture use or study; requires commission rulemaking.

wy:HB 69.title: Department of health-land transfers.
wy:HB 69.summary: Directs the Department of Health to convey a 28.94-acre State Training School parcel in Fremont County to the Department of Transportation at no charge, and authorizes sale of a 90.87-acre parcel restricted to residential housing. Transportation reports to an interim committee.

wy:HB 70.title: Wyoming GRANITE Act.
wy:HB 70.summary: As introduced, creates a state cause of action against foreign states and international organizations over foreign censorship laws that violate speech rights, and bars Wyoming from recognizing or cooperating with certain foreign judgments.

wy:HB 75.title: Virtual currency kiosks.
wy:HB 75.summary: Requires virtual currency kiosk operators to hold a money transmitter license or financial institution charter; knowing violations are a felony punishable by at least three years in prison, a fine of at least $10,000, or both; the banking commissioner writes rules.

wy:HB 76.title: Exception for annexation with landowner objections-repeal.
wy:HB 76.summary: As introduced, repeals the provision barring landowners from objecting to an annexation when part of the area borders the city or town, for annexation proceedings begun on or after July 1, 2026.

wy:HB 78.title: Forest health grant program.
wy:HB 78.summary: Creates a forest health grant program run by the state forester, giving nonprofits and governments grants covering up to 75% (50% on federal land) of eligible forest health project costs. Appropriates $3.5 million; requires attorney general approval of grants and annual reports.

wy:HB 84.title: Falsifying election documents.
wy:HB 84.summary: As introduced, adds submitting a false post-election ballot audit to the secretary of state to the acts that count as falsifying election documents.

wy:HB 85.title: Post-election audit procedures.
wy:HB 85.summary: As passed by the House, requires county clerks to take minutes of the post-election ballot audit, notify party chairs and independent candidates of its time and place, and have at least two electors from different parties observe.

wy:HB 96.title: Carrying of concealed weapons-age requirement.
wy:HB 96.summary: Lowers the minimum age to receive a Wyoming concealed carry permit from 21 to 18.

wy:HB 98.title: Prohibit Red Flag Gun Seizure Act-penalty amendments.
wy:HB 98.summary: Makes knowingly violating the Prohibit Red Flag Gun Seizure Act a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in jail, a fine of up to $2,000, or both.

wy:SF 101.title: Second amendment protection act amendments-3.
wy:SF 101.summary: Amends the Second Amendment Protection Act, which bars state and local use of personnel or funds to enforce certain federal firearms laws against law-abiding citizens, to add damages, a $50,000 per-violation civil penalty against violating agencies, and a lawsuit right for interested parties.

wy:SF 102.title: Wyoming energy transmission study.
wy:SF 102.summary: Requires the Wyoming energy authority to complete a two-phase transmission study covering low, moderate and high load growth scenarios and utility participation in regional markets, reporting by November 2027 and September 2028.

wy:SF 104.title: Higher education-research funding.
wy:SF 104.summary: Appropriates $50 million to a new University of Wyoming faculty research account, spent on research projects with one-to-one nonstate matching funds, plus $1.2 million for graduate student research stipends of up to $1,500 per month.

wy:SF 106.title: Welfare Fraud Prevention Act Amendments.
wy:SF 106.summary: Sets welfare eligibility rules: limits SNAP certification periods to six months or less, bars Medicaid self-attestation of eligibility factors, caps Medicaid retroactive coverage at two months, requires citizenship verification, refers unlawfully present people to law enforcement, and has Medicaid hospitals collect patients' citizenship status.

wy:SF 107.title: Motor vehicle registration and plate issuance system.
wy:SF 107.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to run a statewide electronic vehicle registration and license plate issuance system by July 1, 2028, which county treasurers must use, as part of replacing the revenue information system.

wy:SF 109.title: Cowboy state agricultural trust fund.
wy:SF 109.summary: Creates a Cowboy State Agricultural Trust Fund with a $10 million transfer from the general fund, using earnings for matched grants to agricultural projects, overseen by a new committee. Grants over $200,000 need legislative authorization.

wy:SF 110.title: Residential property tax revisions.
wy:SF 110.summary: Sets taxable value at 8.3% of fair market value for owner-occupied primary residences and 9.5% for other residential property, assesses zero school mills on primary residences on a March 1 claim, and repeals the long-term homeowner exemption. Appropriates $500,000; first applies to tax year 2028.

wy:SF 111.title: Select committee on gaming.
wy:SF 111.summary: As amended, creates a six-member legislative select committee on gaming, appointed after each general election, to study gaming law and regulation, meet with local governments, review gaming taxes and compliance, and recommend legislation.

wy:SF 112.title: Elimination of license plate replacement cycle.
wy:SF 112.summary: As introduced, ends the eight-year license plate reissue cycle, requiring replacement of plates only when unreadable, with a fee for the two replacement plates.

wy:SF 113.title: 2026 election hand count comparison.
wy:SF 113.summary: Requires each county clerk to hand count ballots from about 5% of election-day ballots after the 2026 primary and general elections. Audits one federal race, one statewide race and each legislative race, compares results to machine counts, and reports discrepancies to the secretary of state.

wy:SF 117.title: Zoning protest petition-amendments.
wy:SF 117.summary: Changes the city and town zoning protest rule: a protest needs more than one owner holding 33% (was 20%) of the area or 33% of adjacent owners within 300 feet (was 140); overriding it takes a two-thirds vote, not three-fourths.

wy:SF 119.title: Strategic investments and projects account-repeal-2.
wy:SF 119.summary: Repeals the strategic investments and projects account, moving its funds to the general fund, and from fiscal year 2027 appropriates to the public school foundation program account 45 percent of the amount creditable to the legislative stabilization reserve account.

wy:SF 123.title: Wyoming energy dominance fund.
wy:SF 123.summary: Creates the Wyoming energy dominance fund, run by the Wyoming energy authority and financed by up to $105 million of FY2027 severance tax revenue, for matching grants and loans to coal, gas, oil, uranium and other energy projects, but not wind or solar.

wy:SF 124.title: Economic development-rodeo museum.
wy:SF 124.summary: Appropriates $15 million from the tourism reserve and projects account to the office of tourism to contract with a rodeo and cowboy museum and hall of fame project, with a dollar-for-dollar nonstate match. Requires repayment if the project is not completed by June 30, 2030.

wy:SF 125.title: Wyoming business council-amendments.
wy:SF 125.summary: As introduced, starting April 15, 2027, bars the Wyoming business council from accepting, processing or approving new grant, loan, bond or other funding applications, and requires reports on its outstanding obligations, loans, bonds, property and funds.

wy:SF 126.title: Wyoming-Ireland Trade Commission.
wy:SF 126.summary: As introduced, creates a nine-member Wyoming-Ireland trade commission of legislators and appointees to promote trade, investment, and business and academic exchanges between Wyoming and Ireland, reporting yearly to the governor and legislative leaders.

wy:SF 14.title: Literacy position for K-3 reading program.
wy:SF 14.summary: Appropriates $240,000 for July 2026 to June 2028 to fund one full-time Department of Education position assisting school districts with the required reading assessment and intervention program and language and literacy programs.

wy:SF 16.title: Subleasing of state lands-exemptions.
wy:SF 16.summary: Requires state grazing lessees who graze livestock they do not own to give notice within 30 days and pay a monthly per-head fee, defines "excess rental" for the half payable to the state on subleases, and exempts leases with at least 80% common ownership.

wy:SF 17.title: Good neighbor authority-amendments.
wy:SF 17.summary: Removes the cap of four full-time and six at-will good neighbor authority forestry positions, lets them be paid from any funds in the good neighbor revolving account (not just federal funds), and lets the state forester accept gifts and grants into it.

wy:SF 20.title: Data privacy-government entities.
wy:SF 20.summary: Bars state and local government entities (not courts or law enforcement) from buying, selling or transferring personal data without written consent, with exceptions, and requires them to adopt policies on collecting, securing and using personal data.

wy:SF 21.title: Wyoming stable token-amendments.
wy:SF 21.summary: Changes the stable token program: lowers to 100% (from 102%) the trust level above which earnings go to the administration account, creates a 2% liquidity account, allows gifts to its accounts, adds investments meeting a federal money-market rule, and allows agreements with other states.

wy:SF 22.title: Unincorporated nonprofit associations-amendments.
wy:SF 22.summary: Updates the laws on decentralized unincorporated nonprofit associations, including automatic conversion to a Wyoming unincorporated nonprofit association when membership falls below 100, and requires assets on winding up to be distributed as federal law requires.

wy:SF 23.title: Outpatient examination and commitment length.
wy:SF 23.summary: As amended in committee, adds advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants to the professionals who may examine a proposed patient in involuntary hospitalization proceedings.

wy:SF 24.title: Lottery tickets-acceptance of debit card payments.
wy:SF 24.summary: Allows the Wyoming lottery to accept debit card payments for ticket purchases, while payment by check, credit card or charge card remains prohibited.

wy:SF 25.title: Landowner license limits in limited quota hunt areas.
wy:SF 25.summary: Lets the game and fish commission cap landowner hunting licenses in limited quota hunt areas, but bars issuing zero landowner licenses in those areas when eligible landowners apply.

wy:SF 26.title: Game and fish property tax exemption-amendments.
wy:SF 26.summary: Exempts most real property owned by the game and fish commission from property tax, while keeping a special tax on land used for wildlife management or employee housing.

wy:SF 28.title: Elections-voting machine and voting system tests.
wy:SF 28.summary: Requires county clerks to test every voting machine individually, lets members of the public attend machine tests, removes the presumption that a certified machine is properly prepared, and allows court challenges for five days (previously two) after sealing.

wy:SF 34.title: Roadside safety-amendments.
wy:SF 34.summary: As introduced, requires drivers to yield to roadside service and tire repair vehicles using warning lights, lets them display flashing red and blue lights at emergency scenes or while performing roadside services, and exempts them from siren requirements.

wy:SF 35.title: School district-cell phone and smart watch policies.
wy:SF 35.summary: Requires each school district board to adopt, by July 1, 2026, a policy on student possession and use of cell phones and smart devices in schools and send it to the state superintendent.

wy:SF 36.title: Hathaway lump sum merit scholarship.
wy:SF 36.summary: As introduced, sets each Hathaway scholarship (except need-based) as a fixed total amount ($3,360 to $13,440 by type) drawn down by semester, repeals the per-semester award schedules, and caps combined aid at tuition and mandatory fees instead of cost of attendance.

wy:SF 37.title: K-12 school facilities maintenance and appropriations.
wy:SF 37.summary: As introduced, raises the cap on education space counted in school maintenance and building repair funding from 115% to 135% of standard space (135% now applies only to 2025-26), and appropriates $31.9 million for major and $11.8 million for routine maintenance.

wy:SF 39.title: Long-term homeowner tax exemption-amendments.
wy:SF 39.summary: Repeals the sunset of the long-term homeowner property tax exemption, moves the claim deadline to March 1, lets claimants reconfirm by contacting the assessor in later years, and limits the 50% exemption to the first $3 million of fair market value.

wy:SF 4.title: Medicaid rate increase-EMS services.
wy:SF 4.summary: Sets Medicaid reimbursement for ground ambulance emergency medical services at 100 percent of the Medicare rate from July 2026 through June 2028, requires enhanced rural fee schedules, and requires a cost report by October 31, 2027.

wy:SF 43.title: Conservation district supervisor contracting.
wy:SF 43.summary: As introduced, repeals the requirement that conservation district supervisors have funds immediately available to cover a contract's full amount before entering the contract.

wy:SF 45.title: Local approval for simulcasting.
wy:SF 45.summary: Requires simulcasting permits, including historic horse racing terminals, to be approved by the city, town or county where located, in addition to the racing commission, and allows conditions, revocation of approval and appeals.

wy:SF 5.title: Hospital bankruptcy proceedings.
wy:SF 5.summary: Allows county memorial hospitals and hospital districts to file for Chapter 9 federal bankruptcy, with county commissioner approval for memorial hospitals.

wy:SF 50.title: State engineer-surface and ground water study.
wy:SF 50.summary: Requires the state engineer, subject to funding, to study groundwater at least every 10 years in counties with control areas where corrective controls were ordered, and appropriates $500,000 for an initial study due by June 30, 2030.

wy:SF 52.title: 2026 large project funding.
wy:SF 52.summary: Approves 2026 large wildlife and natural resource projects, including fish passage, fish screen and cheatgrass control projects, and authorizes distributions for them from the wildlife and natural resource trust income account.

wy:SF 53.title: Keeping amateurism in high school athletics.
wy:SF 53.summary: Requires students representing Wyoming high schools in sanctioned activities to be amateurs; accepting money for competing, prizes above association-approved limits, name, image or likeness compensation, or a professional contract forfeits amateur status, with listed exceptions.

wy:SF 54.title: State banks and SPDI conversions.
wy:SF 54.summary: Lets the state banking commissioner, with board approval, convert a special purpose depository institution into a state bank, and a state bank into a special purpose depository institution. Sets application and shareholder-approval requirements and requires rulemaking.

wy:SF 55.title: Special purpose depository institution-amendments.
wy:SF 55.summary: Changes rules for special purpose depository institutions: extends the deadline to open for business from six months to one year, allows chancery court appeals, creates a resolution fund account financed by part of supervisory fees, and repeals the contingency account requirement.

wy:SF 56.title: Kratom product regulation.
wy:SF 56.summary: Amends the kratom bill to replace its regulatory framework with a ban on dispensing, making or selling kratom or tianeptine products not FDA-approved, with a penalty up to $750, seizure and forfeiture, and $650,000 for state testing equipment and its maintenance.

wy:SF 58.title: Wyoming Indian Child Welfare Act sunset repeal.
wy:SF 58.summary: Repeals the sunset date of the Wyoming Indian Child Welfare Act (W.S. 14-6-715(b)), so the state law continues in effect past its scheduled end. Takes effect July 1, 2026.

wy:SF 59.title: K-12 language and literacy program.
wy:SF 59.summary: Creates a K-12 language and literacy program requiring screening, assessments and diagnostics, professional development, parent notice, and individual reading plans for students with reading difficulties, and lets the state superintendent create a literacy division.

wy:SF 6.title: Eligibility for Medicaid-criteria.
wy:SF 6.summary: Codifies current Medicaid eligibility criteria in state law from July 2027: U.S. citizenship or lawful presence, Wyoming residency, and at least one listed category such as disability, SSI, hospice or an authorized waiver; expanding eligibility beyond January 2026 levels needs legislative authorization.

wy:SF 61.title: Motor vehicle sales to family members-not taxable.
wy:SF 61.summary: Exempts motor vehicle purchases from, or transfers to, immediate family members (parent, child, spouse, sibling, step-relatives, grandparent, grandchild) from sales and use tax, if the seller or donor already paid tax on the vehicle.

wy:SF 67.title: Wyoming state guard-amendments.
wy:SF 67.summary: Lets the governor organize and maintain the Wyoming state guard at any time, without requiring that the national guard first be called into federal service, removes the U.S. defense secretary's role, and appropriates $25,000.

wy:SF 68.title: Water districts-funds for maintenance projects.
wy:SF 68.summary: Lets irrigation, watershed improvement and water conservancy districts set aside part of annual funding for major maintenance projects and invest those accounts, and lets water conservancy districts levy up to one additional mill for major maintenance.

wy:SF 69.title: Waste and storm water infrastructure study.
wy:SF 69.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to study public waste water and storm water infrastructure statewide, with local governments supplying data, makes the data publicly available, and appropriates $8 million.

wy:SF 7.title: Theft amendments.
wy:SF 7.summary: Raises the maximum penalty for theft of property under $1,000 from six months and $750 to one year and $1,500, and makes a third or subsequent theft offense, rather than a fifth, a felony punishable by up to 10 years.

wy:SF 71.title: Wyoming department of homeland security.
wy:SF 71.summary: Turns the Office of Homeland Security into a Wyoming Department of Homeland Security on July 1, 2026, moving its property and duties, with a director appointed by the governor.

wy:SF 72.title: Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact.
wy:SF 72.summary: As introduced, joins Wyoming to the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, which creates a licensure pathway letting teachers licensed in one member state teach in other member states, including relocating military spouses.

wy:SF 8.title: Absconding for criminal purposes-criminal offense.
wy:SF 8.summary: Creates the crime of absconding for criminal purposes: traveling between counties or out of state to evade police, commit another offense, or hide proceeds, punished like the most serious underlying crime.

wy:SF 81.title: K-12 public school finance-2.
wy:SF 81.summary: Implements the 2025 cost of education study as modified by the legislature, changing the education resource block grant model for K-12 funding. Also changes cash-reserve rules, limits some funds to instructional spending, creates a postsecondary enrollment grant program, and appropriates $275 million.

wy:SF 87.title: Felony interference with a police officer-amendments.
wy:SF 87.summary: Expands the felony of interfering with a peace officer (up to 10 years) to cover a person who causes bodily injury to an officer while violating the interference law, in addition to intentional or attempted injury.

wy:SF 88.title: Sex offenders-residence near child care facilities.
wy:SF 88.summary: Bars registered adult sex offenders from living within 1,000 feet of a child care facility, unless their residence was established before July 1, 2026 or before the facility. Requires the state registry division to check offenders' addresses against the limit.

wy:SF 9.title: Fentanyl to minors-enhanced penalty.
wy:SF 9.summary: Makes it a felony for a person 18 or older to distribute fentanyl to someone under 18, punishable by a fine, up to twice the prison term otherwise allowed for that drug offense, or both.

wy:SF 90.title: School facilities-use fees.
wy:SF 90.summary: Limits fees school districts charge youth clubs and activities not sponsored by the district to the district's actual added personnel, equipment, utility and supply costs, with an itemized statement on request; districts may charge nothing.

wy:SF 95.title: Driver's and motor vehicle services-third party providers.
wy:SF 95.summary: Allows the Department of Transportation to contract with third-party providers to administer driver's license tests and motor vehicle services, and to set up a partner program; requires rules on qualifications, training, background checks, bonding and fees.

wy:SF 96.title: Tobacco sales and taxation.
wy:SF 96.summary: As introduced, states that wholesalers may not sell nicotine products to anyone under 21, caps the cigar tax at 30 cents per cigar, taxes remote sales of cigars and pipe tobacco at 20% of wholesale price, and licenses remote sellers.

wy:SF 99.title: Prescriptive easements for electricity delivery.
wy:SF 99.summary: Grants electric utilities a nonexclusive easement, up to 30 feet from the line, over land crossed by distribution lines visibly installed by January 1, 2006, in continuous use and without a written easement. Lets utilities rebuild, maintain and trim hazardous vegetation.

wy:SJ 5.title: Convention of states.
wy:SJ 5.summary: As introduced, asks Congress to call a convention of the states limited to proposing amendments that impose federal fiscal restraints, limit federal power and jurisdiction, and set term limits for federal officials and members of Congress.

wy:SJ 6.title: Shared parenting day.
wy:SJ 6.summary: Designates April 26 of each year as shared parenting day in Wyoming.

wy:SJ 9.title: Keeping public lands protected and decisions local.
wy:SJ 9.summary: Asks Congress to recognize Wyoming's access to public lands under multiple-use management. Opposes broad or indiscriminate sale of public lands, demands that federal agencies respect county land-use plans, supports locally backed land exchanges and disposals, and supports funding for agency land review.
